### Same-session follow-up: located the exact consumer mechanism and its one known producer, both by pure source reading (no rebuild)

With the crash's `mb=0x80111270 pri=1 dir=0` constants in hand, searched
the recompiled guest C (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/
funcs_1.c`) for the address `0x80111270` and its containing function.
Found it directly — no decomp asm needed after all; N64Recomp already
translated this guest code to (ugly but fully readable) C, and s92's
"no C source available" conclusion only applied to the *hand-decomp*
tree, not the *recompiled* one, which covers 100% of the ROM.

**`piDmaWorker`** (guest `0x80005570`, symbol_files-confirmed, "cartridge
PI DMA worker; ring at 0x801112B0 (256×20B)") is a persistent
consumer-loop thread. Each iteration: reads a producer counter at
`0x801126B4`, a consumer counter at `0x801126B0`; while they differ,
computes `ring_slot = 0x801112B0 + (consumer_idx % 256) * 20`, and if
the byte at `ring_slot+0x10` is 0 (a "DMA request" tag, vs. non-zero
for some other message-type path at `L_80005660`), calls
`osPiStartDma_recomp` with **literal constants `mb=0x80111270`
(a different, hardcoded 32-bit constant — the PI manager's own
persistent completion-notify queue, distinct from the ring), `pri=1`,
`dir=0`**, and `devAddr = ring_slot+0x4`, `dramAddr = ring_slot+0x8`,
`size = ring_slot+0x0` (stack args). **This is an exact, unconditional
match to all four `do_rom_read` crash log lines' `mb`/`pri`/`dir`** —
proof (not inference) that every occurrence of this crash is this
exact consumer loop, reading a corrupted `devAddr` straight out of
`ring_slot+0x4` in RDRAM.

**`submitDmaRequestBatch`** (guest `0x8000569C`, writes the same
20-byte slot layout from a caller-supplied array of 12-byte `{size,
romAddr, dramAddr}` entries, same ring-index arithmetic mirrored on a
producer counter at the same `0x801126B4`) is the only function in the
entire recompiled codebase that references the ring base literal
(`grep -rl "0X12B0\b"` and `grep -rl "0X26B4"` across all 45
`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c` each return exactly `funcs_1.c` and nothing
else). Its **only static call site** is inside **`mainBootstrapWorker`**
(guest `0x80000C68`, immediately after `osStopThread` +
`loadDebugAssets` — genuinely one-time boot code, not a per-frame or
per-level worker), with a single request (`count=1`) whose `size`
(`0xCE00`), `romAddr` (`0xB0101000`), and `dramAddr` (`0x80100400`) are
**all fixed immediate constants** baked into the instruction stream —
not data-driven, not dependent on any register input. **This does not
match the crash's target (`dram=0x80195190`, `size=0x600`)** — the one
known producer cannot be the source of the corrupted request.

This is a genuine open puzzle, not yet resolved: the ring's only known
write path fires exactly once, at boot, with sane fixed values, yet
the crash (which is unambiguously this same ring/worker, by the
literal-constant match above) fires much later (hold+13s into a driven
session) with a different, corrupted target. Two live explanations,
not yet distinguished:
1. There is a second producer this static search missed — an indirect
   call to `submitDmaRequestBatch` via a function pointer/`jalr`
   (invisible to a literal-`jal`-address grep), or a duplicate
   inlined ring-write using a cached pointer instead of re-deriving
   the `0x12B0`/`0x26B4` literals each time.
2. The ring truly is written once, and something unrelated writes
   stray garbage into the `ring_slot+0x4` (devAddr) field of RDRAM
   between the boot-time write and whatever much-later read/rewrite
   the consumer sees — i.e. the "shared corruption race" from s85 is
   real but its landing zone is now precisely known (a fixed 20-byte
   window inside `0x801112B0..0x801126B0`), which is a much smaller,
   more instrumentable target than "somewhere in an OSThread context."

Not instrumented or soaked this session (source-reading only, no
rebuild) — the next concrete, cheap, discriminating step is in
CURRENT-TRUTH next-steps item 1.

## Session 94 (2026-07-27) — landed NEXT.md's DMA-ring producer/consumer instrument; one soak discriminates cleanly: the producer fires 10x, not once, refuting the s93 "one static call, boot-only" premise, and pins the corruption to the moment of the write, not a later stomp

Executed the exact work unit s93's NEXT.md specified: two new log points
gated on `ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_RING=1`, added via
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` (not `lib/` — recompiled guest code).
Producer side logs right after the `L_80005768` label inside
`submitDmaRequestBatch`'s write loop (both branches of the `bgez` at
`0x8000575C` converge there; `ctx->r3` still holds the just-written
ring-slot pointer, unclobbered, so the log re-reads the slot's three
fields straight back out of memory instead of tracking registers).
Consumer side logs every iteration of `piDmaWorker`'s poll loop right
after the tag-byte read at `0x80005608`, before the `if (tag != 0)`
skip branch, so idle polls log too. Full regen pipeline ran clean
(`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`,
exit 0, only pre-existing-class warnings); `fixup_game_funcs.py`
confirmed both patches applied exactly once (`funcs_1.c: DMA ring
producer diagnostic patched x1` / `... consumer ... x1`).

One soak (`s94_dmaring1`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME=0` to avoid s93's
confound, all other diagnostic flags armed per NEXT.md's prescribed
command) reproduced `do_rom_read` again — **5th occurrence**, still
byte-identical to s85/s91×2/s93 (`phys=0x1C676672 dram=0x80195190
bytes=0x600`, `mb=0x80111270 pri=1 dir=0`), dying at the same
`piDmaWorker` → `osPiStartDma_recomp` → `do_dma` → `do_rom_read` SIGSEGV
backtrace as every prior hit. This alone is now a 5-for-5 deterministic
reproduction, not a coincidence.

**The new data: the producer log fired 10 times this run, not 1.**
`n=0` is the known boot-time call (`mainBootstrapWorker`, fixed
constants `size=0xCE00 devAddr=0xB0101000 dramAddr=0x80100400`,
consumed correctly by the matching `n=0` consumer log, then one idle
poll `n=1 tag=1`) — this part matches every prior session exactly and
is the positive control that the instrument works. Then, ~140s later
in the same run (line 36802 of `run.log`, immediately preceding the
crash), the producer log fires **9 more times back-to-back** (`n=1`
through `n=9`), each with a **different** `devAddr`/`dramAddr` pair:

    n=1 size=0x600 devAddr=0x6C676672 dramAddr=0x80195190   <- this exact entry is what crashes
    n=2 size=0x600 devAddr=0x77696E67 dramAddr=0x80195790
    n=3 size=0x300 devAddr=0x6C637265 dramAddr=0x80195D90
    n=4 size=0x500 devAddr=0x6C676C72 dramAddr=0x80196390
    n=5 size=0x500 devAddr=0x77697467 dramAddr=0x80196990
    n=6 size=0x100 devAddr=0x6C677172 dramAddr=0x80196890
    n=7 size=0x400 devAddr=0x6C677272 dramAddr=0x80196F90
    n=8 size=0x100 devAddr=0x77697967 dramAddr=0x80196E90
    n=9 size=0x400 devAddr=0x77697A67 dramAddr=0x80197590

`dramAddr` climbs in plausible, roughly-sequential ~0x600–0x780
steps (`0x80195190` → `0x80197590`) — this looks like a genuine
real-subsystem batch (e.g. a streaming/load request for several
buffers), not noise. But every `devAddr` in the batch decodes as
readable ASCII when split into big-endian bytes: `0x6C676672`="lgfr",
`0x77696E67`="wing", `0x6C637265`="lcre", `0x6C676C72`="lglr",
`0x77697467`="witg", `0x6C677172`="lgqr", `0x6C677272`="lgrr",
`0x77697967`="wiyg", `0x77697A67`="wizg" — never a plausible ROM
address (no `0xB0xxxxxx`/kseg1 shape). The very next consumer log
(`n=2`) reads back exactly the `n=1` entry's fields verbatim
(`devAddr=0x6C676672 dramAddr=0x80195190`) and forwards it to
`osPiStartDma_recomp`, which is the crash. The consumer never gets to
`n=2..9` — the process dies on the first corrupted entry of the batch.

**This directly answers NEXT.md's discriminating question and lands on
its first branch: "producer fires >1 time: a second producer exists."**
Re-checked immediately (in case the loop inside `submitDmaRequestBatch`
itself just iterates `count>1` in its one known call): grepped fresh
for `submitDmaRequestBatch(rdram` (the direct-call idiom the
recompiler emits) across all 45 `funcs_*.c` — **still exactly 1 hit**
(`funcs_0.c`, the boot call). Combined with the 140-second gap between
`n=0` and `n=1` (a single straight-line loop with no yield points
inside it, confirmed by re-reading the loop body, cannot pause
mid-execution for two minutes), this rules out "the boot call's own
loop has more than one iteration" — the 9 extra firings must come
through a call this literal-name grep cannot see: an **indirect call**
(`LOOKUP_FUNC(...)` / `jalr` through a function pointer) to
`submitDmaRequestBatch`'s address (`0x8000569C`) from somewhere else
in the game, not yet located.

**Reframing of the root-cause hypothesis (supersedes s85's "shared
corruption race" as the leading explanation, though it doesn't fully
retire it — see below):** the corrupted value is present at the
moment the producer *writes* it, not stomped afterward by an unrelated
race. Whatever this second, indirect caller is, it is populating the
request struct's `devAddr` field with bytes that look like they came
from a name/string table (short lowercase-letter runs, all in the
`0x60`-`0x7A` ASCII range) rather than a real physical address — most
consistent with an **off-by-a-field / wrong-offset read** in that
caller (reading a name or label field where a ROM address field
belongs), not a cross-thread memory stomp. This is now a narrower,
more source-findable bug class than "something elsewhere in RDRAM
stomps this 20-byte window." The s85 shared-race framing is not fully
dead — it's still possible the *indirect caller itself* is reading
from a corrupted/reused struct — but the immediate next step is to
identify that caller, not to instrument a wider memory-stomp watch.

Controls/other instruments this run: `thr-resume bad_total=0` (with
`ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME=0` so the gate itself has no log, consistent
with s93's confound finding, not a regression); `anim-recurse`,
`anim-tex-stream`, `hangar-entry`, TMEM-zero all present in the binary
but did not need to be read for this soak's discriminating result (the
crash pattern is identical to prior sessions, `do_rom_read` wins the
race as expected with the confound off).

## Session 95 (2026-07-27) — landed a global `get_function` chokepoint instrument (`ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_CALLER=1`) to find `submitDmaRequestBatch`'s indirect caller; one soak ran, but a pre-existing uncatalogued crash (`composeNpcOrientationMatrix`, first seen once at s74) killed the process before the ~140s mark where the target phenomenon occurs — 0/0, inconclusive, not refuted

### Work unit

NEXT.md's step 2 (the concrete-instrument option): find what calls
`submitDmaRequestBatch` (`0x8000569C`) indirectly. Before writing any
code, read `recomp.h`'s `LOOKUP_FUNC` macro and its implementation:

```c
#define LOOKUP_FUNC(val) \
    get_function((int32_t)(val))
```

`get_function` (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/overlays.cpp:397`)
is the resolver every `LOOKUP_FUNC(...)` call site invokes just before
calling the result. Checked whether it would be safe to widen
`get_function`'s signature to also take `ctx` (so the instrument could
read `ctx->r31`, the return address) — **rejected**: `get_function`'s
1-arg signature (`recomp_func_t*(*)(int32_t)`) is a shared ABI used by
the mods system (`mods.hpp:534,568`, `mods.cpp:416` DLL symbol lookup)
and the live-recompiler JIT (`live_generator.cpp` emits a call with a
hardcoded single-argument calling convention, `SLJIT_ARGS1(P, 32)`).
Changing it would mean updating several unrelated subsystems just to
add one instrument — too invasive for what's needed.

Confirmed the call-site pattern is completely uniform first, so the
chokepoint approach is sound: grepped the codegen template itself
(`N64Recomp/src/cgenerator.cpp:410,414`, the sibling tool checkout, not
the generated output) — it always emits either
`LOOKUP_FUNC(0x{addr})(rdram, ctx);` or `LOOKUP_FUNC({reg})(rdram,
ctx);`, i.e. `ctx` is *always* the very next expression evaluated after
`get_function` returns. Cross-checked against the actual generated
output: **28388/28389** `LOOKUP_FUNC(` occurrences across all 45
`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c` are immediately followed by
`(rdram, ctx);` on the same line (the one non-match is a comment, not
code). This also reconfirms s93/s94's finding from a different angle:
the known boot-time call to `submitDmaRequestBatch` is compiled as a
**direct** call (`submitDmaRequestBatch_...(rdram, ctx)` by literal
name, not through `LOOKUP_FUNC`), so it will **never** trigger this
instrument — only a genuine indirect (`jalr`) caller can, cleanly
separating the two without needing extra filtering logic.

Landed the instrument without touching `get_function`'s signature:
since `get_function` is called and returns *before* its result is
invoked, a native stack backtrace taken from inside `get_function`
itself has the actual calling generated function as the very next
frame up — no need for `ctx` at all. Added (in
`lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/overlays.cpp`, gated
`ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_CALLER=1`):

```c
static void rs64_log_dma_ring_caller(int32_t addr) {
    constexpr int32_t k_submit_dma_request_batch = 0x8000569C;
    if (addr != k_submit_dma_request_batch) return;
    // ...env-var gate...
    void* frames[8];
    int n = backtrace(frames, 8);
    fprintf(stderr, "[dma-ring-caller] resolved 0x%08X, native backtrace (%d frames):\n", addr, n);
    backtrace_symbols_fd(frames, n, fileno(stderr));
}
```

called from the top of `get_function`. Rebuilt clean (`cmake --build`,
exit 0, no new warnings), ran `submodule-patches/export.sh` (this is a
`lib/` edit), committed the refreshed patch before running anything.

### Result

Timeline (from the script's own stdout, not `run.log` — the script's
`print` calls go to the wrapper's stdout, only the game binary's output
is redirected into `run.log`; conflating the two wastes a grep, note
for future sessions): phase width=1024 (title) at 44.8s, scripted
`start/start/start/a` at 3/25/40/60s from-phase (AVAILABLE CRAFT),
12s stable wait, single `start` leave probe, then the 30s hold window.
**Process died at hold-iter 3** (~3s post-leave) — even earlier than
s95's ~5s.

reinterpretTileRecord, file rt64_framebuffer_manager.cpp, line 480`.

`RT64::FramebufferManager::recordOperations` ← `State::fullSync`'s
lambda ← `State::fullSync` ← `GBI_RDP::fullSync` ←
`Interpreter::processRDPLists` ← `Application::processDisplayLists` ←

`factor5_gfx_runner` ← `rs64_run_lle_gfx` ← `RT64Context::send_dl` ←
`gfx_thread_func`. This is RT64-internal code (no source-level bug on
our side to fix, same class as the s86 TMEM-zero assert) hitting a
framebuffer-format reinterpretation case its own author never
implemented — a **13th, brand-new crash class**, first occurrence. No
field values are logged at the assert site (just the source condition
text), so the actual `srcFmt`/`srcSiz`/`dstFmt`/`dstSiz`/`tlutFormat`
combination that triggered it is unknown; not instrumenting yet per
the project's own convention (first occurrence, no dedicated soak
until a 2nd recent recurrence).

`composeNpcOrientationMatrix` (the 12th class, s92/s95) did **not**

meet the 2nd-recurrence bar NEXT.md set for promoting it to a
dedicated instrument.

Controls/other instruments: `dma-ring-producer` fired **only the n=0
boot call** (1/1) — confirms the process died before the ~140s mark
where the indirect-caller phenomenon occurs, same as s95.
`ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_CALLER` **0/0 again** — inconclusive, not refuted,

### Assessment

This is the **2nd consecutive soak** with `ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_CALLER`
armed that died to a *different*, unrelated crash before the ~140s
target window (s95: 12th class at hold+~5s; s96: 13th class at
hold+~3s). Per rule 8 this is 2 of up to 3 allowed non-discriminating
attempts — not yet grounds to park the DMA-caller hypothesis itself.
But two different early deaths in a row, both earlier than s93/s94's
soaks (which reached the ~140s mark and discriminated cleanly with a
similar-but-not-identical flag set), raises a **new, unconfirmed**
question worth a single falsifying check before a 3rd blind retry:
does adding `ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_CALLER` itself perturb timing enough to
let other races win earlier — the same *shape* of confound as s93's
`ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME` finding, not the same mechanism? The
instrument's check runs unconditionally inside `get_function`, a
single chokepoint called for every indirect (`LOOKUP_FUNC`/`jalr`) call
in the entire recompiled program (28388 call sites) — if that check
does anything more expensive than a raw integer compare per call (e.g.
an uncached `getenv()` read), it adds trivial-looking but very
high-frequency overhead exactly where s93's confound lived. **Checked
immediately, same session, no soak needed**: read
`lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/overlays.cpp:406-423` —
`rs64_log_dma_ring_caller`'s first statement is `if (addr !=
k_submit_dma_request_batch) return;`, a single `int32_t` compare, and
only the (already-rare) matching path reaches the `getenv`, which is
itself cached in a function-local `static const bool` evaluated once

correction, done before proposing any fix. The crash mechanism is a
classic unguarded table-lookup-then-dereference, identical shape to every
other class in this family:

    ctx->r2 = ADD32(((ctx->r4 & 0xFFFF) << 2), 0x8009FC10);  // table_base + (a0&0xFFFF)*4
    ctx->r17 = MEM_W(ctx->r2, 0x0);                          // s1 = table[idx]  (funcs_14.c:1657)
    ctx->r3  = MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0x30);                        // deref s1+0x30, no null/range check (funcs_14.c:1661)

`arg_r4` (the function's first argument, an animation/keyframe index) is
used unchecked as a table index; whatever pointer that slot holds is
dereferenced immediately at offset 0x30 with no bounds or null check. If
`arg_r4` is out of the table's real range, or the table slot itself hasn't
been populated yet, the dereference SIGBUSes. This is the same
"unchecked-pointer/index-off-an-arg" signature as the 9th
(`updateAnimatedTextureStreaming`), 10th (`static_5_800B4048`), and 14th
(`reserveAndEmitDLEntry`, `arg_r5=0x20000000` in every logged call in this
soak — a suspiciously round, flag-like value, consistent with the family's
"garbage-looking but structured" corruption signature) classes.

### Reframing NEXT.md's outcome-2 guidance

NEXT.md's outcome-2 branch (correctly triggered by this result) suggested
attacking timing — "a shorter hold or narrower probe schedule could reach
the DMA-caller window before hitting any of this family." **Checked this
against the existing timing data already in this log before adopting it**:
grepping this file's own past `hold+`/`hold-iter` mentions shows the
`do_rom_read`/DMA-adjacent crash consistently lands at **hold+11-15s**
(s85, s91, s93 all "hold+13s"; s94 "hold+13s into a driven session"),
while this family's one-off crashes land anywhere from **hold+3s to
hold+17s** across sessions (s96 13th class hold+~3s, this session's 16th
class hold+~4-5s, s97's 15th class hold+~14s) — i.e. **the two windows
overlap, they are not sequential**. Shortening the hold to "get past the
crash family before reaching the DMA window" is not coherent: the DMA
phenomenon's own window sits inside the same few-second span as the crash
family's, not after it. This corrects outcome-2's literal suggestion
without contradicting its actual point (stop instrumenting one-off
crashes) — full detail is a log-only re-read of existing session data, no
new soak was needed to check this.

### Assessment

Four consecutive sessions (s95, s96, s97, s98) and 6 soaks now end the same
way: reach the hangar-tick window, hit a brand-new crash class, die before
~15s into the hold. 16 distinct crash classes cataloged in this window
total (9th-16th being the guest-side, source-fixable family; 13th/15th
RT64-internal). Two of the guest-side family are now source-characterized
at the mechanism level (this session's `activateAnimationKeyframe`, and by
extension the same shape almost certainly applies to the still-uncharacterized
9th/10th/11th/12th/14th sites, which share the identical
"MEM_W-off-an-arg-or-table-slot, no check" signature per their own session
writeups). Given that four sessions of pure observation have each found a
*different* new crash rather than converging on a fix, and given the
mechanism is now understood well enough at two sites to write an actual
guard, the productive move for M3 is a state change: stop adding read-only
entry-log instruments to catalog new crashes, and instead **land a
defensive guard** at a characterized site, mirroring the two prior
successful patterns in this codebase (s83's `evalCubicSplineAtTime` 0/0
guard, s84's `resume_thread_tagged` `bad=1` skip-gate) — both fixed their
own crash class outright rather than just observing it.

### Next

Guard `activateAnimationKeyframe`'s table-lookup dereference
(`funcs_14.c:1656-1661`, guest `0x80061CA4-0x80061CAC`): before the
`MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0x30)` read, check `ctx->r17` for a plausible valid RDRAM
pointer (non-zero, within the guest RAM range the runtime maps) and skip
the crashing path (log via a new `ROGUESQ_LOG_ANIM_KEYFRAME_GUARD`-style
flag, always-on skip like s84's gate) if it looks bad. This is a genuine

sometimes the blocker); if a soak now reaches the DMA-caller window (~140s)

## Session 99 (2026-07-27) — landed the 16th crash class's guard (`activateAnimationKeyframe`, per s98's own pivot), caught and fixed a real bug in the guard's own bounds check same-session, then a clean corrected soak: guard's negative control holds (0/0) but the process died to a **recurrence of the already-catalogued 15th class** (RT64-internal `loadDrawState` assert, first seen s97), not a new class

Executed the exact work unit s98's NEXT.md specified: guarded
`activateAnimationKeyframe` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_14.c`, guest
`0x80061CA4`) at its unchecked `table[arg_r4 & 0xFFFF]` lookup-then-deref
(`ctx->r17 = MEM_W(ctx->r2, 0)` then `MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0x30)` with no
range check on `ctx->r17`). Per NEXT.md's own caution, checked the
function's control flow before writing the guard: `ctx->r17` is used
pervasively as a base pointer for the rest of the function body (not just
the one deref), so a partial guard (defaulting only the `+0x30` read)
would still crash later in the same function on the same bad pointer.
Also confirmed a bare early `return;` would NOT be ABI-safe: the
function's prologue spills `s0-s3`/`ra` to the guest stack and decrements
guest `$sp` by `0x28`; skipping the matching epilogue would leave the
*caller's* register state corrupted and the guest stack pointer
permanently drifted by 40 bytes every time the guard fired. Found the
function's own real exit label, `L_80061F18` (already the `goto` target
of the existing "lookup came back false" branch two lines below), which
performs the correct restore-then-return sequence — the guard `goto`s
there instead of hand-duplicating restore code. Landed in
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` following the `_dma_ring_producer_patch`
mid-function-anchor convention (anchored on the unique
`// 0x80061CA4: lw $s1, 0x0($v0)` comment line, confirmed via grep to
appear exactly once across all 45 `funcs_*.c`). Bounds: guest RAM range
`0x80000000`-`0x80800000`, matching the s78 `rt64_framebuffer_manager.cpp`
gate's convention (RDRAM is 8MB). New always-on flag:
`ROGUESQ_LOG_ANIM_KEYFRAME_GUARD=1`.

**Self-caught bug, same session, before this reached NEXT.md as a
conclusion:** the first build's soak (`s99_animkeyframe_guard1`) showed
`[anim-keyframe-guard]` firing **30333 times** — i.e., on essentially
every single call, not just a rare bad-pointer case. Root cause: `ctx->r17`
is `gpr` (`typedef uint64_t gpr`, `recomp.h:84`), and `MEM_W` returns a
*signed* `int32_t`. Assigning a real guest pointer like `0x8009FC10`
(top bit set, negative as `int32_t`) to a 64-bit unsigned register
sign-extends it to `0xFFFFFFFF8009FC10` — exactly the MIPS64 register
convention the `MEM_W` macro itself encodes (it subtracts
`0xFFFFFFFF80000000`, not `0x80000000`). The guard's original bounds
check compared this 64-bit sign-extended value directly against 32-bit
literals (`0x80000000u`/`0x80800000u`), which is false for every real
pointer and true for every real pointer under the "invalid" branch — the
guard was unconditionally short-circuiting the function's entire body,
not selectively catching one bad case. This is a **generalizable
lesson for any future guard on a `gpr`-typed register**: truncate through
`U32()` (recomp.h's existing `(uint32_t)` cast macro) before comparing
against 32-bit bounds, never compare the raw 64-bit value. Fixed in
`fixup_game_funcs.py` (`uint32_t r17_lo = U32(ctx->r17);` then compare
`r17_lo`), full regen (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py`
→ `cmake --build`, all clean) to get a pristine base for the corrected
patch to reapply onto (the buggy version was already baked into
`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_14.c` on disk and no longer matched the fix's
anchor regex).

Corrected soak (`s99_animkeyframe_guard2`, identical repro/flag set):
`[anim-keyframe-guard]` **0/0** — a real, working negative control this
time (contrast with the first build's 30333/30333 false-positive rate),
confirming the fix. Every other family control held: `[anim-recurse]`
3352, `[compose-npc-orient]` 573, `[dlentry-reserveAndEmit]` 19542,
`[anim-tex-stream]` 4494, `[hangar-entry]` 0, `[tmem-zero]` 0 (now 0/10
soaks armed), `thr-resume bad=1` 0. `ROGUESQ_LOG_DMA_CALLER` 0 (died
before the ~140s window, as expected); `dma-ring-producer` only the boot
call. Process reached "SELECT YOUR CRAFT stable" normally (phase-1024 at
44.7s, full key schedule, craft stable, Start probe) then died at
**hold-iter 5** (~hold+4-5s) — but this time to `RT64::State::
loadDrawState`'s abort (signal 6), the same **already-catalogued 15th
class** first seen at s97 (RT64-internal zero-sample-size assert, no fix
available on our side), not a new 17th class.

**What this establishes:** the guard is landed and functioning correctly
(validated by its own negative control), so it stays in place as a
genuine defensive fix for a real unguarded-pointer bug — but it did not
get to prove out further survival this run, because a *different*,
already-known, not-worth-chasing RT64-internal crash class killed the
process first, at essentially the same hold-offset (+4-5s) as every
other recent attempt. This matches NEXT.md's own outcome-2 branch
("guard never fires, a different crash preempts it — move to the
next-most-recurring characterized class") almost exactly, except the
preempting crash is a recurrence of 15 rather than a brand-new 17th —
arguably a *better* outcome than a new class, since 15 is already known
to need no further characterization. Per rule 8 and NEXT.md's own
precedent, next up is the same guard-not-instrument treatment for
`composeNpcOrientationMatrix` (2 occurrences: s74, s95 — the next most
frequent of the guest-side family), not a repeat soak of this site.

Source-read `composeNpcOrientationMatrix` (`static_5_800AB1C8`,
`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_40.c:6280-7102`) before writing anything,
per NEXT.md's explicit instruction (s92/s95 had only ever logged entry
args, never read the crash mechanism). Confirmed the same
unguarded-table-lookup-then-dereference shape as the rest of the family:
the function's outer loop reads a byte from a fixed lookup table
(`table1[a0 & 0xFF]`, `0x800AB238: lbu $s0, 0x0($v0)`, arbitrary
0-255 value, no range check), multiplies it by a fixed 632-byte stride
(the classic shift/add/sub multiply-by-constant idiom:
`byte*4+byte=byte*5`, `<<4=byte*80`, `-byte=byte*79`, `<<3=byte*632`),
and adds that to a **fixed global base pointer** (`MEM_W(ctx->r21,
-0x25A4)`, always the same value) to produce `v1` (`ctx->r3`,
`0x800AB25C: addu $v1, $v1, $a1`) — immediately dereferenced
(`0x800AB260: lw $t1, 0xC($v1)`, plus `+0x10`/`+0x14` two lines later)
and also stashed into `s3` (`ctx->r19 = v1+0x48`), which becomes a base
pointer threaded through the rest of the function body
(`composeRotationMatrixSlot1/2`, `transformVec3ToNpcLocalWithScale`,
etc.) — so a garbage table byte produces a wild `v1` that corrupts
everything downstream, not just the first deref, exactly like s99's
`activateAnimationKeyframe` finding.

Landed the guard immediately after `v1` is computed, before its first
use, following s99's exact template: `uint32_t r3_lo = U32(ctx->r3);`
checked against `[0x80000000, 0x80800000)` (guest RDRAM range), and on
failure `goto`s the function's own real epilogue, `L_800AB618`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_40.c:7063` — reloads
`s0-s7`/`fp`/`ra`/`f20`/`f22`/`f24`/`f26` unconditionally from the stack
and pops `$sp` by `0x78`, so it's ABI-safe from any point after the
prologue, not just this one). New always-on flag:
`ROGUESQ_LOG_COMPOSE_NPC_GUARD=1`.

**Caught a regex false positive before it ever reached a soak.** The
first `fixup_game_funcs.py` run reported the guard patched **twice** —
once in `funcs_40.c` (correct) and once in `funcs_27.c` (wrong). Checked
immediately rather than assuming success: `funcs_27.c`'s match was
inside `hangarInitialize`, a **completely different function in a
different overlay** that happens to share the same guest address range
(`0x800AB1xx`-`0x800ACxxx` — overlays reuse virtual addresses across
different loaded modules) and coincidentally contains the byte-identical
two-instruction sequence at the byte-identical address labels
(`0x800AB25C addu $v1,$v1,$a1` / `0x800AB260 lw $t1,0xC($v1)`), **including
its own same-named `L_800AB618` label** — so the `goto` would have
compiled cleanly with zero errors and silently jumped to the wrong place
inside a working, unrelated function, the first time this script's
convention of matching on raw instruction text (not function-scoped) has
actually collided. Fixed by scoping the substitution to `p.name ==
"funcs_40.c"` only (confirmed via `static_5_800AB1C8`'s definition site
that the real function lives there and nowhere else). Because the buggy
version had already been written to `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_27.c` and
`funcs_40.c` on disk, a full regen (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py`) was required to get a pristine base before
rebuilding — confirmed via grep that the corrected script now patches
`funcs_40.c` alone (`x1`) and leaves `funcs_27.c` untouched. **Generalizable
lesson for every future guard in this family**: the recompiler reuses
guest address ranges across overlays, so an instruction-text-only regex
anchor is not guaranteed unique across the whole `RecompiledFuncs/`
tree — scope-check the match count and, if a patch ever reports being
applied to more than the one expected file, treat it as a bug to find,
not a bonus.

## Session 102 (2026-07-27) — source-read `submitDmaRequestBatch` and the `musyxSynthFrame` call site, landed a correctly-targeted instrument, and proved the corrupted `devAddr` is already present in the source batch array before the call — ruling out both functions as the bug site and reframing the search one level further upstream

### What ran

Per NEXT.md's queued work unit (M3 item -1): source-read
`submitDmaRequestBatch`'s own body (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/
funcs_1.c:6168`, guest `0x8000569C`) before instrumenting anything, per
the iteration contract's "check the boring thing first" rule and s92's
own lesson about not instrumenting before reading the callee.

**Finding 1 — `submitDmaRequestBatch`'s actual signature**, confirmed by
reading its loop body (not assumed): `a0` (`ctx->r4`) is a pointer to an
array of 12-byte entries (`{size, devAddr, dramAddr}` at offsets
`+0x0/+0x4/+0x8`), `a1` (`ctx->r5`) is the entry count (loop bound,
`blez $s1` gate + `slt $t0,$s1` loop condition), `a2` (`ctx->r6`) is set
but not used in the copy loop itself. The loop increments both the
entry pointer and its `+8`-offset read cursor by `0xC` per iteration
(`addiu $s0,$s0,0xC` / `addiu $a3,$a3,0xC`) and copies each entry
verbatim into the DMA ring: entry`+0x0` → ring`+0x0` ("size"), entry
`+0x4` → ring`+0x4` ("devAddr" — the field every prior session's logs
show corrupted), entry`+0x8` → ring`+0x8` ("dramAddr"). This is a
faithful, unremarkable copy loop — no wrong-offset bug here.

**Finding 2 — this refutes/refines NEXT.md's own instrument plan.**
NEXT.md (written by s101, before this read) asked to log neighbors of
the *global slot* `G_BASE-0x68D8` on the theory that `a0` might itself
be an address one field off from the right one. The call site
(`funcs_24.c:3856-3875`, inside `musyxSynthFrame`) actually does `a0 =
MEM_W(G_BASE-0x68D8)` — a **pointer value loaded out of** that slot, not
the slot's own address (unlike `a2`, which genuinely is the literal
address `G_BASE-0x68D0` via `addiu`). So the informative neighbors to
inspect are around the *entry array `a0` points to*, not around the
global pointer variable itself — NEXT.md's originally-planned instrument
would not have tested the right thing.

**Instrument landed** (correctly targeting the above): new
`ROGUESQ_LOG_MUSYX_DMA_CALL=1` flag in `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`,
file-scoped to `funcs_24.c` (anchor text grep-confirmed unique before
scoping, following s100's belt-and-suspenders convention regardless).
Logs `a0`/`a1`/`a2` plus up to 3 decoded entries plus a raw word window
from `a0-16` to `a0+32`, all read from inside `musyxSynthFrame` right
before the call — directly comparable against the same-run
`dma-ring-producer` log.

**Housekeeping finding (unplanned, found while re-running the fixup
script):** `fixup_game_funcs.py`'s patches are **not actually idempotent**
despite the module docstring's claim. Each patch's regex anchor matches
the original instruction text, which is left unchanged after insertion —
so re-running the script against files that already carry a patch (i.e.
without a full `make_elf.py`→`N64Recomp` regen in between) inserts a
**second** copy of every matching patch. Confirmed via `grep -c` on
`funcs_40.c`: the s100 `composeNpcOrientationMatrix` guard comment
appears **3 times**, not once — accumulated across s100/s101/this
session's `python3 fixup_game_funcs.py` re-runs, none of which did a full
ELF regen first. Functionally harmless so far (each duplicate is an
identical guard; the first one's `goto` always wins if the pointer is
bad, so extras are dead code, not a correctness bug), but it means the
script is quietly bloating `RecompiledFuncs/*.c` every session and any
future guard whose anchor text happens to include something
order-sensitive would be at risk. Not fixed this session (out of scope
for the queued work unit) — flagged as a real, if low-priority, tooling
defect for a future work unit (the fix is straightforward: exclude
matches immediately followed by the corresponding `// PATCH:` marker, or
just always regen from ELF before running fixup).

Rebuilt clean (`DEVELOPER_DIR=... cmake --build ... -j 8`, exit 0, only
the pre-existing-class format/sign warnings). Soaked with the full
family-instrument set plus the new flag
(`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/s102_musyxdma/run.log`,
`PROBE_MODE=start_only HOLD_S=30`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME=0` per
s93's confound lesson).

### Result

Second soak ever (after s101) to survive the full hangar-tick-family
gauntlet and reach the ~140s DMA window alive. `[musyx-dma-call]` fired
17 times (positive control — the call happens, gated correctly on
`a1!=0`); the crash was the familiar `do_rom_read` SIGSEGV, **7th
occurrence**, byte-identical fields to every prior hit (`phys=
0x1C676672 dram=0x80195190 bytes=0x600`). Guard controls held: 11th/12th/
16th classes (`project-model-bounds-guard`/`compose-npc-orient-guard`/
`anim-keyframe-guard`) all fired 0 times (clean negative control, no new
data); `anim-recurse` 12102/12102 and `anim-tex-stream` 20664/no-crash
held as usual; `tmem-zero` still 0/9; no 9th–18th class fired.
`dlentry-reserveAndEmit` (14th class, previously only 1 occurrence) fired
79860 times this run with no crash — first real usage-frequency data
point for that log, not concerning on its own (no assertion tied to it).

**The key result** is the `[musyx-dma-call]` log for `n=0` (the call that
feeds the crashing consumer read), captured **before** `submitDmaRequestBatch`
is even entered:

```
[musyx-dma-call] n=0 a0=0x80179A60 a1=0x00000009 a2=0x80149730
[musyx-dma-call]   entry=0 size=0x00000600 devAddr=0x6C676672 dramAddr=0x80195190
[musyx-dma-call]   entry=1 size=0x00000600 devAddr=0x77696E67 dramAddr=0x80195790
[musyx-dma-call]   entry=2 size=0x00000300 devAddr=0x6C637265 dramAddr=0x80195D90
[musyx-dma-call]   window[-16]=0x00010000 window[-12]=0x00000510 window[-8]=0x4C3F5300 window[-4]=0x00000000
[musyx-dma-call]   window[+0]=0x00000600 window[+4]=0x6C676672 window[+8]=0x80195190 ...
```

`entry=0`'s `devAddr` (`0x6C676672`) is **already** the exact corrupted
value the ring-producer/consumer/`pi-start-dma`/`rom-read` logs show
downstream, bit-for-bit, at the moment `musyxSynthFrame` reads it out of
the array at `a0=0x80179A60` — **before** the call into
`submitDmaRequestBatch` even happens. This **proves** (not just refutes
by elimination) that neither `musyxSynthFrame`'s call-site register setup
nor `submitDmaRequestBatch`'s copy loop introduces or corrupts the value
— the bug is already fully formed in whatever populated this batch array,
one or more levels further upstream than either function this session
investigated.

The full 9-entry batch this run (`n=1`–`n=9` in `dma-ring-producer`
terms, `n=0` there is the unrelated boot call) decodes as: `lgfr`,
`wing`, `lcre`, `lglr`, `witg`, `lgqr`, `lgrr`, `wiyg`, `wizg`. This is
**not unstructured garbage** — every entry fits one of exactly two
4-byte shapes: `"lg" + <1 varying byte> + "r"` (n=1,4,6,7) or `"wi" +
<1 varying byte> + "g"` (n=2,5,8,9), plus one outlier (`n=3`, "lcre").
`size` and `dramAddr` are sane and mutually consistent in every entry
(`dramAddr` increments by exactly the previous entry's `size`: `0x80195190
→(+0x600)→ 0x80195790 →(+0x600)→ 0x80195D90`), so only the `devAddr`
field is wrong, consistently, across the whole batch — not a one-off
bit-flip. The fixed 2-byte prefix + 1 fixed suffix byte + 1 varying byte
shape is a stronger structural signature than "looks like ASCII" alone:
it reads like a **packed tag/index word being read where a ROM offset
belongs** (e.g. a 2-byte type tag + 2-byte per-entry sub-index, or a
name/hash table entry), not memory noise, a race, or a stomp. This is
additional, independent evidence against every already-refuted framing
(random per-run garbage, shared-corruption race, consumer desync,
external stomp) — the same two structural "families" recur with the
same shape both within this run's 9 entries and matching (for `n=1`)
every previous session's exact value back to s85.

### Assessment

This is real, source-grounded progress, not a repeat of the s94-s95
"instrument fired, still don't know who's upstream" pattern — this
session **positively confirmed** (via direct read-before-the-call
instrumentation, not inference) that the bug is not in either function
NEXT.md asked to investigate, and characterized the corruption's shape
precisely enough to narrow what kind of function must be upstream (one
that builds a small array of `{size, devAddr, dramAddr}` audio-DMA
requests once per VI retrace, sourcing `devAddr` from the wrong field of
whatever per-sample/per-instrument descriptor it reads). It does **not**
land a fix — per NEXT.md's own outcome-2 branch, forcing a guess-and-check
fix without knowing the populating function would not be evidence-based.
Matches outcome 2 as anticipated, but with substantially more evidence
than "doesn't match a neighboring field" — the neighboring-field question
was based on a premise (s101's) this session's own source read corrected
before ever building the wrong instrument.

## Session 103 (2026-07-27) — found and instrumented the real DMA-batch entry-writer, `fillSampleStreamRange`; refuted the session's own leading hypothesis (`acquireSampleStreamBlock`) with a clean discriminating soak

### What ran

Per NEXT.md's queued work unit (M3 item -1 continued): find what
populates the MusyX DMA-batch array (`a0=0x80179A60` in s102's soak)
with the corrupted `devAddr` field, one level upstream of
`musyxSynthFrame`/`submitDmaRequestBatch` (both cleared s102).

**Step 1 (cheap, no rebuild):** grepped `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c`
for the global slot the array pointer is loaded from
(`G_BASE-0x68D8`, confirmed s102 to be a fixed global holding a pointer
value, not the array's own base). Found it is written exactly **once**,
in `setupSongRenderBuffers` (`funcs_23.c:11344`, guest `0x8008F478`) —
a one-time `rs_malloc` at MusyX init, confirmed by reading the whole
function: it computes a buffer size from a count global, calls
`rs_malloc`, stores the result into the `-0x68D8` slot, and sets up a
mesg queue. Not a per-tick writer. The two other read sites
(`funcs_24.c:5128/5402`) are both `rs_free` calls in a teardown/shutdown
function's cleanup path — also not writers.

**Source-read of `acquireSampleStreamBlock`** (`funcs_23.c:11871-12057`,
guest `0x8008F758`), found via a broader `68D8` grep across all
`funcs_*.c` (the first pass had only checked the 4 refs already
in-hand; a second pass turned up 4 more, all in `funcs_23.c`). This
function is a linked-list cache lookup keyed by its sole argument `a0`
(walks a list rooted at global `-0x6650`, compares each node's `+0xC`
field against `a0`). On a cache miss it allocates a fresh node from a
free list (`-0x6654`), sets the new node's tag field (`+0xC`) to `a0`,
and then — at label `L_8008F800` — appends a new entry to the DMA batch
array: `entry.size = 0x100` (constant), `entry.devAddr = a2` (== `a0`,
unchanged since function entry — `addu $a2,$a0,$zero` is the only write
to `a2` anywhere in the function), `entry.dramAddr = node->0x8`. **This
looked like a strong candidate**: `devAddr` copied verbatim from a
cache-key argument with no translation step, and the sole call site
(`funcs_24.c:531-536`, inside `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`) passes
`a0 = MEM_W($s1, 0x34)`, a field off a per-stream object — plausibly a
name/tag rather than a ROM address. The corrupted values s102 captured
(`"lgfr"`/`"wing"`/`"lcre"`/…) are exactly what a packed 4-character
sample/stream tag would look like when misread as an address.

**Instrument landed to test this** (`ROGUESQ_LOG_STREAM_TAG=1`,
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, anchored on `acquireSampleStreamBlock`'s
function-entry boilerplate — unique by construction, function name
appears once): logs `a0` (the tag/candidate-devAddr) and the return
address at function entry, before anything touches it.

**Full regen from ELF this session** (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp
rogue_squadron.toml` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`, all rc
0) instead of re-running `fixup_game_funcs.py` alone against the
already-patched tree — this incidentally fixed s102's flagged
non-idempotency symptom for free: every patch reapplied exactly **x1**
(confirmed via the fixup script's own report line), including the s100
`composeNpcOrientationMatrix` guard that had accumulated 3 copies in
`funcs_40.c`. The underlying non-idempotency bug in the script itself
is **not** fixed (still no lookahead guard against re-matching an
already-patched anchor) — only worked around by regenerating clean this
time. Future sessions get the same accumulation if they run
`fixup_game_funcs.py` again without a fresh regen first.

Soaked (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/s103_streamtag/run.log`,
`PROBE_MODE=start_only HOLD_S=30`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME=0` per

### Result — hypothesis REFUTED, real writer found instead

Third soak to reach the ~140s DMA window alive (after s101/s102).
`[musyx-dma-call]` fired once more, byte-identical to s102: `n=0
a0=0x80179A60 a1=9`, `entry=0 devAddr=0x6C676672` ("lgfr"), same

signature (`osPiStartDma_recomp` → `do_dma` → `do_rom_read` SIGSEGV via

matching s101/s102's timing). Control held: `thr-resume bad=1` 0.

**`[stream-tag]` fired 0 times.** This is a real discriminating result,
not an unarmed-control null: the batch's own count field
(`G_BASE-0x68DC`, read as `a1=9` in the same `[musyx-dma-call]` log)
proves 9 entries were appended to the array **within this run**, and
that field is reset to 0 unconditionally at the top of every
`musyxSynthFrame` tick (`funcs_24.c:3295`) — so something added 9
entries this same tick, but it provably was not
`acquireSampleStreamBlock` (0 executions of that C function, any
calling convention, positive or negative). **This refutes the session's
own leading hypothesis** — the tag-copy code in
`acquireSampleStreamBlock` is real and does what the source read says,
but it is not what ran to build this run's crashing batch.

**Found the actual writer while re-reading the wider `68D8` grep
results**: `fillSampleStreamRange` (`funcs_23.c:12473-12630`, guest
`0x8008FAAC`), called from `musyxRenderVoiceSamples` *before*
`acquireSampleStreamBlock` in program order (`funcs_24.c:452/524`, two
calls per invocation). It walks a **different** linked list (rooted at
global `-0x664C`, not `acquireSampleStreamBlock`'s `-0x6650`/`-0x6654`
block cache) and, on finding a matching range node, appends a batch
entry at guest `0x8008FB40-0x8008FB90`: `entry.devAddr = node->0x8 +
node->0x10`, `entry.size` = a locally-computed fill-gap byte count,
`entry.dramAddr = node->0x14 + node->0x10` — every field a **computed
sum of two struct fields**, not a raw copy of an opaque argument. This
looks like legitimate address arithmetic (a running "bytes filled so
far" cursor added to a base), the opposite shape from the refuted
hypothesis.

**New open question, not yet answered**: if `fillSampleStreamRange`'s
arithmetic is sound, the corruption must be upstream of it too — most
likely `node->0x8` (the base-address field of this *second*,
still-unidentified struct type) already holds a tag-shaped value when
the node is created, and `fillSampleStreamRange` faithfully propagates
it forward by adding a (correct) running offset to a (wrong) base.
Confirmed by reading `acquireSampleStreamBlock`'s node-init path
(`L_8008F7A4`-`L_8008F800`) that it does **not** touch offsets `0x8`,
`0x10`, or `0x14` of anything — those must be set by whatever allocates
`fillSampleStreamRange`'s `-0x664C` list nodes, a function not yet
located (a same-file, `funcs_23.c`-only global per a `664C` grep across
all `funcs_*.c` — every other hit is an unrelated absolute address
substring-matching "664C", confirmed by inspection). Next work unit:

## Session 104 (2026-07-27) — refuted the `-0x664C` node allocator as the corruption source; new instrument proves the corruption is already present in `fillSampleStreamRange`'s own incoming arguments, closing the "is this function's arithmetic buggy" question and localizing the search to whatever writes the shared struct field both suspect functions read from

**Read `NEXT.md` first.** s103 left an open question: whatever
allocates/initializes `fillSampleStreamRange`'s `-0x664C` range-list
nodes must set a new node's `+0x8` field (the value that becomes
`devAddr`'s base) — that initializer was the next candidate for the
field-mapping bug.

### Found the allocator — and cleared it

`initSampleStreamBlockCache` (`funcs_23.c:12070-12227`, guest
`0x8008F858`), found via a straightforward `664C` grep across
`funcs_23.c` (a hit at guest `0x8008F8D0`, well before
`fillSampleStreamRange`'s own range at `0x8008FAAC`). Source-read in
full: a one-time MusyX-init routine. It calls `rs_malloc` twice — once
for a `1536*N`-byte sample-data buffer (`N` = the function's own `a0`
argument, the block count), once for a `24*N`-byte array of `N`
0x18-byte list nodes — then builds the node array's forward/backward
links (offsets `0x0`/`0x4`) and assigns each node a `0x600`-byte slice
of the sample buffer (offset `0x14` = `sample_base + i*0x600`,
confirming `0x600` as this system's fixed block size, matching
`fillSampleStreamRange`'s own `0x600` comparison constant from s103).
**It never touches offsets `0x8`, `0xC`, or `0x10` of any node.**

This looked at first like exactly the bug (a field silently left as
heap garbage) — but reading the rest of `fillSampleStreamRange` (past
where s103 stopped, `funcs_23.c:12693-13002`) shows every path that
claims a node for use — free-list pop (`L_8008FCD8`), single-active-
node eviction (`L_8008FD48` fast path when the active list has exactly
one entry), and general LRU eviction (unlinking the active list's tail
and reinserting it at the front, the longer `L_8008FD48` path) — all
converge on one shared block (`L_8008FDB8`, guest `0x8008FDB8`,
`funcs_23.c:12993-12999`) that **unconditionally recomputes**
`node->0x8 = a1 - ((a1 - a3) mod 0x600)` from the function's own `a1`
(the requested DRAM target) and `a3` (the tag) arguments, immediately
before use. So the allocator never needs to initialize `+0x8` — nothing
ever reads a node's `+0x8` without first passing through this
recompute. **`initSampleStreamBlockCache` is cleared as a suspect.**

### New instrument — and a clean discriminating result

This pushes the search one level up: `a1`/`a3` are themselves computed
in `musyxRenderVoiceSamples` (`funcs_24.c` ~397-451, identical shape at
all 4 `fillSampleStreamRange` call sites in that function, not just the
2 s103 had looked at) from a single shared source: `MEM_W($s1, 0x34)`
— and `$s1` there is `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`'s own `a0` argument (a
per-voice/stream descriptor pointer). Notably this is the **exact same
struct field** (`+0x34`) the existing `fixup_game_funcs.py` comment for
`ROGUESQ_LOG_STREAM_TAG` had already identified as feeding
`acquireSampleStreamBlock`'s (unreached-this-run) `a0` argument at a
different call site in the same function — i.e. both candidate writer
functions independently bottom out at one shared field.

Landed `ROGUESQ_LOG_FILL_RANGE_ARGS=1` (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`,
anchored on `fillSampleStreamRange`'s function-entry boilerplate) to log
its raw incoming `a0`-`a3` (`ctx->r4`-`r7`) before anything touches
them. Full regen from ELF (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`, all rc 0); fixup report showed
every patch applied exactly **x1** including the new one — no
duplication this time (s103's full-regen workaround holds up on a
second use).

Soaked (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/s104_fillargs/run.log`,
`PROBE_MODE=start_only HOLD_S=30`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME=0`,
`ROGUESQ_LOG_MUSYX_DMA_CALL=1` + `ROGUESQ_LOG_STREAM_TAG=1` +
`ROGUESQ_LOG_FILL_RANGE_ARGS=1`). Reached the ~140s DMA window alive
(phase log: `vi_width=640` at 146.5s) and died at hold-iter 15 to the
same `do_rom_read` assertion abort as every prior session (9th
occurrence; `[rom-read]`/`[pi-start-dma]` fields weren't logged this

held: `thr-resume bad=1` 0, `ost-wb SKIP_WIDTH` 0.

**`[fill-range-args]` fired 7 times, immediately before `[musyx-dma-call]`'s
9-entry batch dump, and the values match byte-for-byte**: `n=0
a1_dram=0x6C676672` = the batch's `entry=0 devAddr=0x6C676672`
("lgfr") exactly; `n=1 a1_dram=0x77696E67` = `entry=1
devAddr=0x77696E67` ("wing") exactly. **The corruption is already
present in `fillSampleStreamRange`'s own incoming `a1`/`a3` arguments
at function entry, before its alignment arithmetic runs at all.** This
closes the question s103 left open in the opposite direction from what
looked likely: `fillSampleStreamRange`'s own computed-arithmetic write

Read `musyxKeyOnVoice` (`funcs_24.c:1825`, guest `0x80090A3C`) start to

block at destination `+0x30/+0x34/+0x38` (source-copied from a

like a match for the field we're chasing. But its destination pointer
is computed from a completely different global (`G_BASE-0x68B0`'s
*dereferenced* value, i.e. a runtime pointer stored at guest
`0x80149750`, described by the existing `musyxBuildVoiceCommandList`
symbol comment as the head of an "RSP cmd-list") — not the
`G_BASE-0x6908`-plus-`voiceIdx*0x88` array that `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`
actually indexes (confirmed by re-reading `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`
itself, `funcs_24.c:6-`: its own `$s1` is simply its own `a0` argument,
untouched by any global lookup). **`musyxKeyOnVoice`'s write is to an
unrelated RSP-microcode command list, not the CPU-side voice struct —
cleared as a suspect for this specific field.**

Found the actual matching writer instead: **`musyxInitVoiceFromSample`**
(`funcs_24.c:5753`, guest `0x80092128`, symbol-commented "load
loop/base/sampPtr from descriptor"). Its voice-slot base is
`G_BASE-0x6908` indexed by `voiceIdx*0x88` — matching
`musyxRenderVoiceSamples`'s own indexing exactly, confirmed by 3
independent offset matches: `+0x4` (rate, this function's own default
`0x1000` write vs. `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`'s `MEM_HU(+0x4)` read) and
`+0x3C`/`+0x40` (loop points, written here from `sampleDesc+0x10`/
`+0x14`, read directly by `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`'s own resample
loop). Its body contains one exact-match instruction, `sw $v1,
0x34($a0)` where `$v1 = MEM_W(a1, 0x4)` — i.e. `voice+0x34 =
sampleDesc+0x4`, a straight verbatim word copy, no arithmetic to be
buggy in. Also copies `sampleDesc+0xC/+0x10/+0x14` to `voice+0x38/

chain traces back to.

Both call sites (`funcs_22.c:3667`, `funcs_26.c:1418`) build
`sampleDesc` **fresh, right before the call**, rather than pointing at
a stable ROM/asset table entry: `funcs_22.c`'s site points `a1` at a

by `-8`) that earlier code in the same function populates field by
field; `funcs_26.c`'s site builds a small on-stack struct from local
registers (`$s1`-`$s6`) immediately above the call. Neither is a raw
"read the wrong offset of a real asset table" bug on its face — if the
corruption enters here, it's carried in from whichever of those
call-site-local sources the live run actually used, not from a
mis-indexed table lookup inside `musyxInitVoiceFromSample` itself.

framing was wrong in a useful way: `tickAllAudioChannels` has a **real
static caller**, findable by plain grep — `tickAudioSequencerFrame`
(`funcs_23.c:6654`), called unconditionally partway through that function's
body (after an early-return gate, see below), *not* another
invisible-to-grep indirect call like `serviceVoicePoolFrame`'s own caller.

`tickAudioSequencerFrame` itself has exactly 3 static call sites, all
inside `musyxSynthFrame` (`funcs_24.c:3097`, the already-confirmed-running
per-VI-retrace audio tick, s101). Each of the 3 sites is gated by the same
shape: a per-tick countdown at a fixed global (`G_BASE-0x68EC`) is
decremented; only when it hits exactly 0 does the code call
`tickAllActiveSongs` then `tickAudioSequencerFrame`, and reload the
countdown from a period value at a second fixed global (`G_BASE-0x68E8`).
This is a classic tick-divider ("run the sequencer once every N ticks"),
structurally unrelated to the DMA-batch/streaming machinery s101-s106
already confirmed active. `tickAudioSequencerFrame` also has its own,
independent second gate at its own entry — `if (MEM_W(rdram, 0x80142038)
== 0) return;` — before it would ever reach the (unconditional, further
down) call to `tickAllAudioChannels`. So the real ladder, corrected, is:
`musyxSynthFrame` → [countdown-divider gate] → `tickAudioSequencerFrame`
→ [gate2038 early-return] → `tickAllActiveSongs` +
`tickAllAudioChannels` → [channel-count gate] → per-channel loop →
[per-channel active-flag gate] → `tickAudioChannel`.

Landed entry counters at the two newly-found rungs (`N64Recomp/
fixup_game_funcs.py`, same shared `ROGUESQ_LOG_VOICE_TRIGGER_CHAIN=1`
gate and cap-at-20 style as s106's two): `tickAudioSequencerFrame`
(logs `n` + the `gate2038` value read fresh at entry) and
`tickAllAudioChannels` (logs `n` + the channel-count byte at
`0x80141AD0`, the value its own `blez` skip-the-whole-loop check reads).
Full regen from ELF (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py`
→ `cmake --build`, all rc 0); fixup report showed both patched exactly
`x1` in `funcs_23.c`, no duplication, alongside all prior patches
re-applying cleanly at `x1` each.

**Soak** (`s107_voicechain`, same repro shape as s105/s106): reached
`vi_width=640` at 151.1s (past the familiar ~140s DMA window) and died to
the same `do_rom_read` SIGSEGV as every prior session — **12th
occurrence** (same crash signature: `piDmaWorker` → `osPiStartDma_recomp`
→ `do_dma` → `do_rom_read`). Positive control clean and strong:
`musyx-dma-call` fired **17** times, `fill-range-args` fired **7** times
— the surrounding MusyX per-tick system was genuinely active across the
whole run, same as s106 soak 2. Against that backdrop, **both new
counters read 0/0**: `tickAudioSequencerFrame` never fired once, and
neither did `tickAllAudioChannels` (unsurprising given the former is its
only caller, but confirms no other call path exists either).
`tick-audio-channel`, `service-voice-pool-frame`, and `init-voice-sample`
all still read 0/0 too, consistent with s106.

**This is a materially stronger result than s106's**, not just one more
null in the same chain: it proves the block sits at or before the
countdown-divider gate *inside `musyxSynthFrame` itself* — a completely
different location than "an unlocated indirect caller" (there is none;
every link in this chain is a plain static call once you read the
source instead of grepping for `LOOKUP_FUNC`/`jalr`). Two live
possibilities, not yet distinguished: (a) the countdown genuinely never
reaches 0 in this run because its period (`G_BASE-0x68E8`) is very large
or the countdown itself starts corrupted/frozen — testable directly; or
(b) some higher-level "is a sequenced song even active" flag this
tick-divider logic itself depends on (not yet located, could gate the
whole `musyxSynthFrame` region these 3 call sites live in) is off for
this scene's music, which would mean the per-tick song-sequencer
subsystem is simply not exercised by this scene's audio at all — a clean
fit for s105/s106's H1 (this scene never needs a fresh key-on via this
path) rather than H2 (wrong struct). Not a 3rd consecutive null on the
*same* sub-hypothesis (rule 8) — this is the 1st soak testing the
countdown-divider location specifically, so continuing is still in
budget, but per "one work unit," parked for next session.

**Next step**: instrument the countdown/period pair directly
(`G_BASE-0x68EC`/`G_BASE-0x68E8`) at `musyxSynthFrame`'s own entry or at
one representative call site (e.g. log once per `musyxSynthFrame` call,
capped, the current countdown value before decrement) — this single
instrument distinguishes (a) "counting down normally, just needs a
longer capture or a smaller period to observe a firing" from (b) "stuck
at a fixed nonzero value" from (c) "period reloaded to something huge/
corrupted every time it would hit zero." If the countdown is behaving
sanely and firing is simply *rare*, do not repeat the same ~150s soak
shape hoping to get lucky — either lengthen the hold window or (cheaper)
just log every reload of the period value directly to see its magnitude
without needing to catch a live firing at all.

**Placement correction (found before shipping, not after a failed soak):**
NEXT.md's literal wording said to guard "immediately after
`ctx->r16 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0);`" (right after the entry diagnostic). Source
reading the full prologue first showed this is unsafe: at that point `$ra`
and the old `$s1` are not yet saved to their stack slots (`0x18`/`0x14` off
`$sp`) — only the old `$s0` is (saved one instruction earlier, before
reassignment). Jumping straight to a restore-from-stack epilogue from there
would load uninitialized stack bytes into `$ra` and corrupt the return
address on the way out. The function's own existing bounds check (an
`sltu`/`bne` a few instructions later, unrelated to this guard — it
compares `$s0` against a value loaded from a fixed global slot, likely a
buffer-end check, not an address-space sanity check) saves `$ra` to its
stack slot on both the taken and fall-through paths at guest `0x8000CBAC`.
The guard is anchored on the fall-through copy of that save (disambiguated
from the taken-branch copy via a lookahead on the immediately-following
`0x8000CBB0 lui`, which only precedes the fall-through copy) — this is
still strictly before the first dereference of `ctx->r16`
(`MEM_W(0X0, ctx->r16) = 0xB5000000;` at `0x8000CBBC`), and now all three
restore-target stack slots are populated before any jump to the epilogue.

`G_BASE-0x6908 + voiceIdx*0x88`, built by a `lui/lw` load of a fixed global
pointer slot followed by `voiceIdx*0x11*8`. A literal-offset store-form
grep (`MEM_W(0X34, ctx->rN) =`, the LHS/store shape N64Recomp emits for
`sw $rN, 0x34($base)`) across all 45 files returns ~250 hits, but the
overwhelming majority are `ctx->r29` (stack-frame register-save
prologues/epilogues, offset 0x34 into an unrelated stack frame) or other
structs that coincidentally share offset 0x34. Rather than hand-classify
250 unrelated hits, anchored the search on the base-pointer computation
itself: `grep -n "MEM_W(ctx->r[0-9]*, -0X6908)" *.c` (the load-form read of
the fixed global slot) returns **exactly 21 hits, all in one file**,
`funcs_24.c` — confirming the entire voice array is only ever addressed via
that one global slot, and only from that one file. (A second grep hit two
lines in `funcs_32.c` matching the bare substring `-0X6908`, but those pair
with `lui $a0,0x800B`, not `0x8015` — a different global 108 KB away that
coincidentally shares the low-16-bit displacement; confirmed unrelated and
discarded.)

Mapped all 21 load sites to their enclosing functions in `funcs_24.c`
(`musyxMixActiveVoices`, `musyxBuildVoiceCommandList`, `isAudioSlotActive`,
`musyxInitVoiceFromSample`, `musyxStartVoiceRelease`,
`musyxStoreVoiceAdsrParams`, `musyxTriggerVoiceAttack`, `musyxStopVoice`,
`musyxSetVoicePitchBend`, `setVoiceModulationParams`,
`stopVoiceMarkRetrigger`, `beginVoiceFadeRelease`, `deactivateVoice`,
`getVoiceUserField`) and grepped each function's own line range for any
`0X34)` reference at all (read or write). Also checked
`musyxRenderVoiceSamples` and `musyxKeyOnVoice` (voice pointer arrives as a
direct argument in these two, not via the global-slot load, so they don't
appear in the -0x6908 list but are known voice-struct consumers) and
`musyxSynthFrame` (the per-tick driver) for the same reason.

**Result: exactly one write to voice+0x34 exists anywhere in the
recompiled tree** — `musyxInitVoiceFromSample`, guest `0x800921E8`
(`sw $v1, 0x34($v0)`, `funcs_24.c:5881`), already fully cleared by s105/106
(clean verbatim copy from `sampleDesc+0x4`, both call sites build the
source struct fresh from local data, 0/0 fires across 2 soaks with a
positive control). Every other function that touches the voice array reads
other offsets but **never touches offset 0x34** at all (not even as a
read) — including `musyxKeyOnVoice`, which reads offset 0x34 three times
(`0x34` off `$s0`, confirming it as a genuine voice-struct consumer) but
never writes it, consistent with s105's "writes a different global
entirely" classification. `musyxRenderVoiceSamples` reads voice+0x34 once
(guest `0x8009023C`, feeding the corrupted value into `fillSampleStreamRange`
per s103/s104) but does not write it — the write-form grep inside that
function's body (line 465) is a false-positive-looking hit on a
*different* pointer (`$s0`, the function's own 4th argument, a
stream/node struct — not the voice pointer `$s1`/arg0), confirmed by
tracing both registers back to their originating arguments.

**This closes the "static-write" branch of NEXT.md's own two-way question
with a clean, decisive null**: the corruption does **not** enter via any
direct `MEM_W(..., 0x34)` store keyed off the confirmed voice-slot base
anywhere in the 45-file recompiled guest tree. Per NEXT.md's own framing,
this points the mechanism at one of: (a) an LLE RSP-side write via the
MusyX audio microcode (`factor5_ucode`) — the microcode has its own
independent `MEM_W`-equivalent access to the same RDRAM and is **not**
covered by this guest-C grep at all — or (b) a runtime-computed (non-literal)
offset store that a literal-immediate grep cannot see by construction.

**(a) gained real, independent support this session, not derived from any
new instrument**: s110 (previous session, same soak) flagged 385 lines of
`Unhandled jump target 0x1883 in microcode factor5_ucode` — the first time
that specific diagnostic has ever read nonzero — as an unexplained side
observation. `M5`'s notes describe the recompiled MusyX ucode
(`factor5_ucode_b_recompiled.c`) as "recompiles but is a never-called
artifact"; s110's evidence and this session's decisive guest-side null
together now make "the RSP audio ucode actually runs and writes RDRAM
directly, bypassing every guest-C store this grep could see" the leading
candidate mechanism, not a coincidental side note. Confirmed (source read,
no build) that the ucode's own recompiled output and dispatch tooling
(`tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py`, `docs/factor5-ucode-dispatch.md`,
`include/rsp_dpc_macros.h`) exist as real, separate artifacts from the
guest-C tree grepped this session — a plausible, previously-uninvestigated
write path.

**Assessment**: this retires the "enumerate static writers" work unit
cleanly (decisive null, not inconclusive) and reframes M3's blocker
question from "which function writes voice+0x34" (answered: nothing in
guest C does, beyond the already-cleared writer) to "does the LLE MusyX
RSP microcode write into the voice array, and does its unhandled-jump-target
0x1883 correlate with the corruption". That is a different investigative
surface (RSP ucode dispatch table / `factor5_ucode` recompiled output, not
`RecompiledFuncs/*.c`) and needs its own read before any instrument is
designed — do not assume the mechanism without first reading how
`factor5_ucode`'s recompiled dispatch handles (or fails to handle) jump
target `0x1883`.

## Session 112 — 2026-07-27

Picked up NEXT.md's prescribed work unit: read (not instrument) how
`factor5_ucode`'s RSP dispatch handles the unhandled jump target `0x1883`
that s110 first observed, to test hypothesis (a) — that the LLE MusyX
audio microcode writes into the voice array's RDRAM range via its own
independent `MEM_W`-equivalent path, bypassing every guest-C store s111's
grep could see. Pure source-read/grep task, **no build or run**.

**Method.** Read `docs/factor5-ucode-dispatch.md` first (per NEXT.md step
2) — it documents the *graphics* ucode's dispatch loop and opcode table
(vertex pipeline, clip, F3D-style opcodes), not audio. Located the actual
"Unhandled jump target" printf sites (`tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py` only
silences the *boot* ucode's expected one; the *main* ucode's own printf is
untouched, generated by RSPRecomp itself) in the built output:
`build/factor5_ucode/factor5_ucode_recompiled.c:3165`, inside the
`do_indirect_jump` switch's default case. That switch (`(jump_target |
0x1000) & 0x1FFF`, ~45 cases) is the exhaustive set of jump targets
RSPRecomp statically resolved during translation; `0x1883` is absent from
it entirely — not fixed up away, never a recognized target at all. Two
supporting observations, neither pursued further this session (not needed
to answer the discriminating question): `0x1883` falls strictly between
labels `L_1828` and `L_18F0` (mid-block, not an instruction boundary) and
its low 12 bits (`0x883`) are not a multiple of 4 — consistent with a
corrupted/garbage register value driving the jump, not a legitimate
control-flow edge, but this is a side note, not this session's finding.

**The decisive result**: `factor5_ucode` (no suffix) is **not** the MusyX
audio microcode. `src/main/main.cpp:407` calls `factor5_ucode(rdram,
ucode_addr)` unconditionally for **every single graphics task** (the
call immediately following DL/DMEM staging, `[runner-step] entering
factor5_ucode` on the hot path). The actual MusyX audio ucode is a
**separate, differently-named** recompiled function, `factor5_ucode_b`
— and `main.cpp:76` only `extern`-declares it; a repo-wide grep for
`factor5_ucode_b(` across `src/` finds **zero call sites**, matching
`main.cpp:292`'s own comment verbatim: *"An earlier theory recompiled
0x99FE0 as a 'second gfx ucode' factor5_ucode_b — wrong: it's the audio
ucode. The recompile is kept in-tree but must never run for gfx tasks."*
M5's characterization ("recompiles but is a never-called artifact") is
therefore about `factor5_ucode_b`, and is correct and unrelated to the
`0x1883` diagnostic — which fired in `factor5_ucode`, the graphics ucode,
called thousands of times per soak for ordinary DL processing, with no
audio/MusyX involvement whatsoever.

**This refutes hypothesis (a) as s111/NEXT.md framed it, at the source
level, with no instrument needed**: s110's "385 lines of `Unhandled jump
target 0x1883 in microcode factor5_ucode`" is not audio-adjacent evidence
at all. The apparent "independent support" s111 cited was a naming
collision — "microcode factor5_ucode" in the printf string and "the MusyX
ucode" in M5's prose are two different microcodes that happen to share the
"factor5_ucode" substring, one with and one without the `_b` suffix.
`voice+0x34`'s corruption cannot be explained by this RSP task: the
graphics ucode has no reason to touch MusyX voice-descriptor RDRAM, and
the actual audio ucode that might is provably dead code.

**Reopens hypothesis (b)**: a runtime-computed (non-literal-offset) store
in guest C that s111's literal-immediate grep (`MEM_W(0X34, ...)`) could
not see by construction — e.g. a byte/word copy loop indexed by a variable
field offset, or a `memcpy`-shaped helper, writing into the voice struct's
`+0x34` slot without any source line containing the literal text `0x34`.
Not yet searched this session (out of scope — NEXT.md's step 3/4 gate on
first confirming or refuting ucode plausibility, which is now done).

**Assessment**: retires the RSP-ucode branch of the M3 blocker question
with a decisive, no-build source read — `0x1883` is an orphaned artifact
of the *graphics* dispatch table (likely itself a downstream symptom of
the same corruption elsewhere, given its mid-instruction/non-4-aligned
shape), not a MusyX write path. Next step is searching for computed-offset
writes into the voice struct in guest C (hypothesis b), not any further
RSP-ucode instrumentation.

## Session 113 — 2026-07-27

Picked up NEXT.md's prescribed work unit: search guest C for a
runtime-computed (non-literal-offset) store into the MusyX voice struct
that could land on `voice+0x34` — hypothesis (b), reopened by s112 after
it closed the RSP-ucode branch. Pure source-read task, **no build or
run**.

**Method.** Three files reference the voice-array base pointer's global
slot (`-0x6908`) at all: `funcs_23.c`, `funcs_24.c`, `funcs_32.c`
(confirmed via `grep -rl -- "-0X6908"` across every `RecompiledFuncs/*.c`
— exhaustive, not a sample). Delegated one focused read-only audit per
file (parallel subagents) with an explicit brief: trace every arithmetic
path from the `-0x6908` load to any store (`MEM_W`/`MEM_H`/`MEM_B`/
`MEM_HU`/`MEM_BU`/`SD` as an lvalue), flagging any target address built
from a register/loop-index rather than a bare literal immediate. Verified
the two highest-value claims myself afterward by reading the exact lines
before writing them here (not taking agent prose on faith).

**Hypothesis (b) refuted, exhaustively.** `funcs_24.c`: 12 functions
(`musyxMixActiveVoices`, `isAudioSlotActive`, `musyxInitVoiceFromSample`,
`musyxStartVoiceRelease`, `musyxStoreVoiceAdsrParams`,
`musyxTriggerVoiceAttack`, `musyxStopVoice`, `musyxSetVoicePitchBend`,
`setVoiceModulationParams`, `stopVoiceMarkRetrigger`,
`beginVoiceFadeRelease`, `deactivateVoice`, `getVoiceUserField`) all
compute the same `idx*0x88` stride off the voice base, but every single
store through the result uses one more **compile-time literal** offset
(0x0/0x1/0x4/0x22/0x28/0x2A/0x2C/0x30/0x58/0x60/0x64/0x68/0x6C/0x7C/0x80/
0x84/0x85 — never 0x34, never computed). The one genuine per-voice stride
loop in this file (`musyxSynthFrame`, `L_800913C0`) only stores to fixed
literals 0x10/0x14. `funcs_32.c`'s two `-0x6908` hits are a **different,
unrelated** global at a different base address (`0x8015` vs `0x800B`) and
aren't stores at all — this file has no voice-array reference whatsoever.
`funcs_23.c` writes the `-0x6908`/`-0x6904` globals exactly once
(`allocateSongChannelArray`, confirming the 0x88 stride and the
base-pointer relationship) and never reads them back in this file, so no
further chained store exists here either — its own init loop only writes
0x0/0x84/0x85. **No computed-offset write to voice+0x34 exists in guest C,
full stop** — every arithmetic path from the voice base terminates in a
literal, non-0x34 store. This closes hypothesis (b) the same way s112
closed hypothesis (a): decisively, at the source level, no instrument
needed.

**Unplanned high-value find, same audit: the missing `-0x664C` node
allocator, located.** s103 characterized `fillSampleStreamRange` as
computing `entry.devAddr = node->0x8 + node->0x10` off a linked list at
global `-0x664C`, and confirmed `acquireSampleStreamBlock`'s node-claim
path never touches offsets `0x8`/`0x10`/`0x14` — but its allocator was
"not yet located" across three prior sessions (s102-s104). It's
`initSampleStreamBlockCache` (`funcs_23.c:12103`, guest `0x8008F858`) —
confirmed the only function anywhere referencing the exact literal
`-0X664C` besides the three already-characterized consumers (`grep -rl
-- "-0X664C"` across all of `RecompiledFuncs/*.c` returns only
`funcs_23.c`). It `rs_malloc`s an array of 0x18-byte nodes and its init
loop (`L_8008F8FC`, `funcs_23.c:12204-12228`) writes exactly two fields
per node: `0x4` (next-pointer) and `0x14` (a data-buffer address,
`base+n*0x600`). **It never writes offsets `0x8` or `0x10` — the exact
two fields `fillSampleStreamRange` sums into `devAddr`.** Read
`rs_malloc`'s own full body (`funcs_0.c:2743`, ends `funcs_0.c` ~line
2950s) end-to-end looking for a zeroing call: **no `memset`/`bzero`/
`rs_memset` call anywhere in it** — it is a bare heap-carve allocator,
does not zero returned memory.

**New root-cause hypothesis, well-supported by three independent static
facts, not yet runtime-confirmed**: offsets `0x8`/`0x10` of every
`-0x664C` list node are **never initialized by any guest code** —
neither the allocator (this session) nor the claim path (s103) ever
writes them, and no other file references this exact global (this
session's grep). `fillSampleStreamRange` reads them anyway and sums
whatever `rs_malloc` handed back — leftover contents of previously-used
heap memory, not a corrupted *write*. This would explain, for the first
time with a mechanism instead of a label: (1) s102's "structured
tag-like" byte patterns (`"lg?r"`/`"wi?g"`) — plausible fragments of
whatever string/tag data last occupied that heap region (asset names are
the obvious candidate in an audio-asset-heavy allocator); (2) s91/s93's
byte-identical reproduction across independent runs/rebuilds — not a race
at all, just a deterministic function of asset-load heap history, which
is itself deterministic given deterministic boot-time loading order.
This reframes the entire `do_rom_read` corruption chain (s85 through
s104, 9 occurrences) from "something writes the wrong value" to "nothing
ever writes a value, and the field was never actually the field
`fillSampleStreamRange` thinks it is" — same diagnostic shape as s78's
uninitialized-field bugs elsewhere in this codebase, not a new mechanism.

**Not yet done, and the reason it isn't in CURRENT-TRUTH as confirmed**:
this is three *static* facts (no writer in the allocator, no writer in
the claim path per s103, no other referencing file), not a *runtime*
observation. The two-independent-lines-of-evidence bar (ITERATION.md rule
4) is arguably met by the static reads alone, but a single runtime log —
reading `node->0x8`/`node->0x10` immediately inside the allocator's own
init loop, before any consumer could possibly have touched them — would
turn "never written, by exhaustive static search" into "read back as
already-nonzero garbage at the moment of allocation," which is strictly
stronger and cheap to get. That's the next work unit (see NEXT.md);
deliberately not attempted this session per the same discipline s112 used
(read first, instrument only once the read narrows the target to
something a single soak can decide).
