source-file:line resolution if it worked, entirely sidestepping the
byte-offset-guessing exercise below) — **both denied**, "This command requires
approval," in this non-interactive session. Confirms s202-206's note is still
current; not re-litigating this again barring an environment change.

**Step 2 — a build-config fact that answers a standing open question**: grepped
`CMakeLists.txt` for the RecompiledFuncs target and found (line 239, s38's own
comment): **this whole project builds `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` (`-O0`), and
`RecompiledFuncs` (which holds `funcs_4.c`/`funcs_6.c`) is NOT in the
short-list of 3 translation units (`FACTOR5_UCODE_C`/`_B_C`/`_BOOT_C`) that get
an explicit `-O2` override.** So `renderUnlitMeshFaces` and its callee both
compile fully unoptimized. Separately, `RECOMP_FUNC` (`N64Recomp/include/recomp.h:22`)
expands to `extern inline __attribute__((weak,noinline))` on the clang/GCC
branch this build uses — **every recompiled game function, including
`getTextureLUTFieldAt8`, is explicitly `noinline`.**

Together these two facts **definitively rule out** the possibility raised
while re-reading this session (see Step 3): that `renderUnlitMeshFaces+508`
in the crash log could actually be *inside* an inlined call to
`getTextureLUTFieldAt8` (the function's one and only callee — grepped the
full `4951-5605` range for the `[A-Za-z_]+\(rdram, *ctx\);` call pattern s206
used on `processSceneNode`, exactly one hit). `noinline` + `-O0` means that
call is a real, separate machine-code jump to a real, separate symbol; a
fault inside it would dladdr-resolve to `getTextureLUTFieldAt8+N`, not
`renderUnlitMeshFaces+508`. **The crash is confirmed to be genuinely inside
`renderUnlitMeshFaces`'s own body**, closing off a branch that would otherwise
have needed its own investigation.

`-O0` also revises (upward in confidence, but not to certainty) the
offset-to-source-line linear-mapping assumption NEXT.md flagged as unverified:
no inlining, no cold-path splitting, no instruction scheduling/reordering at
`-O0` — source order should track machine-code order much more faithfully
than under `-O2`. The magnitude of the ARM64-instructions-per-MIPS-line ratio
is still unmeasured (no calibration point exists — this is the only
`[CRASH][pc-symbol]` line captured so far, see PORTING-STATE grep), and `-O0`
tends to be *more* verbose per statement (stack-spill-heavy), which could push
the true offset earlier than a naive per-line estimate, not later — so this
is a *directional* refinement, not a solved calibration.

**Step 3 — the actual re-read.** Read `funcs_4.c:4951` through `5605` (the
full function, but line-by-line with the offset framing and the callee
question in mind, not a repeat of s204's method) plus `funcs_6.c:13392-13417`
(the one callee, `getTextureLUTFieldAt8`). Findings:

- The conservative NEXT.md window (`4951-5030`, prologue + the linked-list

  correctly via C's implicit `int32_t -> uint64_t` promotion rule on
  assignment (same convention verified for the other five callees since
  s200).
- The one callee call site (`getTextureLUTFieldAt8`, line 5083, ~132 source
  lines / an estimated ballpark of the 127-ARM64-instruction mark) — the
  callee itself (`funcs_6.c:13392-13417`, 11 real instructions) is a clean
  bounded LUT lookup: its one argument is masked `& 0xFFFF` on entry, all
  address math goes through `ADD32`, the one load is `MEM_HU` at a fixed

  used as a pointer). No zero-extension-bypass pattern; also now confirmed
  architecturally non-inlined (Step 2), so this call cannot be the
  `+508`-attributed fault regardless.
- Extended the read past both offset estimates through the rest of the
  function (`5090-5605`) with the same checklist — including the two loop
  back-edges that walk linked-list "next" pointers via `MEM_W(reg, 0)`/`MEM_W(reg,
  4)` (lines 5546, 5563 — exactly the free-list/linked-list pointer-chase
  pattern that has been the root cause of several OTHER guards elsewhere in
  this codebase, e.g. s123/s131's `SCENE_NODE_LIST_GUARD` family, s133's

**What this rules out**: the `getTextureLUTFieldAt8`-inlining hypothesis
(architecturally impossible per Step 2); a source-level zero-extension bypass
anywhere in `renderUnlitMeshFaces`'s own body (re-confirmed, now twice,

priority per the boring-first-explanations rule until (a) and a proper

proving it ran. **This is a real gap the design should have caught up front**

inconclusive null result, per the "a null result is worthless without a
positive control" rule. Cheap fix: edited `fixup_game_funcs.py`, deleted only
`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c`, regenerated just that file, re-ran fixup (patch
report confirmed the OTHER 44 files were untouched — re-running fixup safely
no-ops on already-patched files whose bare-code regex no longer matches;
spot-checked `funcs_0.c` for duplicate `PATCH:` markers, found none),
rebuilt clean.

**Step 4 — third soak (`unlitmeshtracer3`) caught a live occurrence.**
Positive control fired at call #1 (proves the instrument executed on the
very call that later crashed). **Zero OOB fired at any of the 4 traced
sites.** The process then SIGBUS'd (signal 10) with `si_addr=far=0x380630062`,
which `[CRASH][pc-symbol]` resolved directly to `renderUnlitMeshFaces+792`
(backtrace: `renderUnlitMeshFaces+640 (lr, i.e. the getTextureLUTFieldAt8
call's return point) ← processSceneNode+10408 ← traverseSceneGraphRecursive
← setupCameraMatrices`). Register dump: `x8=0x0000000300000000` (rdram host
base), `x9=0x0000000080630062` (the zero-extended, NOT sign-extended, KSEG0
guest pointer — upper 32 bits are `0x00000000`, should be `0xFFFFFFFF`).

**The cross-reference that makes this session's result matter more than one
more data point**: `far=0x380630062` is not merely "a KSEG0-shaped crash" —
it is the EXACT SAME 64-bit value as s194's original `mcontext1` occurrence.
Grepped `si_addr=0x380630062\|far=0x380630062` across every soak log in
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/*/run.log` and found it FOUR times: `mcontext1`
(s194, first documented), `videoframetickguard3` (an earlier, undocumented-at-
the-time occurrence, no pc-symbol available then), `pcsymbolize1` (s206,
resolved to `renderUnlitMeshFaces+508`), and this session's `unlitmeshtracer3`
(resolved to `renderUnlitMeshFaces+792`). **This recurring bug is not random
heap/pointer garbage** — the identical byte value `0x80630062` reappearing
across independent runs, independent inputs (different stick-schedule timings
across sessions), and now two DIFFERENT instruction offsets within the same
function, is far more consistent with a specific, deterministic data source
(a fixed asset field, a specific global, or a specific struct offset that
always holds this address) than with heap corruption or a timing race. s194's
"not yet confirmed recurring" is SUPERSEDED — this is confirmed recurring,
4 occurrences, single value.

**What this rules out**: explanation (a) in its NAIVE form — "the SOURCE
register at one of the 4 highest-probability sites is already a bad address
before the dereference" — for whichever of the 4 sites executed before the
crash point this run. Given `lr=+640` sits at the `getTextureLUTFieldAt8`
call's return (source-confirmed at `funcs_4.c:5104`, well after site B's load
at line 5029), site A and site B's checks both necessarily ran and reported
IN_BOUNDS before the crash — i.e., `ctx->r20` (site A/B's source register)
was a valid pointer, and the BYTE READ from `ctx->r20+0x20` (which becomes
`ctx->r16`, site B's result) was itself readable/in-bounds at the time of
that specific load.

**What this does NOT resolve, and sharpens instead of closes**: `ctx->r16`
(loaded at site B) is dereferenced roughly 35 more times between line 5029
and the loop-back reload at 5546 (grepped: lines 5057, 5069, 5114, 5117,
5129, 5141, 5157, 5167, 5177, 5187, 5189, 5191, 5195, 5347-5542) — my 4 sites
only checked the LOAD's source address, never the LOADED VALUE (`ctx->r16`
itself) before its first subsequent use as a base pointer. Per C's implicit
`int32_t -> uint64_t` promotion (verified correct architecturally many times
over s200-207), assigning `ctx->r16 = MEM_W(...)` should ALWAYS sign-extend a
raw 32-bit RDRAM value like `0x80630062` into the correct KSEG0 form
`0xFFFFFFFF80630062` — meaning if `ctx->r16` really held the naive
zero-extended `0x0000000080630062` at the time of the crash, that value did
NOT arrive via the normal `MEM_W`-assignment path this codebase already
audited clean. Two live sub-hypotheses now, neither yet distinguished: (a1)
some OTHER register (not `ctx->r16`) is the actual zero-extended one at the
fault site (ARM64 register `x9` in this dump does not have a confirmed
`ctx->rN` mapping without disassembly, which stays blocked); (a2) the
recurring EXACT value `0x80630062` points at a specific fixed data source
(worth grepping decomp symbol tables / asset headers for this literal
address) rather than a generic "corrupted linked-list node."

**Next work unit** (see rewritten NEXT.md): two candidate probes, pick
whichever is cheaper to falsify first — (1) grep the ELF/symbol tables and

address) immediately after the site-B load and before its first subsequent
dereference (line 5057), which would catch the corruption at its true origin
point regardless of which of the ~35 later derefs actually faults.

`heapWalker+1128` crash whose register shape proves a generalizable,
project-wide blind spot in every `U32(ctx->rN)`-truncated guard, not a
heapWalker-specific miss

`run_unlitmeshtracer8.sh`, changed only `STICK_SCHEDULE` to drop the early

(`ROGUESQ_LOG_UNLIT_MESH_TRACER=1`, `PROBE_MODE=start_only`, `HOLD_S=300`,
`CAPTURE_TICK_S=0.2`, `HOLD_TICK_S=1`) byte-identical to unlitmeshtracer7.

**Result**: the run reached `SELECT YOUR CRAFT stable` normally (phase width
1024 at 46.4s, same as prior soaks) but the game process died at
`hold-iter 1` — almost immediately after the hold window opened, far
earlier than s210's crash (6s into hold) or s211's stall (near the run's
natural 300s end). `unlit-mesh-tracer`/`B_LOADED`: 0 lines again — the
original s208 `ctx->r16` question is STILL unanswered, now 0/5 soaks across
4 sessions (s209/s210/s211/s213) and 3 different varied recipes.

**Crash detail** (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/unlitmeshtracer8/run.log:141317-
141353`): signal 10 (Bus error), `si_addr=far=0x380003827`,
`decisionN=7988 lastFireDecisionN=7969 decisionsSinceFire=19 stalledNow=0`
(not stall-related — genuine crash during active operation). Register dump:
`x10=0x0000000080003827`, `x11=x12=x13=0x0000000080000000`, all other
general-purpose registers either small stack/heap pointers or zero.

**Finding 1 — live confirmation of the s157/s172 inlining theory.**
`[CRASH][pc-symbol]` (dladdr-based, trusted per NEXT.md environment notes)
names `heapWalker+1128`. `backtrace_symbols_fd`'s own stack dump names the
*same* frame `frameStartReset+532` (duplicated at frames 3 and 4). s157/s172
theorized from a source read alone (never proven with a live crash) that
`frameStartReset`-attributed crashes are actually inside its first,
unconditional callee `heapWalker`, misattributed by imprecise
symbolication — this crash is the first LIVE data point where both
symbolication paths disagree on the exact same frame and the more precise
one (dladdr) names heapWalker. Confirms the theory; not itself new
evidence about heapWalker's specific fault mechanism.

**Finding 2 — the crash's register shape exposes a project-wide guard
design gap, source-confirmed via `recomp.h`.** heapWalker already carries
10 guard sites since s172 (5 head-deref `GUARD` on `ctx->r4`, 5 walk-loop
`GUARD3` on `ctx->r3`), each written as `if (U32(ctx->rN) < 0x80000000u ||
U32(ctx->rN) >= 0x80800000u) goto <skip>;`. Neither guard fired this run.
Dispatched a research agent to read `recomp.h` (`N64Recomp/include/
recomp.h`, identical copy in this repo's `lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/
include/recomp.h`) for the exact macro bodies:
- `U32(val)` = `(uint32_t)(val)` — plain truncation to the low 32 bits.
- `gpr` = `uint64_t` (`ctx->r4` etc. are 64-bit fields).
- `MEM_W(offset, reg)` = `*(int32_t*)(rdram + ((reg) + (offset) -
  0xFFFFFFFF80000000))` — uses the FULL 64-bit `reg`, no truncation.

Cross-referenced against the s99 lesson already in this doc (and
CURRENT-TRUTH ~line 343): a *correctly* sign-extended KSEG0 pointer has
upper 32 bits `0xFFFFFFFF` (that's why s99's guard, written to compare the
raw 64-bit `gpr` against a 32-bit literal, false-positived on 100% of calls
before being fixed to truncate through `U32()` first). This run's crashing
register (`x10=0x0000000080003827`) has upper bits `0x00000000`, not
`0xFFFFFFFF` — the same "KSEG0-zero-extension" shape already named for item
-49's `renderUnlitMeshFaces`/`0x80630062` bug and s210's
`evalCubicSplineAtTime`/`0x7ffffff8` bug (3 distinct exact values, so still
NOT one shared deterministic constant — but a 3rd independent function now
hit by the qualitatively identical corruption mechanism).

**The mechanism, stated precisely**: `U32()` discards the upper 32 bits
before the bounds check runs, but a legit sign-extended pointer
(upper=`0xFFFFFFFF`) and a corrupt zero-extended one (upper=`0x00000000`)
have IDENTICAL low-32-bit representations. Any guard using this exact
`U32(ctx->rN) < 0x80000000u || >= 0x80800000u` template is structurally
unable to tell them apart — not a coverage gap (missing site), a design
gap in the check itself. This template is used project-wide, not just in
heapWalker (same pattern at CURRENT-TRUTH doc lines ~3109/3402/3434/3622/
3777).

**Not yet done this session** (would require its own build+soak cycle,
against "one work unit" discipline): actually adding an upper-bits check
(`(ctx->rN >> 32) != 0xFFFFFFFFu`) to heapWalker's 10 existing sites and
soaking to see if the strengthened guard fires live for the first time.
That's the next work unit — see NEXT.md.

**Ruled out this session**: heapWalker's own existing GUARD/GUARD3 protecting
this run's crash site was not itself investigated for which of the 10 sites
is nearest pc+1128 — no disassembly tool is available (blocked, re-confirmed
prior sessions) to map the offset to a specific site, so it's unknown
whether this crash hit an already-guarded-but-blind site or a still-
uncovered 11th call. Irrelevant to the fix: the upper-bits check needs
adding to all 10 regardless.

## Session 215 (2026-07-28) — source-read reclassifies s214's do_send SIGBUS as
NOT the s176+ scheduler-UAF family; landed and soaked a new mesgqueue guard;
soak died to yet another unrelated pre-existing crash before the guard could
be exercised against the target, extending the "random unrelated crash wins
the race" pattern to a 6th consecutive session and surfacing a much higher-
value lead for next session

### Work unit: Option A from NEXT.md (chase the do_send SIGBUS)

Per NEXT.md's decision gate ("prefer A only if the source read in step 2
confirms same-mechanism quickly, within ~15 min"), read
`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/mesgqueue.cpp`'s `do_send`/`do_recv`
and cross-referenced against the s176-184 thread-context-UAF mechanism
(`threads.cpp`'s `resume_thread_tagged`/`run_next_thread_and_wait`/
`wait_for_resumed`).

**Finding: the do_send SIGBUS is almost certainly NOT the s176+
scheduler-UAF family — it's a structurally different, more mundane bug.**
This build has no LTO (`grep -rn "INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION\|LTO"` on both
CMakeLists.txt files: 0 hits) and is `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` (confirmed via
`build/CMakeCache.txt`), so there is effectively no cross-translation-unit
inlining. `do_send` (mesgqueue.cpp) and `run_next_thread_and_wait`/
`wait_for_resumed`/`resume_thread_tagged` (threads.cpp) are separate TUs with
real out-of-line calls between them — a fault instruction inside any of the
threads.cpp functions would dladdr-symbolicate to THAT function's own symbol,
not to `do_send+388`. Since the crash's `[CRASH][pc-symbol]` line resolved
directly to `_Z7do_sendPhiibb+388` (established s213 as more precise than
`backtrace_symbols_fd`), the faulting instruction is almost certainly literal
code inside `do_send`'s own compiled body, not a callee.

The only unguarded native dereferences directly in `do_send`'s body are the
`TO_PTR(OSMesgQueue, mq_)` computation and the two
`TO_PTR(OSMesg, mq->msg)[...]` writes. `TO_PTR` (`ultra64.h:42`,
`#if 0`-gated native-compile branch confirmed dead, so the active branch is
always `((type*)(&rdram[(uint64_t)var - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000]))`) does
zero-bounds-checked pointer arithmetic on a raw 32-bit guest value — if `mq_`
(the guest `OSMesgQueue*` argument) or `mq->msg` (a struct field read out of
that same queue) is corrupted, the very next field access SIGBUSes with a
wild native address. This is the **same generic "unguarded TO_PTR on a
corrupted guest pointer" pattern already fixed at ~15 other sites this
project** (heapWalker's 10 GUARD/GUARD3 sites, `activateAnimationKeyframe`,
`composeNpcOrientationMatrix`, `rs_malloc`/`rs_free` call sites, the s78/s182
framebuffer refuse gates) — not a new investigation thread, and not the
scheduler-UAF mechanism s214 hedged toward ("this looks like the crash
variant of that same corrupted-thread-context family" — that framing is
**superseded** by this session's structural read; see CURRENT-TRUTH).

Also checked: `PTR(x)` is `int32_t` in the active build config (not the
64-bit-register case heapWalker's guards handle) — `mq_`/`mq->msg` are
already-truncated 32-bit values by the time C++ sees them, so this is a
simpler single-range bounds check, not an "upper 32 bits" check.

### Fix landed

`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/mesgqueue.cpp`: added
`mesgqueue_guard_refuse(who, mq_)`, mirroring the s78
`FramebufferManager::get()` refuse-gate pattern — rejects (returns `false`
instead of dereferencing) any guest pointer outside `0x80000000`-`0x80800000`
(the same 8MB KSEG0/RDRAM bound used by every other guard site in this
project). Applied at the top of both `do_send` and `do_recv` (guarding
`mq_` before `TO_PTR(OSMesgQueue, mq_)`), and a second time on `mq->msg`
immediately before each `TO_PTR(OSMesg, mq->msg)` dereference in both
functions (4 call sites total) — `mq_` itself checked out doesn't guarantee
the struct's own `msg` field wasn't independently corrupted by the same
upstream heap-corruption family. Diagnostic: an always-on atomic counter
(`g_mesgqueue_guard_bad`) plus an `ROGUESQ_LOG_MESGQUEUE_GUARD`-gated
`fprintf` (always prints on the very first refusal regardless of the env var,
so a same-run positive control doesn't depend on remembering to set it).
Pure `lib/N64ModernRuntime` host C++, no guest regen needed. Built clean
(`cmake --build . -j8`, only pre-existing SDL2-version linker warnings).
Exported (`submodule-patches/export.sh`, refreshed
`submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch`, +100 lines) and committed this
session.

### Soak (`mesgqueueguard1`, copy of s214's `run_heapwalkerguard4.sh` env
block/`STICK_SCHEDULE`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_MESGQUEUE_GUARD=1` added)

Died at hold-iter 91 (~100s into the 300s hold) to signal 6 (abort):
`Assertion failed: (ctx->f2.fl == ctx->f2.fl), function mat3x3InverseInto,
file funcs_5.c, line 7582` — the project-wide `NAN_CHECK` safety assert
family (s83 `evalCubicSplineAtTime`, s214 soak 1 `sinfApprox`) firing at yet
**another** new call site. `[mesgqueue-guard]` fired **0** times,
`[heapwalker-guard]`/`[heapwalker-guard3]` (still armed, carried over from
s214's env block) fired **0** times, `[unlit-mesh-tracer]` **0** hits — the
process never reached the do_send/do_recv corruption window (if one even
exists on this run's random schedule) before dying to an unrelated crash.

**No direct positive control for "do_send/do_recv executed and passed the
guard cleanly N times" was instrumented** (the guard only logs on refusal,
not on every call) — a real gap, flagged for next session if this exact
question needs revisiting. Indirect evidence the guarded code path was live:
`[thr-resume] tag=run_next` fired part of 202,082 total `[thr-resume]`
events by the time of the crash, and `run_next_thread_and_wait` (which the
`tag=run_next` resumes trace back to) is reached **exclusively** through
`do_send`/`do_recv`'s blocking loops or `osStopThread`'s self-stop path —
so `do_send`/`do_recv` almost certainly ran many thousands of times this run
without the guard ever refusing, consistent with a genuine but rare
corruption event (s214 saw it exactly once) rather than dead/unreached code.

### Rules out / reframes

**Supersedes s214's "this looks like the crash variant of that [s176+
scheduler-UAF] family" framing** — this session's structural read (no LTO,
Debug build, dladdr resolves straight to `do_send`'s own symbol) makes it far
more likely the do_send SIGBUS is a plain corrupted-guest-pointer crash, the
same family as ~15 other already-guarded sites, not a new manifestation of
the multi-session scheduler stall investigation. Single-source (one
structural/source-level read, not cross-confirmed by a second independent
run) — flag as such if cited before a 2nd line of evidence lands (e.g. a
future soak where the guard actually fires with a wild `mq_`/`mq->msg`
value, or a future soak reaching the same SIGBUS with the guard still
silent, which would refute this session's read).

**Does not confirm or refute** whether the mesgqueue guard actually fixes
the target SIGBUS — the soak never got the opportunity. Neither confirmed
nor refuted, same "instrument armed but crash race lost to an unrelated bug"
outcome as s209/s210/s211/s214.

### The bigger pattern, and this session's real finding

This is the **6th consecutive session** (s209, s210, s211, s213, s214, s215)
where a soak of this general recipe family dies to a genuinely different,
previously-uncatalogued-at-that-call-site crash before reaching its intended
target — 3 of those 6 were `NAN_CHECK` assert firings alone (s83 lineage,
now at `evalCubicSplineAtTime`, `sinfApprox`, `mat3x3InverseInto` — 3
distinct call sites of the identical assert). Continuing to design ever-more-
targeted single-purpose guards one soak at a time, when a random *different*
pre-existing bug has better than even odds of winning the race first, is
hitting diminishing returns — each session characterizes and fixes one real
thing, but the overall "can we reach content past the craft-select hold"
question is not advancing at the same rate.

**High-value lead for next session, not yet acted on this session (too big a
decision to tack onto an already-substantial iteration):** `NAN_CHECK` is
defined in `N64Recomp/include/recomp.h:396-397` as `assert(val == val)`, and
the line immediately below it (`recomp.h:399`) is a **pre-existing, already-
written no-op alternative**: `//#define NAN_CHECK(val)` — commented out, not
something that needs to be authored from scratch. Toggling which of the two
definitions is active is a single-line edit in a header the game's generated
code (`funcs_*.c`) includes at compile time, not something baked into
generated code content — almost certainly a plain `cmake --build` recompile,
**not** a full `make_elf.py -> N64Recomp -> fixup_game_funcs.py` regen (not
yet verified this session — flagged as the first thing to check, not
assumed). If confirmed cheap, this could eliminate the entire recurring
`NAN_CHECK`-family crash class in one edit (it has now independently
blocked at least s83, s97-99 lineage, s214 soak 1, and this session), letting
soaks reach much further before dying to something else. Trade-off: it also
suppresses whatever genuine floating-point NaN bugs are actually occurring
at those call sites — acceptable if the goal is "reach further past
craft-select to test unrelated fixes," not acceptable if a NaN itself is the
thing under investigation. This needs its own session with a clear
before/after soak-depth comparison, not a rushed addition here.

**Full detail**: this entry. Code: `lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/mesgqueue.cpp`
(`mesgqueue_guard_refuse` + 4 call sites) — patch exported
(`submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch`) + committed this session. Soak
artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/mesgqueueguard1/` (run.log, screenshots),
driver script `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_mesgqueueguard1.sh`.

### Boring-thing-first check (step 1 of NEXT.md's plan) found a real gap

Before touching anything, verified which `recomp.h` the build actually
compiles against, per rule 5. **NEXT.md's premise was wrong**: it pointed at
`/Users/williambuckley/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` (the
separate sibling checkout) and reasoned edits there wouldn't need
`export.sh` because that checkout isn't under this repo's `lib/`. But
`CMakeLists.txt:96/157/268` (`target_include_directories`) only ever adds
`${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/include` — a **second,
nested copy of N64Recomp that lives inside the `lib/N64ModernRuntime`
submodule as its own nested submodule** (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/.gitmodules`
has `[submodule "N64Recomp"] path = N64Recomp`). `RECOMP_FUNCS_DIR`
(`CMakeLists.txt:64`, `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs`)
does pull generated `.c` files from the sibling checkout, but their
`#include` of `recomp.h` resolves through the include path to the **nested**
copy, not the sibling one. The two files were byte-identical
(`diff` = no output) before this session's edit, which is why nobody had
been burned by this yet — but the nested copy is the one that's live, and it
**is** under this repo's `lib/`, so the "any edit under lib/ needs
export.sh + commit" hard rule applies to it.

Checked coverage: `submodule-patches/export.sh`/`apply.sh` only handled
`lib/N64ModernRuntime`, `lib/rt64`, and rt64's two nested contrib submodules
— **zero coverage for `lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp`**. Any prior or
future edit to files under that nested submodule (recomp.h or otherwise)
would have been silently unprotected: invisible to `export.sh`, lost on any
reset of the parent submodule, no patch to restore it from. Fixed this
session: added a `N64Recomp-nested.patch` export/apply pair to both scripts
(`submodule-patches/export.sh`, `submodule-patches/apply.sh`). Also had to
add `--ignore-submodules=dirty` to the `N64ModernRuntime` diff line —
without it, a dirty nested `N64Recomp` leaks a spurious
`Subproject commit ...-dirty` pointer line into `N64ModernRuntime.patch`
that `git apply` can't consume (caught this live: `N64ModernRuntime.patch`
grew from 958 to 964 lines on first export, traced to exactly this, fixed
before it was committed).

This gap-fix is a durable, standalone improvement independent of the
NAN_CHECK experiment's outcome — kept regardless of what the soak showed.

## Session 218 (2026-07-28) — source-read `heapWalker` end to end per NEXT.md's
plan, found and fixed the ACTUAL gap GUARD3 left open (a second, unguarded
deref per loop iteration using the freshly-read pointer value), shipped

(reached hold-iter 28, far past s217's hold-iter 1) but died to a **third**
independent sighting of the exact literal corrupt value
`0x0000000300000000`, this time in a completely unrelated subsystem
(scene-graph rendering, not heap-walking) — upgrading last session's
"two-source" lead to a three-source one and pointing the investigation away
from per-site guarding entirely.

### Correcting NEXT.md's own line-range estimate

NEXT.md inherited an estimate that `heapWalker` was `funcs_3.c:99-7978`
(~7880 lines) and told this session to delegate the read to a subagent given
the size. Before delegating, checked it directly: `grep -n "^RECOMP_FUNC"
funcs_3.c` shows the *next* function (`countDisplayListChunks`) starts at
line 701 — `heapWalker` is actually **99-700, ~600 lines**. Small enough to
read directly in one `Read` call; no delegation needed. (The 7978 figure
seems to have been carried forward from an unrelated function's size at some
earlier session and never re-checked — exactly the kind of unverified
line-range NEXT.md's own instructions warned this session to confirm before
trusting.)

### Source read: the actual mechanism GUARD3 misses

Read the full function directly. All 5 per-mode-table sections share an
identical shape: load a table-sourced head pointer `a0`; if non-null,
dereference it once (`v0 = *a0`, the GUARD2/head-deref site, s157); if that
dereference is non-zero (list has 2+ entries), walk a loop:

```
v1 = a0;
LOOP:
    v1 = *v1;      // (A) GUARD3 (s172) validates the OLD v1 before this load
    v0 = *v1;      // (B) peek: dereferences the NEW v1 -- the value (A) JUST
                    //     read from heap/RDRAM memory, i.e. untrusted content
                    //     -- with ZERO validation
    if (v0 != 0) goto LOOP;
```
GUARD3 validates the pointer used to *produce* line (A)'s result, but never
validates the *value* that produces — and that value is immediately
re-dereferenced by line (B), one full iteration before GUARD3 would ever
re-check it (on the next loop-back, if the peek says "keep going"). This
structurally explains why the existing 10-site guard (`heapwalker-guard`/
`heapwalker-guard3`) has now stayed armed-and-silent (0/0) across **4
consecutive soaks** (s214 x2, s217, and every prior heapWalker-attributed
death) while the crash signature keeps recurring: GUARD3 was never
positioned to catch the deref that actually faults. Confirmed line (B)'s
`MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0)` call shape is byte-identical to line (A)'s, which
explains why both would produce the identical crash-address arithmetic
(`si_addr = corrupt_value + rdram_base`) when either one is the fault site.

Verified all 5 loops share this shape by direct read (not sampling one and
assuming): loop-back labels `L_80007A1C`/`L_80007A78`/`L_80007AD4`/
`L_80007B30`/`L_80007B8C` (matching `_heapwalker_guard3_sites` in
`fixup_game_funcs.py` exactly, confirming s172's list is complete for what it
guards), each followed immediately by the unguarded peek load at `+4`
(`0x80007A20`/`0x80007A7C`/`0x80007AD8`/`0x80007B34`/`0x80007B90`).

### Guard landed: heapWalker GUARD4 (5 sites)

Also had to work out a safe bail target, which is *not* simply "the loop's
own postloop-append label" (e.g. `L_80007A2C`) the way GUARD3's bail target
is — that label's code unconditionally **writes through** the walked-to
pointer (`MEM_W(0X0, ctx->r3) = ...`, linking the list's tail into another
structure) before falling into the next block, so jumping there with a still-
corrupt `v1` would just relocate the fault a few lines later. Read forward to
find the first label that only touches `a0` (`ctx->r4`, the table-sourced,
structurally-trusted head pointer) and not `v1` — that's consistently 0x14
bytes past the postloop-append label in all 5 cases (`L_80007A40`/
`L_80007A9C`/`L_80007AF8`/`L_80007B54`/`L_80007BB0`) — and used that as the
skip target instead. Same upper-32-bit-check template as GUARD3/`heaplistdeq`
guard (env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_HEAPWALKER_GUARD4`). Landed in
`fixup_game_funcs.py` (`N64Recomp` sibling checkout, not `lib/` — see
CURRENT-TRUTH's housekeeping note on this file's persistence, unchanged this
session).

Full regen (`make_elf.py` -> `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py`, run once ->
`cmake --build`): confirmed exactly 5 sites patched exactly once
(`grep -c "heapwalker-guard4" funcs_3.c` = 5, syntax-checked one site by
direct read). Build exit 0, only pre-existing warning classes (DDIV
sign-conversion, SDL2-version linker warnings).

### Soak (`heapwalkerguard4_1`, same s213-217 STICK_SCHEDULE/HOLD_S=300
recipe, all 6 diagnostics armed): heapWalker signature didn't recur, but a
new crash surfaced the same corrupt literal in a third, unrelated subsystem

`ROGUESQ_LOG_UNLIT_MESH_TRACER`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_HEAPWALKER_GUARD`,
`ROGUESQ_LOG_HEAPWALKER_GUARD3`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_HEAPWALKER_GUARD4`,

variance already established). All 6 armed guards/tracers fired **0 times**

all 0; `unlit-mesh-tracer`'s positive control fired once, confirming the
instrument itself works, but none of its labeled OOB-address sites fired).

Crash: signal 10 (SIGBUS), `[CRASH][pc-symbol] pc=... sym=renderUnlitMeshFaces
+792` (backtrace frame reads `+640` — the usual dladdr-vs-backtrace precision
gap, s213; dladdr is the trusted one). Backtrace:
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive` -> `processSceneNode` -> `renderUnlitMeshFaces`,
via `setupCameraMatrices` -> `static_5_800C9BF0` -> `menuOverlayInit` ->

first time this crash-literal has appeared outside the heap free-list-walk
family. Register dump: `x8=0x0000000300000000`, `x9=0x0000000080630062`,

`0x0000000300000000` upper-bits shape as s216's `heapFreeListDequeue` crash
and s217's `heapWalker`-attributed crash**, now in a third register slot
(`x8`, not `x0`/`x9` as before) at a third, structurally unrelated call site
never before covered by any guard or the existing `unlit-mesh-tracer`
instrument (which logs OOB `MEM_W` addresses at specific labeled sites in
this same function but didn't fire — this fault is at an untraced site
within it).

**Conclusion, three-source confirmed**: this is not a per-consumer bug that
per-site guarding will ever fully whack down — the identical corrupt 64-bit
literal (integer `3` in the upper 32 bits) has now surfaced in the heap
free-list-walker, the heap mode-table walker, and scene-graph mesh rendering,
three subsystems with no structural relationship to each other except that
they all eventually dereference *some* pointer-sized value. This is strong
evidence of a single shared corruption source (something writes this exact
bit pattern into a location many unrelated consumers later read), not
independent local bugs. **Recommended pivot for next session**: stop adding
consumer-side guards one call site at a time and instead hunt for the WRITE

literal `0x0000000300000000`" premise: that value is not corrupted data, it
is this process's constant native RDRAM host base pointer, already named as
such by s194 and never connected back to by s216-218; one of the "three
independent sightings" (s218's `renderUnlitMeshFaces` crash) is actually the
4th recurrence of a bug s194/s199 already diagnosed and precisely localized
20+ sessions ago and simply never fixed. Sourced-read that exact function,
found and shipped a guard for the one unguarded "peek-load on a freshly-read
list-walk pointer" site in it (same idiom as heapWalker GUARD4/
heapFreeListDequeue's guard), regenerated clean, and soaked to a **first**:
the full 300s hold window completed with **zero crashes** — but the new
guard's positive control (the pre-existing `unlit-mesh-tracer` call counter)
fired **zero times**, meaning `renderUnlitMeshFaces` was never even called

fix, not a confirmation.

### Step 1 (NEXT.md): tabulating the three sightings turned up a fact NEXT.md's
own authors didn't have

Before writing any new instrumentation, did NEXT.md's own prescribed Step 1
(`grep -n "0x0000000300000000" PORTING-STATE.md`, build a table of session /
register / low-32-bits). The grep surfaced hits going back further than
s216-218 — to **s194** (`PORTING-STATE.md:17930-17968`) and **s199**
(`:19144-19211`), sessions the s216-218 lineage never cited. Reading those in
full changes the picture completely:

- **s194** (crash log still on disk,
  `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/mcontext1/run.log:4468133-4468166`): first-ever
  register-level crash dump, decomposed `si_addr` directly as `x0/x8
  (0x0000000300000000) + x9 (0x0000000080630062)` and stated explicitly:
  "`x0 =0x0000000300000000 (== x8; almost certainly the rdram host base
  pointer)`". s194 then derived the actual mechanism from `recomp.h`'s real
  `MEM_W` macro (`rdram + ((reg+offset) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000)`, which only
  produces a valid ~8MB rdram offset because `ADD32` sign-extends a 32-bit
  guest value to `0xFFFFFFFF80xxxxxx` first): whatever computed this
  particular fault address added the RAW, zero-extended 32-bit guest pointer
  (`x9=0x80630062`, KSEG0 tag `0x8` intact, upper 32 bits zero, not
  `0xFFFFFFFF`) directly to the rdram host base with **no KSEG0 subtraction
  at all** — a different, unsafe code path from `MEM_W`. `lr` pointed at
  `processSceneNode+8772`, calling into an unresolved leaf.
- **s199** (log still on disk,
  `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/pcsymbolize1/run.log:4463555-4463585`): added a
  `dladdr`-on-raw-`pc` diagnostic (`[CRASH][pc-symbol]`, still permanent
  today) specifically to pin down that unresolved leaf, and got
  `sym=renderUnlitMeshFaces+508`, **byte-identical** `x9=0x0000000080630062`
  to s194 — confirmed same bug, 2nd occurrence, `decisionN` in the same
  9660-9800 band both times. CURRENT-TRUTH item -48 (superseded) and the s199
  entry both flag `renderUnlitMeshFaces+508` as "the single, precisely-scoped
  next work unit" — this was never picked up.
- **s216** (`heapFreeListDequeue`, raw dump: `si_addr=0x338d47580`,
  `x8=0x300000000` — the s216 writeup's transcribed `x9=0x0000000300000000`
  does not arithmetically reproduce its own stated `si_addr` and appears to
  be a copy-paste slip; the raw log for that specific run was not re-checked
  this session, budget permitting a future session should verify it
  directly).
- **s217** (`heapWalker`, raw dump re-pulled this session from
  `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/heaplistdeq1/run.log:140456-140491`, still on
  disk): `x0=x8=0x0000000300000000`, **`x9=0x0000000038d47580`** (not
  `0x80xxxxxx`-shaped — no KSEG0 tag), `si_addr=0x338d47580`, exactly `x0+x9`.
  This is a **different** low-32-bit value from s194/s199/s218's
  `0x80630062` and does not carry the KSEG0-tag shape at all — a separate
  bug from the renderUnlitMeshFaces one, not the same value recurring.
- **s218** (raw dump re-pulled this session from
  `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/heapwalkerguard4_1/run.log:169337-169370`, still
  on disk): `x8=0x0000000300000000`, **`x9=0x0000000080630062`**,
  `si_addr=0x380630062`, `sym=renderUnlitMeshFaces+792`. **Byte-identical
  `x9` to s194 and s199** — this is the SAME already-diagnosed bug's 4th
  recurrence (offset `+792` vs. `+508`, ~70 ARM64 instructions apart in a
  `-O0`/no-LTO build — plausibly two different call/loop iterations hitting
  the same faulting instruction, or a slightly different codegen offset from
  intervening unrelated patches over 20 sessions; not investigated further
  this session), not a new, independent "third sighting."

**Discriminating conclusion**: `x0`/`x8 = 0x0000000300000000` is a
**process-wide constant** (the host virtual address this build's mmap/malloc
happened to place the RDRAM buffer at — identical across every run for
months of sessions, which is itself consistent with a deterministic
allocator/ASLR-disabled layout, not evidence of a shared write). It appears
in every one of these dumps for the boring reason that `MEM_W` (and any
code imitating it) always adds rdram-base to compute a host address — of
course it's present whenever ANY memory access faults. **NEXT.md's premise
("hunt for the write site of this literal") has no target: there is no
write, and the "three-source-confirmed" framing in CURRENT-TRUTH item -59
conflates one already-solved bug (s194/s199/s218, 3 of the 4 same-value
sightings) with at least one structurally distinct one (s217, different low
bits, no KSEG0 tag) that happens to share the same uninteresting rdram-base
addend.** The real, per-site question was always "what corrupts/leaves
unmasked the OTHER operand (`x9`)" — precisely the question s216's and
s217's own source-reads already answered correctly for their own functions
(class A, upstream-corrupted-value propagation) without needing to invoke a
shared literal at all.

### Fix: renderUnlitMeshFaces list-walk peek-load guard

Read `renderUnlitMeshFaces` end to end
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:4963-5630`, ~668 lines, no delegation
needed) specifically hunting for the same "peek-load on a freshly-read,
unvalidated list-walk pointer" gap GUARD4 (s218) fixed in `heapWalker` and
the loop-back guard (s217) fixed in `heapFreeListDequeue`. Grepped every
`MEM_W(ctx->rN, ...)` in the function for one immediately re-reading the
same register at offset 0 right after an assignment to it (the exact GUARD4
shape) — found exactly **one** such site, at `0x80011CE0`:

```
L_80011CDC:
    ctx->r18 = MEM_W(ctx->r18, 0X0);   // 0x80011CDC: validated by the
                                        // loop's own beq/bne structure
    ctx->r2  = MEM_W(ctx->r18, 0X0);   // 0x80011CE0: peek-load on the BRAND
                                        // NEW r18 -- zero validation
    if (ctx->r2 != 0) goto L_80011CDC;
```

No other `MEM_W(ctx->rN, offset)` pair in this function repeats the same
register at the same offset back-to-back — unlike `heapWalker`'s 5 identical
copies, this function has only the one. (This function also has 3 *other*
pre-existing, unrelated single-deref list-walk-shaped loads already covered
by the s208/s209 `unlit-mesh-tracer` observer sites A-D — none of those is
the double-deref shape; confirmed by direct inspection, not assumed.)

Shipped a guard (`fixup_game_funcs.py`, mirroring the `heapwalker_guard4`
template exactly: upper-32-bit check `r18_hi != 0xFFFFFFFF` — a bare
`U32()` truncated compare would silently PASS this corruption shape, per
s213's documented trap). Bail target: force `ctx->r18 = 0` then `goto
L_80011CEC` — that label is this loop's own natural exit, and it already
contains the exact "list is empty" handling
(`if (ctx->r18 == 0) { ctx->r10 = 0 | 0xFFFF; goto L_800120A4; }`) the
function was compiled with; forcing `r18=0` makes that pre-existing branch
fire correctly with no new semantics invented, the same "reuse the
function's own degrade contract" approach every prior guard in this family
uses.

Regenerated in the mandated order (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`). Fixup report confirmed the new
patch matched **exactly once** (`funcs_4.c: renderUnlitMeshFaces list-walk
peek-load guard (0x80011CE0) patched x1`), alongside the pre-existing
`heapWalker`/tracer patches re-applying normally (no double-apply, single
fixup run). Build clean (only the pre-existing `DDIV` pointer-sign
deprecation warnings, nothing new).

`fixup_game_funcs.py` lives in the untracked sibling `N64Recomp` checkout
(known, flagged risk since s83 — not this session's problem to fix); the
edit is on disk but outside this repo's commit scope, same as every prior
session's edits there. No `lib/` files touched this session — nothing to
export.

## Session 221 (2026-07-28) — found and closed the actual gap behind s220's `emitAllocatedDLCommand` hold-iter-1 crash: a 15+-session-old guard mechanism (s133) that only covered 2 of the function's 3 identical unguarded copies, not a new bug

NEXT.md's planned unit: source-read `emitAllocatedDLCommand`
(`funcs_3.c:2622-3210`, confirmed via `grep -n "^RECOMP_FUNC"` — matches
s220's estimate exactly) end to end and guard whatever unguarded
peek-load idiom explains s220's hold-iter-1 crash there.

**The read found something better than a new guard: the function already
has a guard mechanism for exactly this idiom, and it has a documented gap.**
Session s133 (PORTING-STATE.md:11791+) found that `emitAllocatedDLCommand`
inlines the same `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry`-return-then-walk-to-tail-of-
chain idiom `submitSceneNodeRender` was guarded for (s123/s131), and shipped

`_emit_dl_guard2_sites`/`_emit_dl_guard3_sites` table mechanism in
`fixup_game_funcs.py`. s133's own comment says the idiom is inlined "TWICE"
(an `r4` copy, an `r5` copy) and lists exactly two site-tuples per table.

**That count is wrong.** The idiom is inlined **three** times: `r4` is
reused by two *separate* copies (`findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry` call sites at

(`0x800087D8`/`0x800087E4`, skip-label `L_80008814`) and the `r5` copy
(`0x800088DC`/`0x800088E8`, skip-label `L_80008918`) — but never the
**first** copy (`0x800086DC`/`0x800086E8`, skip-label `L_80008718`), which

(`emitAllocatedDLCommand <- submitSceneNodeRender <- processSceneNode <-
traverseSceneGraphRecursive x2 <- setupCameraMatrices <-
runHangarSelectionFrame <- runHangarMenuFromOverlay <- menuOverlayInit`,

carries s133's guard blocks verbatim.

**This also explains a 15+-session-standing mystery, not just s220's
crash**: `emit-dl-guard2`/`emit-dl-guard3` have fired **0/0 in every single

## Session 223 (2026-07-28) — refuted the mat3x3InverseInto/setupCameraMatrices determinant hypothesis with a well-controlled null (456k+ firings spanning the whole hold), but a same-schedule re-run of s222's exact soak reached mesh-heavy space combat AND the opening crawl for a 2nd-ever time, then froze on a flat ground-color fill (not "torn/striped") with the swap/present pipeline still demonstrably live — non-determinism now proven on byte-identical scripted input, not just suspected

NEXT.md's planned unit: source-read `setupCameraMatrices`/
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive`/`composeNpcOrientationMatrix` end to end for a
transform value that could go degenerate during the post-`SELECT YOUR
CRAFT` camera fly-out, then land ONE targeted diagnostic and re-soak.

**Source read** (delegated to an Explore sub-agent, then independently
verified by direct read, not taken on trust): `setupCameraMatrices`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:19142-21603`) conditionally computes
a 3x3 matrix inverse of the camera struct's own `+0x2C` submatrix
(`$s1+0x2C`, gated on a flag byte at `$s1+0x0`) at `funcs_4.c:21299-21322`,
immediately before calling `traverseSceneGraphRecursive` — i.e. its output
feeds straight into the corrupted-frame render path this whole lineage
(s150/s220/s221/s222) has been chasing. The callee,
`mat3x3InverseInto` (`funcs_5.c:7208-7208+`), computes the determinant via
cofactor expansion then `f10 = 1.0f / det` at guest `0x8001C7E4`
(`funcs_5.c:7326`) — a zero/degenerate determinant produces `+/-Inf` here.
Critically, `NAN_CHECK` (`recomp.h:396`, `assert(val == val)`) passes for
`Inf` (`Inf == Inf` is true) and only catches true `NaN`, and only checks
its own OPERAND, never a result — so an `Inf` here sails past every
downstream `NAN_CHECK` on its own value, and the three adjugate multiplies
that follow (`0x8001C7E8`/`0x8001C7F0`/`0x8001C7F8`) check their input
operands (`Inf` passes) but never re-check the PRODUCT. If any cofactor
term is exactly `0.0`, `Inf * 0.0 = NaN` would be produced and stored
straight into the output matrix with no assert ever tripping — a plausible
"silent NaN, no crash" mechanism matching the observed symptom (permanent
visual corruption, process never crashes) exactly. `composeNpcOrientation
Matrix` (`static_5_800AB1C8`) was read too (matching the s150 backtrace
name) but NOT chosen as the instrumentation target: it already carries 7
guards from s99-s158, all confirmed 0/0 across every soak despite its
entry diagnostic firing 508/508 in at least one prior run (CURRENT-TRUTH
item -9/-10) — re-treading that exact function would be budget-rule-8
territory (a 3rd+ attempt at an already-dead-ended lead), whereas
`mat3x3InverseInto` was untested by any prior session.

**Instrument landed**: `fixup_game_funcs.py` (sibling `N64Recomp` checkout,
untracked there per the s83 flag, not this repo's commit scope) gained a
new patch at `funcs_5.c`'s `0x8001C7E4` div site — entry counter (capped at
first 3 + every 2000th to bound log volume, since this is a generic 3x3-
inverse utility called from ~50 sites, ~1300×/s in practice) plus an
UNCAPPED abnormal-value log (`det==0.0f || isnan(inv_scale) ||
isinf(inv_scale)`) gated behind `ROGUESQ_LOG_MAT3INV=1`. Full regen done
clean-room per the s221-proven recipe (not incremental) to avoid any
repeat-invocation risk: deleted all 45 `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c`,
`python3 tools/make_elf.py` (rogue_squadron64 checkout), `./build/N64Recomp
rogue_squadron.toml` (fresh regen), `fixup_game_funcs.py` run **exactly
once** (report captured to `scratch/agent/s223_fixup.log`, confirms
`funcs_5.c: mat3x3InverseInto det/inverse diagnostic (0x8001C7E4) patched

/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer cmake --build . -j8` — clean,
0 errors, only the pre-existing 46 warnings.

**Soak 1** (`mat3inv1`, `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_mat3inv1.sh`,

`[phase]` log lines corroborate real progression, not just cosmetic
similarity: `vi_width` 1024 (44.5s, SELECT YOUR CRAFT) -> 512 (73.2s,
`origin=0x006AB400`, matches s154's own "reached the hangar/departure"
address) -> 640 (**140.6s, `origin=0x006A2900`, the exact address and

CURRENT-TRUTH item -6, "the furthest the process has ever rendered
past the crawl"**) -> 512 (169.9s, `origin=0x00690400`, a phase never
previously reached in this specific lineage). **This is only the 2nd time
in the whole project's history this exact crawl-scene milestone has been
reached**, and the first time via this s150-s222 investigation's own
soak recipe. It directly contradicts s222's own framing ("no soak has
ever reached mesh-heavy content", CURRENT-TRUTH item -63) as a universal
statement: the identical schedule, run twice, produced a total dead-hangar-
freeze once (s222) and a run past the opening crawl the very next time
(this session) — **non-determinism is now demonstrated on byte-identical

**The freeze mechanism is also narrowed, not just relocated**: at the very
end of `mat3inv2`'s run, `[vi-fs-decision]` reports `#31683 FIRE
reason=swap ... stalled=0 ... rdpFs=3481` — the swap/present pipeline is
demonstrably still alive and actively incrementing `rdpFs` at the moment
the screenshot content has been frozen for ~275s. This rules out a
render-pipeline/present stall (the `[vi-fs-decision]` stall class this
project has separately tracked since s180) as the cause of THIS freeze —
the renderer keeps presenting, it is simply presenting the identical scene
every time, meaning whatever supplies the camera pose / scene-graph
content per frame has stopped changing while the rest of the engine
keeps ticking. Combined with this session's own mat3inv null, the
remaining candidate is a game-logic/state-machine freeze (the top-level
scene/camera-update driver stops advancing) rather than either a
transform-math corruption (refuted this session) or a presentation stall
(refuted this session). The frozen frame's flat-color-fill signature (not

consistent with a camera stuck pointed at a plain, distant, undetailed
ground/skybox plane rather than at a NaN-mangled mesh; not yet proven
which of "same mechanism, different endpoint" vs. "different mechanism
entirely" is correct.

**Fix status**: no fix landed — this session narrows the mechanism, it

## Session 224 (2026-07-28) — the camera's own raw pose field keeps changing for ~60s AFTER the picture (and RDP full-sync counter) already froze, directly answering NEXT.md's discriminating question: this is a downstream scene-graph/render-submission freeze, NOT a stuck camera

Per NEXT.md Step 1/2: `setupCameraMatrices` (`funcs_4.c:19142-21603`) never
reads a separate XYZ translation field from the camera struct passed in
`$s1`/`ctx->r17` — offsets `0x10/0x14/0x18/0x1C` are an integer viewport
rect, `0x20/0x24/0x28` are perspective near/scale scalars, and the only
orientation data in the struct is the `+0x2C` 3x3 submatrix that
`mat3x3InverseInto` conditionally inverts (s223's now-closed lead). World
position/view concatenation happens through a separate fixed-address global
matrix (`0x8012xxxx - 0x23A4`), not through this struct. So the field
chosen — the camera's own field, not a derived product, per NEXT.md's
constraint — is `m[0][0]` of that raw `+0x2C` submatrix, read directly
BEFORE any inversion, logged (`ROGUESQ_LOG_CAMPOSE`, `fixup_game_funcs.py`
funcs_4.c, guest `0x800178A8`) alongside the struct's own gating flag
(`+0x0`) and the struct pointer itself (to catch camera-instance swaps),
every 60th call, uncapped on NaN/Inf. Clean delete-all-funcs regen (not
incremental, same proven recipe as s221/s223), built clean (0 errors).

**Soak** (`campose1`, same `schedulepush2`-derived schedule as
s222/s223's `mat3inv2`, `HOLD_S=350`, synchronous foreground): survived
the full 350s hold crash-free. `[campose-entry]` fired 966/966 times, real
positive control (`camptr` visits at least 5 distinct camera-struct
addresses over the run's early menu/craft-select phase before settling on
one address for the whole flight portion), 0 abnormal (NaN/Inf) — a 2nd,
independent confirmation that this struct field is never corrupted
(complements, does not duplicate, `mat3inv-entry`'s 385/0-abnormal 2nd
confirmation of s223's already-closed determinant null in the same run).

**MD5-checksummed all 350 `hold_NN.png`** (`scratch/agent/checksum_campose1.py`):
this run's picture changes through `hold_82`, then is byte-identical
`hold_82`...`hold_350` — a real-content freeze (checksums 1/12-40/70-76/81/82
all distinct, matching the pattern of genuine motion, not an immediate
dead-hangar hang). Cross-checked against this same run's own `[phase]` log:
the LAST `vi_width` transition in the entire 420s-wall run is at process
time **170.6s** (line 176881, `vi_width=512 origin=0x00690400`) — no further
VI-resolution changes for the remaining ~250s, consistent with the
checksum-observed freeze. `[vi-fs-decision]` at the very end of the run
still shows `stalled=0, reason=swap` with the VI buffer address actively
alternating (`0x690000`/`0x620000`) but `rdpFs` plateaued at **3965** — a
2nd independent soak reconfirming s223's finding that the swap/present
pipeline stays alive through the freeze (ruling out a present-pipeline
stall) while RDP task submission itself has stopped.

**The discriminating result**: correlating `[campose-entry]`'s own line
numbers against this same freeze window shows the camera struct pointer
settles onto its final value (`0x80138D20`, the flight camera) right around
`n=15000` (line 177777, essentially coincident with the 170.6s phase
transition and the checksum freeze onset) — but **`m00` keeps changing for
another ~5880 calls** after that (0.99 → 0.887 → 0.823 → 0.809, a brief
plateau ~0.808 for a few hundred calls, then 0.742 → 0.350 → 0.289 → 0.292 →
0.293 → 0.291), only freezing permanently at **`m00=-0.707199`** at
`n=20880` (line 229189) — roughly **60+ seconds of continued camera-pose
change after the on-screen picture and RDP submission had already gone
static**, before the camera itself also eventually wedges and holds
`-0.707199` for the remaining 36900 calls (~end of the 350s hold).

**This directly answers NEXT.md's Step-3 discriminating question**: the
camera does NOT stop at the same moment the picture does — it keeps being
computed for roughly a minute afterward — so per NEXT.md's own framing,
this is the **"camera keeps changing after freeze onset" outcome**: the
camera-matrix code itself is not the wedge; something downstream (scene-
graph population, node visibility/culling, or draw-command submission
itself — `processSceneNode`/`submitSceneNodeRender`/
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive`) stops producing new drawable content while
the camera (and whatever drives it) keeps running for a while longer. The
camera's own later freeze (`n=20880`) is a secondary event, not yet
explained — plausibly it depends on state that the render freeze already
broke (an animation/timer tied to visible progress), or is an unrelated 2nd
wedge; not investigated this session.

**Caveat (rule 4)**: the *picture*-freeze timing has 2 independent
corroborating signals within this one run (checksum + `[phase]`/
`[vi-fs-decision]` plateau) and is consistent with s222/s223's established
pattern across many runs — well-supported. The *specific new claim* here
("camera keeps moving ~60s past the render freeze") rests on ONE run of
this ONE new instrument — strong and internally clean (966/966 positive
control, 0 abnormal, a sharp and large 60s separation, not a marginal
effect), but not yet independently reproduced. Given the schedule's proven
non-determinism (s223), a repeat run may freeze at a different point or not
reach this same clean two-stage pattern; treat as strong first evidence,
not fully closed, but strong enough to redirect the investigation.

**Next step**: per NEXT.md's own pre-registered outcome mapping, shift to
`processSceneNode`/`submitSceneNodeRender`/`traverseSceneGraphRecursive`

lines, plausibly just the last couple of seconds before the driver's SIGKILL
rather than a genuine mid-run plateau. This overturns s224's framing that
"the RDP full-sync counter" itself had already frozen alongside the picture
in that session's run — in THIS run it kept climbing for nearly the whole
window while the picture stayed byte-identical. Combined with the
scene-traversal finding, the emerging picture is: camera pose keeps
changing (s224), scene traversal keeps running and keeps calling
`submitSceneNodeRender` (this session), and the RDP keeps completing
full-sync cycles (this session) — the entire pipeline, top to bottom, is
demonstrably ALIVE and cycling throughout the visible freeze. The bug is not
a stall anywhere in this chain; it is that the pipeline produces the exact
same pixel output on every cycle. That is consistent with s222's own
description of the frozen frame as "a degenerate-polygon frame" — a
plausible mechanism is that whatever data traverseSceneGraphRecursive walks
each pass (the two fixed root pointers noted above) is itself frozen
upstream of this chain (a game-logic/simulation update that stopped
advancing world/animation state, distinct from the camera-pose field s224
already showed keeps moving), so the render pipeline faithfully re-renders
the same stale scene every single frame.

**What this rules out**: a scene-graph-traversal-stops hypothesis (this

separate simulation-tick function that should be mutating the data behind

## Session 228 (2026-07-28) — overturns s226/s227's "`tools/:*`-specific" framing: `Bash(build/:*)` (a different rule) fails identically via a control test, narrowing the gate to a whole class of `Bash(<dir>/:*)` rules vs. working `Bash(<word>:*)` rules, with a concrete one-line-per-rule settings.json fix proposed for a human

*(Note: this session's header was missing in the original write-up — the
body below ran on directly after s227's closing paragraph with no `##`
break. Added retroactively s229 while appending this session's entry, no
content changed.)*

Per NEXT.md's Step 0 (written by s227), re-ran the control command
`tools/agent/stop_gate.sh --verify` first, before touching the actual
regen work. It failed identically to s226/s227: "This command requires
approval." Per this project's own budget rule (iron rule 8, applied to

**New test**: `build/idontexist_permcheck_s228 --help` — a command
targeting the `Bash(build/:*)` allow rule (a DIFFERENT rule from
`tools/:*`) with a deliberately nonexistent binary, so a "command not
found" response would prove permission WAS granted (failure happening
after the permission layer, inside the shell), while "requires approval"
would prove the block happens AT the permission layer, before the shell
ever runs anything. Result: "This command requires approval" — same
failure mode as `tools/:*`, on an entirely different rule.

**This overturns the s226/s227 framing that the gate is specific to
`tools/:*`/`./tools/:*`.** It is not. Both `tools/:*` and `build/:*` fail
identically. Cross-referencing which rules in `.claude/settings.json` HAVE
been empirically confirmed working this session and prior sessions
(`grep`, `python3`, `pwd`, `git status`/`diff`/`log`/`show`, `git add`) —
every working rule is shaped `Bash(<bare-word>:*)` or
`Bash(<word> <word>:*)`, i.e. the ruled prefix is a complete command
token that is followed by a space in real invocations. Every failing rule
found so far is shaped `Bash(<dir>/:*)` — a bare directory name ending in
a slash, where real commands continue immediately with no space
(`tools/agent/stop_gate.sh`, not `tools/ agent/stop_gate.sh`).

**New hypothesis, sharper than s227's two candidates**: Claude Code's
`Bash(<prefix>:*)` syntax treats `:*` as "exact command-word, then any
argument after a space" rather than a raw string-prefix wildcard — so a
rule intended to match "anything starting with `tools/`" needs the
glob-only form `Bash(tools/*)` (no colon), not `Bash(tools/:*)`. This
would explain 100% of the observed pattern with a single mechanism, is a
known distinction in glob-permission systems, and predicts a specific,
cheap, testable fix. Written up in full in `scratch/agent/BLOCKED.md`,
including the exact settings.json edit to try (`tools/:*` -> `tools/*`,
`./tools/:*` -> `./tools/*`, `build/:*` -> `build/*`, `./build/:*` ->
`./build/*`) and a falsification path (test in an interactive session
first if a human wants to confirm before editing).

## Session 230 (2026-07-28) — found and instrumented a concrete render-cache "epoch" mechanism in `processSceneNode`; diagnostic confirms the epoch is a live, actively-changing value early in a run (not stuck), but two soak attempts with it armed both crashed near the SELECT-CRAFT→mission VI transition, before reaching the freeze window — a same-binary control (unmodified campose3, diagnostic compiled in but not env-enabled) ran clean 424s, isolating the crash to the diagnostic being ACTIVE, not to the new code's mere presence

**Read-only source trace (Probe A from s229's NEXT.md, no build) found a
concrete candidate mechanism.** Delegated a deep read of
`submitSceneNodeRender`/`processSceneNode` (`funcs_4.c`, ~4200 combined
lines of decompiled MIPS-to-C) to a subagent, then independently verified
every cited line myself before acting on it (all confirmed accurate):
`submitSceneNodeRender` reads a global word at fixed guest RDRAM address
`0x8011A894` near its top (`funcs_4.c:10-12`) and unconditionally stamps
it into `MEM_W(node_ptr+0x30)` every call (`funcs_4.c:41-42`).
`processSceneNode` has two near-identical cache-check blocks
(`funcs_4.c:13881-13890` and `:14732-14751`) comparing this same global
against a previously-stamped `+0x30` value — on match it falls through to
`L_80014FE8` and reuses a cached `+0x34` value feeding a render-queue
insert (the same queue the existing s152 diagnostic already confirmed
keeps growing); on mismatch it jumps to a recompute path
(`L_8001513C`/`L_80015404`).

**Important sub-finding: exhaustive grep across every `funcs_*.c` file
for a write to this exact address (the only valid MIPS lui/addiu
encoding, base `0x8012<<16` offset `-0x576C`) found exactly ONE writer**:
`buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial` (`funcs_4.c:22608-22636`), which sets
it to the hardcoded constant `1` conditionally — not an increment. No
per-frame increment site was found anywhere in the recompiled game code
via static search. This raised real uncertainty about whether the
mechanism was even a live "epoch" at all (vs. a one-time material-
registry-generation stamp) — resolved empirically below, not by more
static reading (would have been a 2nd+ full-function read pass on the
same question; chose to instrument and measure instead, per iron rule 8's
spirit and the project's own stated preference for discriminating
measurement over indefinite static analysis).

**Landed a diagnostic** (`fixup_game_funcs.py`, two new patch functions
`_render_cache_epoch_patch_a`/`_b`, both anchored on the existing
`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r16/r17, 0X30);` lines at the two call sites) gated
by a new env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_RENDER_CACHE_EPOCH=1`. Logs, per site: a
running call counter, the epoch value, the stamped comparison value, a
hit/miss flag, a heartbeat every 500 calls, and an unconditional log of
the first hit↔miss transition after a run of ≥50 consecutive same-result
calls (to cheaply capture change points without flooding output). Full
regen/build succeeded clean (`make_elf.py` → `regen_n64recomp.sh` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py` once → cmake build, all green, patch report
confirmed both sites patched x1).

**campose4 attempt 1** (new tag, copied from s229's `campose3` per
NEXT.md's own instructions, same schedule, `ROGUESQ_LOG_RENDER_CACHE_EPOCH=1`
added): diagnostic fired correctly and immediately answered part of the
question — the epoch value is genuinely LIVE during early gameplay,
climbing `0x24 → 0xE7 → 0x114 → 0x14A → 0x171 → 0x183` across the first
~1500 `processSceneNode` calls (roughly monotonic, not a stuck constant).
This rules out the most trivial reading of H2 ("constant the whole
run"). But the game process crashed at wall≈23s (`hold-iter 3`), a
Bus error at `pc=0x104c4c8ac`, symbol `static_5_800AB658+49104`
(`far=0x380000014`) — well before the previously-observed freeze windows
(`n=15360`+ in s223-s229). Preserved as
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/campose4_attempt1_crash/`.

**campose4 attempt 2** (2nd of 2 budgeted soak attempts, identical
script): crashed again, even earlier (wall≈21s, `hold-iter 1`), a
different Bus error at `pc=0x1009cfee4`, symbol
`tickTextureMaterialExpiry+612` (`far=0x38000ffb2`). Both crashes'
`[phase] vi_width=512 (was 1024)` transition line landed within 0.6s of
each other (73.9s vs 73.3s) — i.e., both crashes cluster tightly around
the SELECT-YOUR-CRAFT→mission-launch VI-width transition, not at a
random point. Different PC/symbol between the two attempts argues
against a single deterministic fault line in the new patch's own logic
(a genuine bug in one exact line would crash at the same PC every time);
both `far` addresses match the `0x38...`-prefixed garbage-pointer pattern

crash families (the same family the dozens of existing `GUARD`-suffixed
patches exist to catch). Preserved as
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/campose4_attempt2_crash/`.

**Control test (not one of the 2 budgeted soak attempts — a
discriminating check, iron rule 1's positive-control spirit applied to a

script verbatim (copied to a new tag `campose3control_s230` so as not to

the added I/O overhead perturbs frame timing enough to reproducibly (2/2)
nudge this specific, already-timing-sensitive scene-transition window
into a pre-existing crash-family bug that this exact schedule would
otherwise avoid or hit only rarely — not a new bug introduced by the
diagnostic's own logic. This is a hypothesis, not a proven mechanism;
flagged as such.

**Net result — the core H1/H2/H3 discriminating question (does the
epoch value go constant at/near the already-known picture-freeze point)
is UNANSWERED this session.** The crash pre-empted reaching that window
in both attempts. This is a null result on the main question WITH a
positive control satisfied (the instrument demonstrably fires and
produces real, changing data before the crash, and the control run proves
the binary itself is sound) — legitimate per iron rule 1, but incomplete.
Genuinely new information gained: (1) the epoch is confirmed live/
changing early in a run, ruling out the trivial "stuck from frame 1"
reading of H2; (2) this diagnostic's I/O overhead is load-bearing for

(`x_hash_table_remove_ptr`<-`CAMediaTimingInvalidate`<-`-[CALayer
dealloc]`<-`CA::Transaction::commit`). No build, no soak — per NEXT.md
and iron rule 8 (the `campose*` soak budget was spent as of s238).
Delegated the file reads to a general-purpose subagent to keep the
source dumps out of the main session's context; verified its key
file:line citations directly afterward (`plume_metal.cpp:2084-2109`,
`rt64_present_queue.cpp:110-120` and `840-860`) before writing them into

**Finding — one concrete, narrow, PLAUSIBLE-not-CONFIRMED candidate**:
`MetalSwapChain::resize()` (`plume_metal.cpp:2084-2101`) calls
`layer->setDrawableSize(drawableSize)` (line 2093) from inside
`PresentQueue::threadLoop()`, which runs on a dedicated background
thread (spawned as `new std::thread(&PresentQueue::threadLoop, this)`,
`rt64_present_queue.cpp:117`, thread named `"RT64 Present"`,
`rt64_present_queue.cpp:855`) — not the main thread, which is what owns
`Cocoa_PumpEvents`/`CA::Transaction::commit` in the crash's outer
frames. `CAMetalLayer` property setters like `setDrawableSize:`
participate in CoreAnimation's implicit-transaction/timing bookkeeping,
which Apple does not document as safe to mutate from a non-main thread
(unlike `nextDrawable`/drawable `present()`, which ARE documented
thread-safe). A race here is a plausible mechanism for exactly this
symptom: corruption introduced by the cross-thread mutation, but only
surfacing later — during a subsequent `-[CALayer dealloc]` inside
`CA::Transaction::commit` on the main thread — rather than crashing
immediately at the mutation site. That fits the observed frame-count-
delayed (not immediate) fault better than a direct double-release at the
resize call site would.

**Important gap, found by the same static read, that keeps this at
PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED**: there is no `SDL_SetWindowSize` or
window-recreation call anywhere in `src/main/` in this repo. The
VI_WIDTH register flip (1024->512, logged at `src/main/
rt64_render_context.cpp:814-838`) is a guest-side N64 framebuffer
register change, not a host OS window resize — no code path was found
in this repo that makes a VI_WIDTH change directly call into
`MetalSwapChain::resize()` or otherwise resize the host window/
`CAMetalLayer`. This means the tight correlation (crash at n=12420/
t≈131s, ~56s after the VI-width transition at t≈74.2s) could be
coincidental — both could be periodic, frame-count-driven events that
happen to land near each other across all 3 soaks — rather than causally
linked through this specific resize path. Do not upgrade this to
"confirmed" without closing that gap.

**Weaker/ruled-out leads from the same read**: `MetalSwapChain::layer`
(`plume_metal.h:238`) is a raw pointer, never retained or released in
this file (set once at `plume_metal.cpp:1998`; `~MetalSwapChain()` at
`2026-2027` is a no-op) — no direct double-release of the `CALayer`
object itself lives in this file. `MetalSwapChain::
currentAvailableDrawableIndex` (`plume_metal.h:244`) is read
non-atomically on the present thread (`acquireTexture`, `plume_metal.
cpp:2154-2155`) and written inside a GPU-completion-handler callback
that can run on yet another thread (`plume_metal.cpp:2056`) — a real
unsynchronized data race, but it affects drawable/texture refcounting,
not the `CALayer` object directly, so it's a weaker match to this
specific crash signature. No fixed-size pool/ring-buffer/counter
(`MAX_DRAWABLES = 3`, `plume_metal.cpp:89`) numerically lines up with
n=12420 or the ~56s delay.

## Session 243 (2026-07-28)

Ran the `mtldebug1` soak per s242's NEXT.md plan: same `campose*`/guard
set and `schedulepush2` schedule as `malloclog2`, `GAME_EXTRA_ENV="MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1"`
(Apple's Metal API validation layer) instead of malloc-scribble vars,
scoped to only the game process via the s241 `GAME_EXTRA_ENV` mechanism.

**Positive control passed**: `run.log` line 1 is
`Metal API Validation Enabled`, confirming the env var reached the
Metal runtime inside the game process (not silent like `malloclog2`'s
MSL/scribble vars were).

**Result: the soak found a NEW, distinct, much-earlier crash — NOT the
`n=12420`/`t≈131s` host-CALayer-teardown SIGSEGV family under
investigation.** `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER` triggered a fatal Metal validation
assertion at guest decision counter `n=4421` (vs. the family's
historical `n=12420`), well before the SELECT-CRAFT->mission transition
was even reached:

```
-[MTLDebugRenderCommandEncoder setViewports:count:]:3961: failed assertion `Viewport Validation
viewport.originX must not be infinite or NaN.
viewport.originY must not be infinite or NaN.
viewport.width must not be infinite or NaN.
viewport.height must not be infinite or NaN.
```

This aborts (`SIGABRT`, `pthread_kill`/`abort`), not the SIGSEGV pattern
of the s238-242 line of investigation. Stack: `MetalCommandList::
checkForUpdatesInGraphicsState` -> `MetalCommandList::drawInstanced` ->
`RT64::VIRenderer::render` -> `PresentQueue::threadPresent` ->
`PresentQueue::threadLoop`. The `run.log` frame immediately preceding
the crash shows `[pe gate #3183] ... viDiff=1 ... viW=0` — a transient
VI-width read of **zero** — right after an `osViSetMode #12` mode change
one line earlier (`width=512`).

**Static read confirms the exact mechanism (two independent lines of
evidence: dynamic trigger log + static code trace agree).**
`lib/rt64/src/render/rt64_vi_renderer.cpp`:
- `getViewportAndScissor()` (line 103) sets `sdSize = vi.fbSize()`
  (when `removeBlackBorders` is on, which it is here).
- `computeHDSize()` (line 17-19): `hdSize = sdSize * resolutionScale /
  downsamplingScale` — if `sdSize.x` (or `.y`) is 0, `hdSize`'s
  corresponding component is also 0.
- `fromSDtoHD()` (line 21-24): `relativeScale = hdSize / sdSize` — with
  both numerator and denominator 0, this is **0/0 = NaN**, which then
  multiplies into every viewport coordinate downstream, exactly
  matching the Metal validation error text.

So: a transient VI framebuffer width (or height) of 0 during a mode
switch produces a `0/0` NaN in `fromSDtoHD`'s scale factor, which
`MTL_DEBUG_LAYER` catches as a hard abort but which is presumably
silently tolerated (drawn as garbage or clipped) by Metal with
validation off — consistent with why this has never surfaced as a
`[CRASH]` in any prior (non-`MTL_DEBUG_LAYER`) soak despite `vi.fbSize()`
apparently hitting zero at least this once.

**This does NOT confirm or refute H1/H2/H3 for the original s238
host-CALayer investigation** — this is a different call stack, a
different signal (SIGABRT vs SIGSEGV), and fires at a different (much
earlier) guest decision count. It's an open question whether this
`fbSize()==0` transient is a NEW, previously-invisible bug that
`MTL_DEBUG_LAYER` merely exposes, or whether it's incidental/rare enough
to be unrelated to the CALayer crash family's `n=12420` convergence.
**Do not conflate the two families without further evidence.**

This is a single-source finding (one soak) for the trigger *condition*
(`viW=0` at gate #3183), but the causal *mechanism* (0/0 NaN in
`fromSDtoHD`) is confirmed by static code read independently of the
dynamic log — satisfies iron rule 4 for the mechanism, not yet for
"how often `fbSize()` hits zero in general."

This session did not modify `lib/rt64`/`lib/N64ModernRuntime` source
(read-only static trace); no `submodule-patches/export.sh` needed. A
fix (guard against zero `sdSize`/`hdSize` components in
`rt64_vi_renderer.cpp`) is proposed but NOT implemented this session,
per the standing "no speculative fix" rule — the next iteration's work
unit is to add the guard and re-soak with `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1` armed to
confirm the assertion stops firing.

scope (`fixup_game_funcs.py` untracked sibling-checkout state,

## Session 245 (2026-07-28)

**Work unit**: static trace of s244's new scissor-rect Metal SIGABRT
(`Set Scissor Rects Validation (rect.x(77)+rect.width(0))(77) must be <=
render pass width(6)`, `FramebufferRenderer::submitRasterScene`). No
`lib/` edit this session — static read only, per NEXT.md's discipline
(trace first, guard second, confirmed guard third, same as s243/s244).

**Mechanism found, H2+H3 CONFIRMED, H1 refuted-and-refined, from static
read alone (two converging code paths, no soak needed to discriminate)**:

1. **`render pass width(6)` is a genuinely tiny GPU texture, not a
   corrupted read of a bigger one** — it is created from
   `fbPair.colorImage.width` (`rt64_state.cpp:2128`,
   `drawParams.fbWidth = fbPair.colorImage.width`) which is the SAME
   value used to build the `RenderTargetKey` that creates/looks up the
   actual color target (`rt64_state.cpp:2052-2054`,
   `fbKey.colorTargetKey = RenderTargetKey(colorFb->addressStart,
   colorFb->width, ...); colorTarget = &renderTargetManager.get(...)`).
   So a real 6px-wide `RenderTarget` gets allocated — this is H2's
   "degenerate value", not H1's "wrong target's dimensions read by
   mistake".
2. **The only width-sanity guard on this path (`rt64_state.cpp:2015`,
   "s78") only rejects `width == 0` or `width > kMaxSaneFbWidth`
   (`=1280u`, `rt64_state.cpp:70`)** — a width of 6 is neither, so it
   sails through untouched. This is the SAME general class of bug
   already named and partially fixed in a DIFFERENT, unrelated consumer:
   `rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp:646-654`'s "s82" comment says
   verbatim *"refuse wild widths (1..257 garbage)"* and gates a
   `saneW` check against `{320, 512, 640, 1024}` — but that guard only
   protects the VI-presentation "last-drawn framebuffer" heuristic, not
   render-target creation or scissor validation. 6 falls squarely in
   the already-documented "1..257 garbage" range. This confirms H3:
   this is the SAME pre-existing wild-width phenomenon s82 already
   named, just reaching a second, previously-unguarded consumer now
   that s244's VI-NaN fix lets the game run long enough to get there.
3. **Why the scissor rect (`x=77`) overflows a 6px target**: traced
   `convertFixedRect()` (`rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp:60-91`, the
   function that builds `InstanceDrawCall.triangles.scissor` at line
   1964) and `FixedRect::left/right(true)`
   (`rt64_common.h:73-97`, implementation not re-read but the signature
   and call sites confirm these return raw RDP/N64-native pixel
   coordinates from the game's `SetScissor` command, e.g. up to ~320,
   independent of the destination `colorImage`'s declared width).
   `convertFixedRect()` only applies origin-recentering
   (`computeOrigin`, scaled by `fbWidth`) and misalignment correction —
   it does **not** scale or clip the raw coordinate against the actual
   destination target's pixel width. So when `fbWidth`/`colorImg.width`
   is a wild garbage value like 6, a `SetScissor` command whose
   coordinates were meant for the real ~320px-wide screen (`x=77`)
   passes through nearly unmodified, producing a scissor rect that
   grossly exceeds the actual 6px target — exactly the assertion Metal's
   debug layer caught. This mechanism generalizes: ANY wild-width target
   combined with a normal-screen-scale scissor command will hit this,
   not just this one instance.
4. **H1 (scissor computed against a DIFFERENT target's size than the one
   actually bound) is REFUTED as stated** — `drawParams.fbWidth` and the
   bound `colorTarget`'s actual width both trace back to the same
   `fbPair.colorImage.width`, so there is no cross-target coordinate-space
   mismatch. H1 is better restated as: there is no validation ANYWHERE
   on this path that clips/rejects a scissor rect against the actual
   bound target's dimensions — the existing empty-scissor skip
   (`rt64_framebuffer_renderer.cpp:736-757`, comment: *"Draw calls can
   sometimes end up with empty scissors and cause validation errors. We
   just skip them."*) already established that this general class of
   "bad scissor reaches the Metal encoder" problem is known and handled
   for the empty case, but not for the out-of-bounds case.

**Two proposed fixes for next iteration** (NOT implemented this
session, per "trace first" discipline):

- (a) Extend the s78 width guard at `rt64_state.cpp:2015` to reject the
  same "1..257 wild" range s82 already names (or require a minimum sane
  width), preventing the tiny garbage target from ever being created.
  Risk: unclear if 1..257 is EVER a legitimate width for some real
  small N64 framebuffer use case in this game — s82's guard was scoped
  to a narrow heuristic, not target creation, so widening its scope
  needs care.
- (b) Clip/skip scissor rects that exceed the destination target's
  actual bound width/height in `submitRasterScene`, mirroring the
  existing empty-scissor skip at line 736-757 (add an out-of-bounds
  check next to the `isEmpty()` check, using `fbStorage->colorTarget`'s
  actual `width`/`height`). This is more general — it catches this bug
  class regardless of WHY the target ended up tiny — and needs no
  change to framebuffer/target creation logic. **Preferred**: lower risk,
  same pattern already proven safe in this exact function.
