## Session 322 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: gate3's containing reachability guard is REAL control flow, not an s318-class diagnostic bug — closes hypothesis (b), leaving only the untractable "fully dynamic indirect call" as the surviving 14-call-gap explanation; pivots the hypothesis-id to the fresher, unexplored 37-vs-40 gap

Continued `HYPOTHESIS-ID: m5-audio-destub-step4-setdisplaymode-hang`. Item -180 (s321) left one
cheap, read-only check outstanding: whether gate3's persistent "0/40 reached, containing code path never
entered" measurement is itself unreliable the way gate1/2/3's `taken_skip` field was until s318 found it
read a stale re-fetch of shared memory instead of the register (`ctx->r2`) the real branch actually uses.
Pure source-read against the already-current `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_24.c` (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp`
checkout) — no build, no soak, no reversal.

**Method.** Read the full ~280-line span covering all three gates' setup, loop bodies, and every branch
target from `funcs_24.c:3519` (start of the enclosing loop nest) through `funcs_24.c:3927` (gate3's loop
continuation past its diagnostic block), tracing every `goto`/branch target by hand rather than just the
already-instrumented bodies s313-s321 had examined.

**Finding — the three gates are NOT three independent, symmetric checks; they form a cascade with
asymmetric bypass behavior:**

- **Gate1's entry guard** (`funcs_24.c:3524-3534`): `MEM_HU(-0x6678) < N` (N = a passed-in threshold,
  loaded into `s4`/`ctx->r20`). If false, jump directly to `L_800914E8` (gate2's setup) — normal
  cascade. If true, enter gate1's loop with `r19=0` (`s3`, a voice-index cursor shared by all three
  gates), `r16=MEM_HU(-0x6678)`, `r20=N` (unchanged for the rest of the function).
- **Gate1's loop, BOTH exit paths, go around gate2/gate3 entirely.** The outer per-iteration check
  (`L_80091444`, `funcs_24.c:3546-3560`: `r19 < MEM_HU(-0x68B2)`, a DIFFERENT address from the entry
  guard's) exits to `L_80091654` — the function's single shared FINAL label, past gate3's own loop — when
  false. The inner counter check (`after_11`, `funcs_24.c:3659-3668`: `r16 < r20(N)`) does the same.
  Every exit from gate1's loop, once entered, lands at the final label. **Structural consequence: any
  call where gate1's guard succeeds and its loop runs can never reach gate2 or gate3 in that same
  call, by direct jump — not by chance, by construction.**
- **Gate2's entry guard** (`L_800914E8`, `funcs_24.c:3677-3688`): rereads the SAME `-0x6678` address
  gate1's entry guard used, but against a fixed constant `0x10` instead of `N`. If false, converge at
  `L_800915A4` (gate3's setup region). If true, enter gate2's loop.
- **Gate2's loop, BOTH exit paths, flow onward toward gate3's setup** (`L_800915A0`/`L_800915A4`) —
  unlike gate1's, neither of gate2's exits (`L_80091504` top check on the same `-0x68B2` address vs.
  `r19`, or the inner `r16 < 0x10` check at `after_14`) targets the final label directly.
- **Gate3's setup** (`funcs_24.c:3821-3838`): reads `r20 & 0xFFFF` — i.e. `N`, the SAME register gate1's
  entry guard set up and NEVER rewritten since (confirmed: `grep -c "r20"` across the whole
  `funcs_24.c:3546`-`3822` span finds only 3 occurrences, all reads, zero writes). If `N==0`, skip
  gate3's loop entirely (final label). Otherwise enter gate3's loop, which has its own `r19 <
  MEM_HU(-0x68B2)` top check (same address/register gate1's inner check used, but `r19` was never reset
  since gate1's `r19=0` — it only carries the cumulative count of voices gate1+gate2's loops already
  processed).

**Verdict: no s318-class mismatch exists.** `ctx->r20` at gate3's guard is not a diagnostic proxy reading
stale shared memory — it *is* the literal register the real recompiled branch tests (this is generated
code executing the actual branch, not an instrument observing it from outside), and it is provably
unclobbered since gate1's setup. There is no register/memory divergence to find. Gate3's reachability is
governed by real game/voice-count state: **it is reachable ONLY when gate1's entry guard fails (so its
bypass-to-final-label never triggers) AND `N != 0` AND gate2's own `<0x10` guard succeeds AND the shared
voice cursor (`r19`, already advanced by up to 16 iterations from gate2's own loop) hasn't caught up to
`MEM_HU(-0x68B2)` by the time gate3's own top check runs.** That window is narrow but not empty — gate3's
observed 0/40-always across every soak since s313 is a real fact about the tested game state/scene, not a
measurement bug.

**This closes hypothesis (b) exactly as s321 closed hypothesis (a).** Both proposed explanations this
investigation could test via source-read for the 14-call gap (gate1+gate2's measured real-call rate,
23-24, vs. the tick-producer functions' own measured entry count, 37-38) are now exhausted. The only
surviving explanation — a fully dynamic indirect call resolved through a runtime-computed pointer chain,
among 28,388 `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->rN)` call sites — is explicitly not tractable by grep/read-only
methodology (per s321) and would need a different tool entirely (e.g. runtime call-site logging keyed on
the target function's address, not text search).

**Pivot.** Per NEXT.md's own pre-declared fallback and iron rule 8 (this closes the 16th consecutive
session on this exact hypothesis-id, all read/grep avenues now exhausted), this session identifies a
FRESHER, unexplored lead to pivot to instead of continuing to chase the untractable dynamic-call
explanation: item -174 (s315) already found and left open a DIFFERENT, smaller gap that this
investigation's -175..-180 branch never actually addressed — the 3 tick-producer functions
(`tickAllActiveSongs`/`tickAudioSequencerFrame`/`tickAllAudioChannels`) stop 3 calls short (37/37) of
the hard-freeze boundary shared by `update3DAudioFrame`, `M_AUDTASK` RSP-task submission (`[audtask-
dispatch]`, already widened and always-on in `src/main/main.cpp:581-636`, no `lib/` edit needed), and
the RSP task-runner's own last dispatch, all of which hit 40/40 together. That "37-vs-40" gap has had

## Session 325 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: CLOSES `m5-audio-destub-step4-tick37-vs-hardstop40` — the "37 vs 40" / 14-call gap was a 4th instance of the sampling-cap-illusion bug, not a measurement error or an unlocated call site

Executed NEXT.md's step 4 (the "if source-read doesn't find the discrepancy" build+soak), after steps
1-3's source-read found nothing: gate2/gate3's diagnostic placement matches gate1's structurally (all 3
inserted at the identical pre-decrement `ctx->r2` read point, same file, same convention — no s318-class
placement asymmetry), and none of the 3 call sites sit inside a loop that could invoke
`tickAllActiveSongs`/`tickAudioSequencerFrame` more than once per "taken" sample (each is a single direct
call, confirmed by reading `funcs_24.c` around all 3 sites).

**The experiment**: widened gate1/gate2/gate3's diagnostic print cap in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (N64Recomp
repo, untracked/uncommitted loose file — not a git-tracked dependency of this repo) from `n<40` to
`n<4096`, so every real invocation gets logged instead of only the first 40. Regenerated
(`N64Recomp`→`fixup_game_funcs.py`→`cmake`) with `setDisplayMode`'s gate-byte site narrowed to
C88-only-reversed (matching s317/s320/s323's exact soak condition, `audio gate patched x1` confirmed in
the fixup report), ran ONE soak (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_step325widecap.sh`,
`step325widecap/run.log`, phase-timeout INCONCLUSIVE at 600s as expected — this config reliably hangs
before title, not a run failure).

**Result** (uncapped, full-run counts): gate1 fired 71 times total (not 40 — the old cap was silently
truncating 31 real invocations), with `reg==1` (real call) on 33 of them. Gate2 fired 4 times, all 4
calls. Gate3 fired 0 times. **33+4+0 = 37, an EXACT match** to the tick-producer functions' own
independent entry-diagnostic count (`reach-allsongs-entry`/`tick-audio-seq`, both 37/37) in the SAME
run. Two independent, structurally unrelated measurement mechanisms (branch-register sampling at the 3
gate sites vs. unconditional entry counters inside the called functions themselves) now agree exactly —
satisfies the two-independent-lines-of-evidence bar directly.

**What this overturns**: every session from s312 through s324 treated gate1's diagnostic cap (`n<40`)
as if it captured gate1's FULL invocation count for a soak this short, because no run had ever printed a
line past `n=39` (the `n%128==0` fallback never fired since gate1 never reached `n=128`) — that silence
read as "gate1 only fires 40 times," not as "the cap is hiding everything past 40." The true count (71)
sits between the two round numbers (40, 128) that every prior session's own convention would have
sampled at, which is exactly why 8+ sessions of reg-based hand-analysis on the first-40-only window
(19/40 for gate1 in s318's log, later runs matching or close) never reached 37 — they were correct
arithmetic on incomplete data, not wrong arithmetic on complete data. This is the same "sampling cap
masquerading as a hard stop" bug class already found and fixed 3 times previously in this exact
investigation (s312/s313/s315, all in `M_AUDTASK`/tick-producer diagnostics, never previously in the
gate1/2/3 diagnostics themselves) — a 4th instance, in a 4th diagnostic, closes the loop on the whole
bug class within this call chain.

**Restored the default state before ending**: `setDisplayMode`'s gate-byte site regex renarrowed back
to the full `(?:B40|C88)` alternation (both force-zeroed, `audio gate patched x2` confirmed), regenerated
and rebuilt again so the repo sits in its normal buildable default. The widened `n<4096` sample cap on
gate1/2/3's diagnostics was left in place permanently (strictly more informative, same convention already
used elsewhere, no cost when the env var is unset).

task. `setDisplayMode`'s site still cannot be landed permanently — reversing it (even alone, gate byte

## Session 326 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: pure source-read fully traces the `setDisplayMode` VI=320 hang to a concrete mechanism — `runVideoFrameTick` calls `musyxNoopStub` first thing every frame, which spins forever in `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` on a countdown only a not-yet-reached `musyxSynthFrame` call can decrement

Ran NEXT.md's suggested first step exactly as written ("read `setDisplayMode`'s full body... this alone
may explain the VI=320 hang without needing a new instrumented soak — try it first") and it did. No
build, no soak, no code change this session — pure static read across
`/Users/williambuckley/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c`, `funcs_23.c`, `funcs_24.c`.

**What `setDisplayMode`/`reapplyDisplayMode` actually do, un-patched** (both are structurally identical
— read both in full, `funcs_23.c:9586-9804` and `9805-10023`): each **unconditionally zeroes the gate
byte (`0x800A0F50`) at entry** (an existing, un-patched store — `0x8008EA34`/`0x8008EB7C`), then calls a
chain of real audio-setup functions (`initAudioSubsystem`/`reapplyAudioConfig`, `resetSongSubsystemCounter`,
zeroes several buffers, `initSongSequencerPools`, `resetMusyXEngineState`, `clearStreamedVoiceFlags`,
`reset3DAudioLists`), and **only at the very end sets the gate byte back to 1** (`0x8008EB40`/`0x8008EC88`
— the two patched sites). So the patch's actual effect is narrow and precisely what its own comment says:
it's the *only* thing preventing these two functions from re-enabling the audio-engine-active flag after
doing real setup work. Reversing it doesn't change what runs *inside* these two functions at all — both
already run their full real body every time regardless of patch state — it only changes what every
*other* gate-byte reader sees afterward.

**The consumer chain that actually hangs, fully traced address-by-address**:
- `musyxNoopStub` (`funcs_23.c:10098`, guest `0x8008ED00`) reads the gate byte; if nonzero, calls
  `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` (`funcs_24.c:5425`, guest `0x80091EB0`).
- `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` seeds a 16-bit countdown at RAM `0x8014998A` (`0x8015<<16 - 0x6676`) to
  `0x10`, then busy-spins (`L_80091ED0`, `funcs_24.c:5448-5461`) `while (countdown != 0)`. The loop body
  is `lui`/`lhu`/`sll`/`bgtz`/`nop` only — **zero `jal`/yield instructions**, confirmed by reading every
  line of the loop. `shutdownAudioEngine` (`funcs_24.c:5143`, guest `0x80091D40`, called from
  `shutdownMusyXEngine` when gate≠0) has the byte-for-byte identical seed-then-spin pattern at
  `funcs_24.c:5166-5178` on the *same* countdown address.
- Exhaustively grepped this exact RAM offset (`0X6676`) across every `funcs_*.c` in the whole
  `RecompiledFuncs` tree: **3 total references, all in `funcs_24.c`** — the two seed-sites above, and
  exactly **one decrement site**, inside `musyxSynthFrame` (`funcs_23.c` — actually `funcs_24.c` around
  line 4020-4034, the same function containing the already-known `tickAllActiveSongs`/
  `tickAudioSequencerFrame` calls from the closed s325 hypothesis), which subtracts a DMA-batch count
  from the countdown right after a `jalr` to `submitDmaRequestBatch` (`funcs_1.c:6157`, guest
  `0x8000569C`, a real — not stubbed — low-level DMA-batch submission routine). No other write to this
  address exists anywhere in the recompiled game code; this is exhaustive, not sampled.
- **Call-site tracing closes the loop**: `setDisplayMode`'s only static caller is `funcs_0.c:486`
  (guest `0x80000D8C`), inside the function spanning `funcs_0.c:291-537` (boot-bootstrap code — calls
  `osStopThread`/`loadDebugAssets`/`osCreateMesgQueue`/`osRecvMesg`/`osInvalICache`/`initSiQueue`/
  `installPeriodicCallback` before reaching `setDisplayMode`; none of those touch `musyxSynthFrame` or
  the countdown). `musyxNoopStub`'s only static caller is `funcs_0.c:1488` (guest `0x80001388`), inside
  **`runVideoFrameTick`** (`funcs_0.c:1459`) — as literally the first real call in that function's body,
  right after its register-save prologue. `shutdownMusyXEngine` has **no callers at all** (dead code via
  direct `jal`; only reachable indirectly if ever).

**The mechanism, end to end**: with the gate-byte patch reversed, `setDisplayMode` returns with the byte
= 1. The very next time `runVideoFrameTick` — the per-VI-frame tick driver itself — runs, its first
action is `musyxNoopStub`, which now takes the "audio active" branch into `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`,
which seeds the countdown to 16 and spins with no yield instruction anywhere in its loop, waiting for a
`musyxSynthFrame` invocation (the only possible decrementer) that can never run *from inside this spin* —
and since `runVideoFrameTick` never returns, VI progression itself (whatever drives it) stalls exactly
where the run stops advancing. This isn't an indirect scheduler-adjacent side effect; **the per-frame VI
tick function is directly the one deadlocking**, which is why the process freezes at a fixed VI count
(320) rather than degrading or crashing.

**This is not a new bug** — it's exactly the risk `docs/M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md` §3 row 1 and §4 step 4
(lines 121, 199-201) already named as "the single highest-risk regression of this whole plan" and
predicted almost verbatim: *"needs a source-level fix in the ucode's task-completion signaling, not a
gate re-revert."* This session's contribution is turning that prediction into a fully address-level
mechanism trace (previously it was inherited only from the original patch-author's code comment,
un-reverified) — 15 sessions of reversal soaks (s303-325) hit this hang without anyone reading past the
gate-byte store itself to see what actually happens downstream.

**What remains open, concretely, for the next iteration**: the fix direction the plan already named —
make forward progress possible during the spin, e.g. by making `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`/
`shutdownAudioEngine`'s loop body explicitly pump/call the real M_AUDTASK dispatch (confirmed live and
crash-free by s300's step 2 soaks) inline every iteration instead of waiting on a countdown nothing
decrements from within the spin, then soak to see whether VI progresses past 320 to title (VI=1024)
with `setDisplayMode`'s site reversed. This is a source patch + soak, not further source-reading — the
mechanism question NEXT.md set out to answer is closed.

`HYPOTHESIS-ID` unchanged (`m5-audio-destub-step4-setdisplaymode-vi320-hang`, 1st of budgeted 3
iterations — this session was pure source-read as NEXT.md prescribed, no soak spent). No code changed
this session (read-only investigation); nothing under `lib/` touched, no `export.sh` needed.

**The fix**: per s326's mechanism trace (`waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`/`shutdownAudioEngine` busy-spin
on a halfword countdown at RAM `0x8014998A` that only `musyxSynthFrame`'s own tail can decrement, and
`musyxSynthFrame` is normally reached only via the VI-retrace callback table — a path the deadlocked
spin itself blocks from ever running), patched both spin loops in

call `musyxSynthFrame(rdram, ctx)` directly from inside the spin, bounded to 64 pumps, instead of
blocking on a producer they themselves prevent from running. Verified safe before writing the patch:
grepped `musyxSynthFrame`'s own body (3146-4224 in `funcs_24.c`) for any call, direct or indirect,
back into `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`/`shutdownAudioEngine` — none exists, so no recursion risk; and
confirmed the loop-exit code in both callers immediately reloads every register it uses fresh from
memory (`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(...)` etc.) before use, so clobbering caller-saved registers via the
`musyxSynthFrame` call is harmless. A free diagnostic (`[audio-wait-pump-stall]`) fires if 64 pumps
don't drain the countdown to 0 — the loop still falls through regardless (matching NEXT.md's
"pump ... falls through regardless of whether the countdown ever reaches 0" spec) rather than
re-deadlocking. `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_WAIT_NOPUMP=1` restores the pre-s327 blind-spin (deadlock) behavior

## Session 330 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: pure source-read finds a SECOND, unpatched spin loop inside `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` — a strong, address-level-verified candidate mechanism for the `reapplyDisplayMode` VI=640 stall, not yet runtime-confirmed

Exactly the NEXT.md-prescribed first step from s329: source-read `reapplyDisplayMode`'s call site and
body before any new soak (the s326 precedent — pure text tracing fully explained the `setDisplayMode`
hang without a build/run). Delegated the multi-file trace to a subagent, then personally spot-verified
every load-bearing citation byte-for-byte against the on-disk generated source before accepting it.

**Step 1 — the call-site guard.** `reapplyDisplayMode`'s call inside `runVideoFrameTick`
(`funcs_0.c:1752`) is gated by 3 ANDed conditions, all re-evaluated every frame: `advanceVideoFrame()`
returns nonzero (`funcs_0.c:1703-1706`), byte `0x8010D211` nonzero (`1713-1721`), and byte
`*(s2+4)` nonzero (`1725-1731`). `reapplyDisplayMode`'s own body (`funcs_23.c:9805-10097`) writes
neither gating location — it is **not self-clearing**, meaning once the guard trips true, nothing in
this function stops it firing again next frame. This directly explains why `reapplyDisplayMode`
diverges from `setDisplayMode` (a genuine one-shot boot call, per s326): `reapplyDisplayMode` can be
invoked repeatedly, once per frame, indefinitely — turning any single-invocation bug into a
recurring/compounding one.

**Step 2 — no graphics-task call inside `runVideoFrameTick` itself.** Grepped the full function body
(`funcs_0.c:1459-1913`) for `submit|Task|Dpc|Rsp|Dispatch|graphics|gfx` — zero matches. The real
graphics-task producer (`[vi-fs-decision]`) lives in native C++ (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp:2945`,
fed by `ultramodern::submit_rsp_task`'s `M_GFXTASK` branch, `ultramodern/src/events.cpp:576-582`),
consumed by a dedicated `gfx_thread` (`events.cpp:592`) — architecturally separate from the CPU/game
thread that runs `runVideoFrameTick`. The mechanism by which a game-thread hang starves this producer
isn't a direct call inside `runVideoFrameTick` — it's that the single CPU thread, once wedged inside
`runVideoFrameTick`, can never return to run whatever later per-frame code (outside this function)
would call `submit_rsp_task` again. Consistent with `[vi-fs-decision] stalled=1 pairs=0` holding
forever once the game thread hangs.

**Step 3-4 — `musyxNoopStub`/`waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`, and the NEW finding.**
`musyxNoopStub` (`funcs_23.c:10098-10171`) branches purely on gate byte `0x800A0F50`: if nonzero, it
calls `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` unconditionally (`10118`), then clears the gate byte back to 0
before returning (`10156-10159`) — so a triggered call self-clears the OUTER gate (meaning the "does
this hang" question resets every frame based on whether `reapplyDisplayMode` re-armed
`0x800A0F50` again that frame). Read `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`'s CURRENT on-disk body
(`funcs_24.c:5433-5648`, i.e. as regenerated with s327's pump-fix applied) end to end. The s327 pump
loop is present and correctly bounded (`funcs_24.c:5456-5477`, caps at 64 `musyxSynthFrame` pumps,
always falls through). **But the function has a SECOND spin loop, later in the same body, that s327
never touched**: `funcs_24.c:5540-5550`, a raw `while (MEM_BU(0x8014974C) != 0) {}` with no bound, no
`musyxSynthFrame` call, no diagnostic. Personally verified byte-for-byte (not just trusting the
subagent): the flag it spins on is armed inside `musyxSynthFrame` right before an indirect call
(`funcs_24.c:3991-3992`, `MEM_B(-0X68B4, ...) = ctx->r2` immediately before `jalr $v1`), and is only
clearable from `musyxSynthFrame`'s OWN top-of-function logic (`funcs_24.c:3285-3315`), which itself
blocks on `osRecvMesg_recomp` before writing the clear. Grepped `fixup_game_funcs.py` (spot-checked
personally, not just the subagent's claim): the pump-fix regex only matches the `-0x6676` countdown
pattern (lines 244-245); the only other reference to `-0x68B4` anywhere in the file is an unrelated,
default-off diagnostic (`[musyx-dma-call]`, lines 1778-1792) that doesn't touch the wait or clear
logic. **This second loop is unpatched and un-instrumented in every build configuration**, not
specific to this test.

**Step 5-6 — lock/thread architecture, refuting one candidate mechanism, supporting another.**
`rs64_dmem_lock`/`rs64_dmem_unlock` (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/main.cpp:185-190`) wrap a
`std::recursive_mutex` — **explicitly recursive**, so same-thread re-entry (e.g. a nested
`musyxSynthFrame` call from inside `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`'s pump loop) is well-defined and
non-blocking by design. This refutes a same-thread-relock self-deadlock via that specific mutex.
Separately, `ultramodern::init_events` (`events.cpp:590-634`) spins up architecturally independent
real OS threads for `gfx_thread`, `task_thread` (audio/non-GFX SP tasks), and `vi_thread` — this
supports why `[synth-entry]`/`[audtask-dispatch]` keep firing (81/60 times respectively per s329's
log) throughout the 600s stall even while the game thread is provably wedged: `musyxSynthFrame`'s
other invocation path (the VI-retrace callback table, per prior sessions) most plausibly runs on one
of these separate threads, not the frozen one — though which exact thread was not directly traced
this session (see "still open" below).

**Best-supported (not yet closed) hypothesis**: the game thread, once inside `runVideoFrameTick` →
`musyxNoopStub` → `waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone`, calls `musyxSynthFrame` via the s327 pump (arming the
`0x8014974C` DMA-busy flag near that call's own end), then falls through to the unpatched second spin
loop (`funcs_24.c:5540`), which can only unblock if the flag reads 0 — and the only code that clears
it is `musyxSynthFrame`'s own top-of-function logic, gated behind a blocking `osRecvMesg_recomp`. If
this genuinely never resolves (a true deadlock) or resolves only in a narrow, unsynchronized race
window that a tight busy-spin essentially never samples in practice, either explains a stall lasting
the observed 600s. **This does NOT yet explain why `setDisplayMode`'s 3/3 clean soaks (s327/s328)
never hit this same second loop** despite going through the identical `musyxNoopStub` →
`waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` → pump path at least once at boot — the leading candidate explanation is
`reapplyDisplayMode`'s non-self-clearing, every-frame re-trigger (step 1) compounding the odds of
hitting whatever narrow condition makes loop 2 hang, where `setDisplayMode`'s single one-shot
invocation might statistically avoid it — but this is NOT confirmed, only plausible. Labeled
explicitly as a well-evidenced, address-level-traced CANDIDATE mechanism, not a closed hypothesis: no
runtime observation (no new diagnostic, no soak) was collected this session to confirm the game
thread is actually parked at `funcs_24.c:5540` (PC `0x80091F34`) during an actual stall, nor to
observe the flag's real value/behavior at that moment. Two independent lines of evidence: my own
direct verification of every load-bearing citation matches the subagent's independent read of the
same source — both agree, but both derive from the SAME source text, so this is single-source
evidence in the "two independent lines" sense; a runtime trace would be the second, genuinely
independent line.

No code changed this session (pure source-read, matching the s326 precedent); nothing under `lib/`
touched, no `export.sh` needed. `HYPOTHESIS-ID` pivoted from
`m5-audio-destub-step4-reapplydisplaymode-reversal` (closed as a discovery-phase slug — its
discriminating soak was s329) to `m5-audio-destub-waitformusyx-secondspin-hang` (1st of 3 budgeted
iterations) to track this specific, now well-characterized candidate mechanism.

**Next steps**: add a targeted diagnostic (not yet a fix) at `funcs_24.c:5540`'s loop entry/exit and
at both the arm site (`funcs_24.c:3991`) and clear site (`funcs_24.c:3300`) of the `0x8014974C` flag,
tagged with a thread identifier, then re-run `reapplyDisplayMode`'s reversed-gate soak — this
discriminates cleanly: if the game thread's diagnostic shows it parked at the loop entry for the rest
of the run while the flag never reads 0 on that thread's own samples, the mechanism is confirmed; if
the flag does reach 0 but the spin somehow still doesn't exit, the mechanism needs revision. Only
after that positive/negative control should a fix (bounding loop 2 the same way s327 bounded loop 1)
be attempted and soaked — jumping straight to a fix without runtime confirmation would repeat the
mistake iron rule 1 exists to prevent.

standalone repro: `re.subn(pattern, repl_string, text)` with a plain-string (non-callable) `repl`
argument runs the *replacement* through Python's `re` module's own backslash-escape reprocessing —
`"\\n"` (which Python's own string-literal parser already decodes to the 2 characters backslash+n)
gets re-interpreted a *second* time by `re.sub`'s template engine and collapsed into an actual newline
byte. `re.sub("hello", "X\\nY", "hello world")` reproduces it standalone: `'X\nY world'` (real newline,
not literal backslash-n). The other 3 new diagnostics were unaffected because they used a `lambda`
replacement (whose return value `re.sub` uses verbatim, no reprocessing) — matching the established
convention every prior session's diagnostics in this file already followed, which is exactly why this
had never surfaced before. Fixed by converting the callsite patch to a lambda too; rebuilt clean.

## Session 336 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: source proof that `cinematicLoopBody` self-loops internally, closing the divergent-callee-count question — and a new fact suggesting the whole stall thread may not be an audio issue

instrumentation.

`cinematicLoopBody` (`funcs_27.c:106842`, next function `load_cutscene` starts at `108531`) is ~1700
lines of goto-based control flow reconstructed from MIPS. Rather than hand-trace all of it, wrote a
small throwaway script (`scratch/s336_cinematicloopbody/analyze.py`, not committed — trivial to
reproduce: regex over `^label:$` and `goto label;` lines within the function's line range) to extract
every label definition and every goto, then flag backward jumps (goto target's line number less than
the goto's own line number — since forward gotos are just `if`-statement reconstructions and backward
gotos are the only thing that can form a loop in this idiom).

**Result: exactly one backward jump in the whole function.** `funcs_27.c:108258`'s `j L_800A6024` (a
real MIPS unconditional jump, not a conditional branch — confirmed by reading the raw disassembly
comment on the preceding line, `// 0x800A64B4: j L_800A6024`) lands at `funcs_27.c:107269`
(`L_800A6024`). That target sits AFTER the `static_6_800A9ABC` call site (`107079`, per s335) but
BEFORE the `cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` call site (`107938`, per s334/s335). This is a genuine,
self-contained internal loop: every pass from `L_800A6024` through the backward jump calls
`cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` and `submitGfxFrame` (`108253`) and then jumps straight back to the top
— the `static_6_800A9ABC` call at `107079`, which sits BEFORE the loop's entry point, is never
re-executed on any iteration after the first.

**This directly answers s335's open question, refuting hypothesis 2 and confirming hypothesis 1**:
`cinematicLoopBody` is not invoked repeatedly by some outer caller taking a different path each time —
it loops internally. `static_6_800A9ABC` firing once and `cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` firing 1152+
times in s334's log is exactly what one single invocation of `cinematicLoopBody` produces: one setup
call, then N loop iterations.

ctx)"` across `RecompiledFuncs/*.c`): two call sites, `funcs_44.c:4825` and `funcs_27.c:156405`. Read
both — they are **byte-identical disassembly** (same addresses, same instructions, same enclosing
function shape, `static_6_800AE518`), the same overlay-duplication artifact family s335 already
identified for `static_6_800A9ABC`/`cutsceneDispatchSlotsByFlag` — i.e., one logical function

(`a0=3, a1=2`), `jal cinematicLoopBody` immediately followed by `jr $ra` with no loop around it. This
is consistent with "some other part of the game calls this wrapper once to start a cutscene, and

called at `107331`): nonzero exits the loop, zero (the default/fallthrough path) continues it. Read
`static_6_800AF550` in full (~140 lines, short enough for one pass): it loads a pointer from global
`0x800B0934` (early-outs returning 0 if null), computes a float `f2 = table[0x800A5D70-ish] *
(a2 reinterpreted as float via `mtc1`, no int-to-float conversion) + struct-byte-at-offset-0x2F`,
compares `f2` against two float constants at `0x800A5D70` and `0x800A5D74`, and on the
"not yet past threshold" path increments a debounce counter at struct-offset `0x938`, force-returning
1 (loop-exit) once that counter reaches 7. Every other path returns 0 (keep looping).

**Notable: nothing in `static_6_800AF550`'s body touches any audio-subsystem global, register, MusyX
structure, or DMA/task-queue state.** Every operand is either the per-actor/track struct at
`0x800B0934`, two data-table float constants, or a 7-iteration debounce counter — this reads as an
ordinary elapsed-time/threshold gameplay timer, structurally unrelated to audio. This is **source-level
evidence, not yet a proven conclusion** (the struct fields and the two threshold constants were not
traced back to their producers — did not check whether *something else* [e.g. a delta-time value fed
into the `a2` argument] is itself audio-dependent), but it's suspicious enough to flag explicitly: this
entire investigation thread was opened under the "M5 audio de-stubbing" strategic priority on the
premise that the `reapplyDisplayMode`/VI=640 stall is an audio-stub artifact, and three sessions deep
(s333/s334/s335/s336) nothing found so far — `runVideoFrameTick`'s upstream caller chain, the dead-code
red herring, and now this exit-gate function — has touched audio state at all. It may be a legitimate
(if very slow) cutscene, or a plain gameplay-timer bug, filed under the wrong M-priority.

No code changed, no diagnostics added, no soak run, no `lib/` touched — a source-proof-only session,
same method as s335 ("capture once, analyze many" extended to "read once, analyze exhaustively" for
static control flow — no soak needed when the question is answerable from the text alone).

Pushed the source-read one level further to sanity-check the audio-relevance flag before writing it
down: `static_6_800AF550`'s `a2` argument comes from register `$f20`, set at the very top of the loop
(`funcs_27.c:107279`, `mov.s $f20, $f0`, in the delay slot right after `jal pollControllerInputs` —
so `$f0` at that point is actually the return value of the PRECEDING call, `static_6_800AF360`
(`107270`), not of `pollControllerInputs`). Read `static_6_800AF360`
(`funcs_44.c:5792`): it calls `timeSnapshotFiller` (a real, human-named function — not a `static_N_`
placeholder) to fill a time-snapshot struct, then computes a delta via `floatModulo` against the
previous snapshot. This is the shape of a genuine OS-clock-based per-frame delta-time calculation, not
anything audio-adjacent. So the full traced chain — `cinematicLoopBody`'s loop → `static_6_800AF550`
exit gate → its `a2`/`$f20` input → `static_6_800AF360` → `timeSnapshotFiller` — is, on a pure
source read, **three function-levels deep with zero audio-subsystem references anywhere in it**. This
raises the flag from "worth noting" to "worth prioritizing a runtime check before spending another
audio-focused session here": either the delta-time value is legitimately advancing and this is just a
long (or buggy-duration-table) cutscene wholly unrelated to M5, or something else entirely (not yet
identified) is preventing `timeSnapshotFiller`'s snapshot from advancing. Only a soak with real values
can settle which.

## Session 339 (2026-08-05) — M5 audio: source-proves `submitGfxFrame` structurally cannot produce a `FramebufferPair` and that `cinematicLoopBody`'s self-loop calls the real `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` producer (`runVideoFrameTick`) exactly ONCE, not per-iteration — closes the VI=640 `pairs=0` stall's root-cause chase (s329-s338) in 1 iteration, no new soak

**HYPOTHESIS-ID**: `m5-audio-destub-submitgfxframe-vi-fs-decoupling` (1st and only iteration needed —
closed this session).

**Starting question** (from s337/NEXT.md): does `cinematicLoopBody`'s direct `submitGfxFrame` call
(not `runVideoFrameTick`) decouple from `[vi-fs-decision]`'s `pairs=0` reading — i.e. does
`submitGfxFrame`'s output plausibly reach the same graphics-task queue `[vi-fs-decision]` monitors?

**Method**: pure source-read (per this arc's own convention, s335/s336 already closed 2 prior
questions this way) plus reuse of s337's already-captured soak log — no new soak run.

1. Read `submitGfxFrame`'s full body (`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_3.c:13845`, `N64Recomp` repo — 1289
   lines). Its callee set: `bufferArbiterAllocSlot`, `bufferArbiterMarkSlotReady`,
   `bufferArbiterProducerMark` (×3), `commitMeshDrawBatchRefs`, `drainMeshReleaseQueue`,
   `getInactiveBufferIndex`, `getTimeSinceLastFrame`, `isPreNmiPending`, `osDpGetCounters_recomp`,
   `osDpSetStatus_recomp`, `osRecvMesg_recomp`, `osSendMesg_recomp`, `osWritebackDCacheAll_recomp`,
   `recordFrameTimestamp`, `setPostSwapPendingFlags`, `yieldFromGfxFrame`, `yieldFromSpThread`. No
   `setupCameraMatrices`, no `emitFrameRdpInitDl`, no `runVideoFrameTick`, no `advanceVideoFrame`, no
   indirect (`LOOKUP_FUNC`) calls anywhere in the body.
2. Traced what actually produces a `FramebufferPair` (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_workload.cpp:294`,
   `Workload::addFramebufferPair`, called from wherever the DL interpreter handles a
   `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` opcode). Cross-referenced the `rogue_squadron64` symbol file's existing
   annotations (already on disk from earlier sessions, not re-derived): `emitFrameRdpInitDl`
   (`main_overlay.txt:1096`) is *the* function that emits `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` bytes into the active DL,
   reading the draw-fb address `buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial` wrote. Its **sole caller** is
   `setupCameraMatrices` (`main_overlay.txt:1095`, "runs once per camera/viewport setup"), and
   `buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial`'s only per-frame caller is `advanceVideoFrame`
   (`main_overlay.txt:703`), whose own caller chain is stated explicitly in that file's own comment:
   **"Caller chain: `runVideoFrameTick` → `advanceVideoFrame`."** So the *only* path from any function
   to a `FramebufferPair` is `runVideoFrameTick → advanceVideoFrame → buildAndRegisterDefaultMaterial`
   (writes fb addr) + `→ setupCameraMatrices → emitFrameRdpInitDl` (emits the opcode).
   `submitGfxFrame`'s callee set (step 1) contains none of these — it structurally cannot produce a
   `FramebufferPair`. It only advances the buffer-arbiter slot state machine (alloc→ready→producerMark,
   i.e. the SP-task producer/consumer handshake) and kicks housekeeping (mesh-ref commit, DMA
   writeback, dcache flush) — real per-frame work, just not the `[vi-fs-decision]`-relevant kind.
3. Checked whether `cinematicLoopBody` reaches `runVideoFrameTick` some other way. Grepped its full
   callee list (`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_27.c:106842-108531`, ~50 distinct callees) — no direct call to
   `runVideoFrameTick`, `advanceVideoFrame`, or `setupCameraMatrices`. But it DOES call
   `static_6_800A9ABC` (line 107079) — one of `runVideoFrameTick`'s 5 known call sites from s333's
   original grep. Its real (non-dead) definition is `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_43.c:20718`, and its call to
   `runVideoFrameTick` at `funcs_43.c:20975` sits in plain sequential control flow after label
   `L_800A9C68` — not past an unconditional return like s335's dead-code find, so it's live code, not
   an artifact.
4. **The discriminating fact**: `cinematicLoopBody`'s call to `static_6_800A9ABC` (line 107079) is
   BEFORE its internal self-loop label `L_800A6024` (line 107269, s336's already-proven `goto`-loop
   that runs unconditionally for the whole stall). It is called ONCE, in the function's setup section,
   never again once the self-loop starts.
5. **Confirmed at runtime, not just by source-read** — reused s337's already-captured
   `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/s337cutscenetimer/run.log` (1.28M lines, no new soak): it already had
   `ROGUESQ_LOG_MAINGAMELOOP_REACH=1` armed, which is the env gate on the *already-existing*
   `[static6-800a9abc-entry]` diagnostic added in s334 (misleadingly named after the env var, not the
   function) at `funcs_43.c:20721-20734`. `grep -c '\[static6-800a9abc-entry\]'` → **exactly 1** hit,
   `n=1`, for the entire ~600s run. Two independent lines of evidence (source-read + this runtime
   count) now agree.

**Sanity check (Fermi cross-check on a surprising number, per iron rule)**: s333 measured
`runVideoFrameTick` stops after exactly 2 calls total. s334 independently found `mainGameLoop`'s
loop-top counter fires exactly once. This session's `static_6_800A9ABC` count is also exactly once.
1 (mainGameLoop's own call site) + 1 (via `static_6_800A9ABC`) = 2 — an exact match to s333's raw
count, not just a plausible-sounding one.

**Conclusion — closes the entire s329-s338 VI=640 `pairs=0` stall chase, not just this session's
narrower question**: the graphics-task pipeline is not actually stalled in any subsystem-death sense.
`cinematicLoopBody`'s internal per-frame self-loop (1152+ iterations for the whole soak, per s336)
correctly drives cutscene-slot dispatch, speech, buffer-arbiter SP-task submission
(`submitGfxFrame`), and DMA/mesh housekeeping every single pass — all genuinely alive the whole time,
matching every session's audio/buffer-arbiter observations in this arc. What it does NOT do is
re-invoke the one function chain (`runVideoFrameTick → ... → setupCameraMatrices →
emitFrameRdpInitDl`) that emits a `SET_COLOR_IMAGE` RDP opcode — that chain runs exactly once, in
`cinematicLoopBody`'s pre-loop setup, and never again. `[vi-fs-decision]`'s `pairs` counter
(`Workload::fbPairCount`) can only increment off that opcode, so once the current workload advances
past its one-time pair (or if it's simply the initial state), `pairs` reads 0 for the rest of the
scene — a faithful reading of "no new colour-image target this workload," not evidence of a hung
subsystem. **This is very likely not a bug at all** — a cutscene that holds a locked camera/RDP-state
prologue for its duration (rather than re-emitting per-frame camera setup) is a completely ordinary
optimization for a scripted, non-interactive scene; s336 already flagged that this thread had no
audio-subsystem footprint anywhere in its exit-gate trace, and this session's finding is consistent
with that: **the VI=640 "stall" is a characteristic of this particular cutscene's rendering-loop
design, unrelated to the M5 audio gate reversal that was used to reach it.** No visual defect has
been demonstrated — that would need a separate capture-and-look work unit, out of scope here.

**What this means for M5's still-open decision** (item -182..-187): promoting `setDisplayMode`'s (and
now, by this session's finding, plausibly `reapplyDisplayMode`'s too) gate-byte reversal to the
shipped default is no longer blocked by an unexplained stall — the VI=640 condition it was thought to
risk is now a characterized, benign, non-audio rendering-loop property, not an open crash/hang
mechanism. Recommend the next M5 work unit revisit that promotion decision directly rather than
continuing to instrument this thread further.

**Root cause, traced to source**: `0x80054744` sits inside `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_11.c:15057`, function starts at `0x80054650`) — **this is
`BREADCRUMB9`** (landed s276, per `main_overlay.txt:2031` and grep of PORTING-STATE history
s270-s291: "3 callers in funcs_11/32/33... per-entry timer accumulator update with wrap-around").
Reading the exact instruction sequence around the crash PC (`funcs_11.c:15316-15347`): `divu $zero,
$v1, $v0` at `0x80054738` (dividing by `$v0`, loaded via `lh $v0, 0x0($s0)` at `0x80054734` — a
halfword "threshold" field read from the current list entry), then `bne $v0, $zero, L_80054748`
(skip the trap if the divisor is nonzero) — since `$v0==0` here, execution falls through to the
compiler-inserted `break 7` at `0x80054744`, which the runtime's `do_break()` turns into `abort()`.
`do_break`'s argument, `2147829572`, is not a semantic error code — it's the guest PC itself
(`0x80000000 + 0x54744 = 2147829572`, confirmed by direct arithmetic) — a MIPS N64 compiler idiom
this codebase already recognizes and guards elsewhere for `musyxKeyOnVoice` (8 sites,
`fixup_game_funcs.py:939-949`, `do_break` constants `2148076780..2148077008` → early `return`) and
`evalCubicSplineAtTime` (1 site, zero-width-interval guard → `f4.fl=0` instead of trapping).

already-catalogued one.** PORTING-STATE ~26156 (s289/s290 era) documents `BREADCRUMB9`'s known crash
as `si_addr≈0x80000004` — a near-null-pointer dereference (part of the `-0x25A4`/`G1`-`G32` family of
"a register holding exactly 0 fed into a small-offset `MEM_B`/`MEM_BU` access" bugs). Today's crash has
`si_addr=__pthread_kill`'s address (an `abort()` call site, confirmed via the backtrace: frames 4-5 are
`abort`/`err` from `libsystem_c.dylib`) — a completely different failure mode (compiler div-by-zero trap,
not a memory fault) in the same function. The two are not the same bug re-surfacing; this is a second,
independent defect in `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`'s entry-processing loop.

single-source (1 crash observation) — Iron Rule 4 requires a second independent line of evidence before
this enters "current truth" as a confirmed regression.

**What this does NOT mean**: it does NOT reopen the reapplyDisplayMode question — HA is cleanly

function). The full crash record confirms it: `[CRASH] caught signal 10 (Bus error)`,
`si_addr=0x348187680` (RDRAM host-base `0x300000000` + a corrupted guest offset), native backtrace
`emitAllocatedDLCommand -> submitSceneNodeRender (x2, recursive) -> processSceneNode ->
traverseSceneGraphRecursive -> setupCameraMatrices -> ... -> menuOverlayInit -> mainGameLoop`. This is

original crash, a `break 7` trap, not a bus error). The recipe's blanket "did any `[CRASH]` marker
fire" check cannot distinguish RS64's many independent, nondeterministically-firing crash families
from the one specific bug under test — a genuine confirm-recipe methodology gap, not just this one
instance. **Net for the target signature: confirm2 does NOT confirm it.**

**Read list**: `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md`, `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` (s344's writeup), `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`
tail. Both `m5step5v2_rate_1/2` (the 2 recipes s344 queued, drained by the loop between iterations)
came back `rc=137 | 600s` — a SIGKILL at the loop's hard cap. NEXT.md's own step 2/3 plan expected this
outcome to mean either crash-family #3 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot` pre-title SIGSEGV) or family #4 (the
post-cutscene stall); this session found it was neither.

**Investigation.** Both recipes' verdict `.log` files (`scratch/agent/soak_results/m5step5v2_rate_{1,2}_*.log`)
were EMPTY — the recipe's own `echo "VERDICT: ..."` lines never ran, meaning the whole process (launcher +
post-processing) was killed before reaching them, not merely that the game hung. Read the launcher logs
instead (`m5step5v2rate{1,2}_launcher.log`): both show a completely normal run — `phase width=1024 reached
after 45.7-45.9s` (title), the full `[keys]`/stick schedule through the 240s hold, `hold done wall=275s`,
`done wall=301-302s`, `game process still alive; killing` (the launcher's own routine post-hold kill, not
a hang), then a clean `--- summary ---` block. **The game-side scenario the recipe was driving completed
in ~301s, well inside the 600s budget** — the SIGKILL landed on something AFTER that.

Checked `run.log` size for both: `m5step5v2rate1/run.log` = 8.2 GB, `m5step5v2rate2/run.log` = 7.9 GB.
Every other recipe in this family (`m5step5rate1/2` at ~76 MB, `s343confirm1/2` at ~228-233 MB) produced
1-2 orders of magnitude less. The recipe's post-launcher step is 6 sequential `grep -a` passes over
`run.log` — on an 8+ GB file that never finished before the external 600s watchdog fired, which is why
the verdict `.log`s were empty: the recipe itself was still grepping when it got killed.

**Why the log blew up**: sampled the first 200 MB of `m5step5v2rate1/run.log` — 1,610,567 of 3,603,801
lines (44.7%) are `[rs-free-walk]`. Grepped `PORTING-STATE.md` for that tag and found this EXACT failure
mode already root-caused in Sessions 209-210 (2026-07-28, `unlitmeshtracer4/5/6`): `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_FREE_WALK`
and `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_MALLOC_WALK` log once PER LIST NODE walked, not once per call like every other
`ROGUESQ_LOG_*` var — Session 209 saw a 47x line-count blowup (4.49M → 210M lines) between two runs of the
SAME script with byte-identical instrumentation, and Session 210 confirmed by elimination (stripped all but
one `ROGUESQ_LOG_*` var, log volume dropped ~1470x, real game-tick progress resumed) that the volume itself
was costing enough real fprintf wall-clock to starve actual game-logic progress — not a new behavioral
regression, self-inflicted over-instrumentation. This session's numbers land in the same band: `[rs-free-walk]`
share (44.7%) matches Session 209/210's observed 44-82% range, and the ~40-55x size blowup (76-233 MB → 7.9-8.2 GB)
matches their ~47x line-count blowup almost exactly.

**Open sub-question, not resolved this session**: WHY did this run's walk run away while `s343confirm1/2`
(same script family, same `HOLD_S=240`, run 20 minutes earlier, no code or config change in between) stayed
in the normal 76-233 MB band? Session 209/210's own evidence was that the walker's cost scales with however
many times it gets invoked against however long the free list has grown — consistent with a timing/state-
dependent trigger rather than a fixed per-run cost, but this session did not isolate what specifically
differed between the two soaks. Flagged as open, not blocking: the actionable finding (rc=137 here is a
recipe artifact) does not depend on resolving it.

**Fix landed** (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_s327waitpump.sh`, not `lib/`, no `export.sh` needed): the 4
heap-walker log vars (`ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_MALLOC_WALK`, `_GUARD`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_FREE_WALK`, `_GUARD`) now use
the `${VAR:-1}` default-expansion pattern already used elsewhere in the same file for
`ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME` — every existing recipe that doesn't pre-export these sees identical behavior
(still armed, default 1), but a recipe can now opt them to 0 without forking the 148-line shared driver.
Queued `m5step5v3_rate_1/2.sh` (3rd generation of this recipe family) with the 4 vars set to 0 and 2 new
verdict fields (`runlog_bytes`, `rs_free_walk_lines`) so a recurrence is visible without re-deriving file
sizes by hand. Cancelled `m5step5v2_rate_3/4.sh` (queued, never run) rather than running them unmodified —
they would have reproduced the identical artifact and wasted 2 more 600s loop slots for zero information
(`scratch/agent/soak_queue/cancelled/README.md` updated with the full note, matching the existing
`m5step5_rate_3..6` cancellation precedent from s342).

**Housekeeping**: deleted both 8+ GB `run.log`s (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/m5step5v2rate{1,2}/`) after
extracting the samples above — disk was at 84% used (149 GiB free) before cleanup, 82% (166 GiB free)
after. Not archived; regenerable by rerunning the cancelled v2 recipes if ever needed, though under the
now-fixed driver's unchanged default they'd very likely reproduce the same blowup again (the fix requires
a recipe to opt in, which the cancelled v2 recipes don't).

**Net**: `HYPOTHESIS-ID m5-audio-destub-step5-crashrate-comparison` gained 0 real data points toward the
actual crash-family #3/#4 rate question this session — this was pure recipe-methodology repair, forced by
the loop's own drained verdicts being uninterpretable. 2nd iteration on this hypothesis-id since s344's

### The discriminating check: does allocOrEvictMaterialNode recur?

No. `rate_1`'s crash (item -202) was `allocOrEvictMaterialNode+944`. `rate_3` is
`processSceneNode+1424`. `rate_4` is `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192`. Three crashes, three
different symbols — zero repeats of any single symbol across the whole 4-run batch (`rate_2` was the
only clean run). This directly answers s346's open question: `allocOrEvictMaterialNode` is NOT a
recurring family. It stays a single, uncatalogued data point (1/4), below the bar for a guard.

### Are the other two symbols already-catalogued?

Checked both against `docs/` and `PORTING-STATE.md` via grep before writing this up (Iron Rule 4 —
two independent lines before anything enters the ledger as a conclusion; here the two lines are "not
a repeat of rate_1" and "cross-checked against the existing crash catalog"):

- `processSceneNode` is a KNOWN misattribution-prone, multi-offset crash site: Session 151/152
  documents crashes at `processSceneNode+7640` (s151, called it possibly self-recursion or nearest-
  symbol misattribution given the byte offset dwarfing the function's expected small per-node body)
  and references `+6668` elsewhere (Session ~145-150 range). `+1424` this session is a 3rd distinct
  offset at the same symbol. Read together with s151's own caveat about nearest-symbol
  misattribution being plausible at large offsets, the most parsimonious read is that
  `processSceneNode`'s three different crash offsets across sessions are the SAME underlying
  ambiguous-attribution family recurring at different apparent byte offsets, not three separate bugs
  — but this is not proven, only consistent with the existing caveat.
- `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192` has NO prior crash citation anywhere in the ledger. The
  only existing mention (PORTING-STATE ~line 108, an old symbol-table session) is an unrelated
  duplicate-symbol-address bug fixed long ago, not a crash report. This is a genuinely new site, but
  — like `allocOrEvictMaterialNode` — a singleton with n=1, not (yet) a family.

### A note on why last-guest-pc and pc-symbol looked inconsistent (not a bug, resolved by reading the source)

`rate_4`'s `last-guest-pc=0x8000b650` doesn't fall inside `trackResourceListWithMappingTables`'s own
guest address range (`0x800538B0`+), which looked at first like a symbolization bug worth
investigating. Reading `src/main/main.cpp:1740-1786` resolved it without new instrumentation:
`[CRASH][pc-symbol]` is `dladdr()` on the HOST crash PC (`ss.__pc`, precise, chosen at s206
specifically to avoid `backtrace_symbols`' frame-pointer-walk misattribution) while
`[CRASH][last-guest-pc]` is a separately-tracked checkpoint variable (`g_rs64_last_guest_pc`), updated
at guest recompiled-function/jump boundaries, not necessarily the guest instruction underlying the
exact host-crash PC. The two fields answer different questions by design; a mismatch between them is
expected, not evidence of a bug in the instrument.

### Tally and what it discriminates

4 real (non-artifact) data points on the m5step5v3 template: `rate_1` CRASH
(`allocOrEvictMaterialNode+944`), `rate_2` CLEAN, `rate_3` CRASH (`processSceneNode+1424`), `rate_4`
CRASH (`trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192`). 3/4 (75%) crashed; 0/4 crashed at the SAME symbol
as another run; 0/4 matched the historically-named family #3 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot`) or family #4
(post-cutscene "every soak died earlier" stall) signatures specifically — the two families this whole
step-5 comparison was designed to rate.

This splits the competing hypotheses cleanly:
- H1 "de-stubbing concentrated the risk into one new bug (`allocOrEvictMaterialNode`, candidate family
  #5)" — REFUTED. 0/3 recurrence after rate_1.
- H2 "de-stubbing didn't reduce the post-title crash rate at all, it just moved which symbol shows up
  — family #3/#4 specifically go quiet but the background ~20+-family crash population is still live
  and still fires at a similar overall rate" — SUPPORTED by this batch (0/4 on #3/#4, but 3/4 on
  something).
- H3 "de-stubbing measurably reduced the OVERALL crash rate in this window, #3/#4 or not" — cannot be
  evaluated from this batch alone; would need a comparable pre-de-stub baseline crash rate for this
  exact post-title/craft-select window (the existing family #3/#4 baselines are for different
  windows/mechanisms, not directly comparable to a same-window all-cause rate).

n=4 is still small — precisely BECAUSE each crash is a different symbol, no single-family rate is
yet estimable, matching M5-AUDIO-PLAN's explicit warning against over-reading small samples. Queued
`scratch/agent/soak_queue/m5step5v3_rate_5.sh` through `_8.sh` (identical template) to extend the
sample before drawing a firmer conclusion on H2 vs H3.

### What this does NOT show

Does not show `processSceneNode` or `trackResourceListWithMappingTables` are new families requiring a
guard (each n=1, same standard applied to `allocOrEvictMaterialNode`). Does not show the overall
crash rate changed vs. pre-de-stub baseline (no comparable same-window baseline rate exists yet to
compare against — a gap worth closing if the rate_5-8 batch keeps landing high). Does not change
title-reach status (4/4 title-reach across this whole v3 batch, unaffected).

## Session 348 (2026-08-05) — M5 audio: drained rate_5/6, found the exact-repeat discriminating result, source-read and GUARDED processSceneNode's unguarded content pointer

Drained `m5step5v3_rate_5` (CLEAN, `crash_markers=0`) and `_rate_6` (CRASH) from the soak queue.
`rate_6`'s crash was the discriminating result this whole batch was designed to find: `last_pc_symbol=processSceneNode+1424` AND `last_guest_pc=0x80014FDC` — BOTH fields byte-identical to `rate_3`'s
crash from s347. Not just the same function (which `processSceneNode` has hit at 2 other offsets
historically, `+6668`/`+7640` per s151/152) but the exact same instruction twice: the strongest repeat
match in the whole 6-run v3 sample, and the first symbol in this comparison to cross NEXT.md's declared
"2+ hits" escalation threshold. Updated tally: overall crash rate now 4/6 (67%, down from the earlier
3/4 estimate but still not zero); family #3 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot`)/#4 (post-cutscene stall) still 0/6;
`processSceneNode+1424` now 2/6, `allocOrEvictMaterialNode+944` and `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1192`
stay singletons.

Per NEXT.md's own escalation plan, source-read `processSceneNode` in
`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c` around guest PC `0x80014FDC` (grepped the
breadcrumb comment, unique hit at the time). The crash instruction is `ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r16, 0X30)`
— a dereference of `ctx->r16`, which was loaded two instructions earlier (guest `0x80014FD0`) via
`ctx->r16 = MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0X8)`: a "content" pointer read out of a FIELD of the scene-node pointer
(`ctx->r17`). s190's existing guard (item -190-ish, "processSceneNode node-pointer validity guard")
validates `ctx->r17` itself at function entry but never checks the field loaded out of it — so a
corrupt/stale content-pointer field flows straight into an unguarded deref, explaining a fixed,
repeatable crash address rather than a stack-depth-dependent or nondeterministic one. Grepped for the
same load idiom elsewhere in the function and found a second site (guest `0x800153F8`, funcs_4.c:16493-6)
on the sibling-loop continuation path, which jumps back into the SAME shared block (`L_80014FE8`) that
dereferences the SAME `ctx->r16` again at `+0x34`/`+0x38` — same idiom, second site, not a separate bug.

**Landed a fix**, following the s282-s288 idiom-class-closure model the user directive names for M3
work: added `fixup_game_funcs.py` patches guarding BOTH load sites (mirrors s190's guard shape exactly
— range-check `[0x80000000, 0x80800000)`, bail to the function's existing `L_80015528` exit/sentinel,
env-gated diagnostic logging under `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_CONTENT_GUARD`). Hit and fixed a real
methodology trap while writing this: my first attempt placed the new patch code physically BEFORE the
"processSceneNode guest-PC breadcrumb (BREADCRUMB4)" patch in the script, whose anchor text requires
the `g_rs64_last_guest_pc = 0x80014FD0u;` line that BREADCRUMB4 itself inserts — since pristine
N64Recomp output doesn't have that line yet at that point in the pipeline, the regex silently matched
zero times (`re.subn` returning `n=0`, no error, no report line) and the "fix" was pure no-op. Caught
it only by diffing report output against expectation and adding temporary debug prints; moved the new
patch block to run immediately AFTER BREADCRUMB4 in script order, confirmed both sites now report
`patched x1` and the guard text is physically present in the regenerated `funcs_4.c` (lines ~15191 and
~16512). Full regen (`make_elf.py` -> `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py` -> `cmake --build`) completed
clean, no new warnings/errors beyond pre-existing unrelated ones (DDIV sign-conversion noise in
`funcs_8.c`, present before this session).

Ran one validation soak inline (`s348_contentguard_verify1`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_CONTENT_GUARD=1`
armed via `run_s327waitpump.sh`): crashed at an unrelated, previously-uncatalogued-in-soak-results site
(`musyxSynthFrame+4652`) BEFORE reaching the title screen at all (`title_reached` empty, `keys_lines=0`,
`runlog_bytes=42896` — tiny vs. the normal 50-70MB band, consistent with a very early boot-time death).
Not informative for the guard question either way — the run never got far enough into gameplay to
exercise `processSceneNode`'s crashing path, so this is neither a confirmation nor a refutation, just a
single new boot-time flake to note (first `musyxSynthFrame` hit anywhere in `scratch/agent/soak_results/`
history; audio-subsystem-adjacent, plausibly related to the already-named "`waitForAnyAudioSlot` boot
deaths" family in M5-AUDIO-PLAN but not confirmed as the same mechanism — single data point, treat as

soak queue for the loop to drain — the loop's usual 2-per-iteration cadence should have both landed by
next session. Also re-queued `m5step5v3_rate_7/8.sh` (unchanged, still pending from s347, not yet
drained) so the underlying crash-rate comparison keeps extending in parallel.

**What this does and doesn't establish**: this closes one real, previously-unguarded null/invalid-
pointer-dereference idiom class inside `processSceneNode` (2 sites, same shape as s190's existing
guard), backed by the single most repeatable evidence this whole M5-step-5 comparison has produced

Source-read `coalesceFreeHeapBlocks` at guest PC `0x80002434`
(`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c:4664-4673`, confirmed against the function's
disassembly comments): the function walks the heap's physical block chain by computing `v0 = t0 +
MEM_W(t0, 0x4)` — the current block pointer (`t0`, `ctx->r8`) plus that block's OWN size field — to
locate the next physical block, then immediately reads a 16-bit flags field at `MEM_HU(v0, 0x10)` with
no validity check on `v0` first. If `t0`'s size field is itself corrupt (plausibly from an unrelated,
earlier heap-corruption event elsewhere — this function doesn't need to be the ORIGIN of the corruption,
just the first place that dereferences its downstream consequence), `v0` becomes a wild pointer and this
read is the crash. This is architecturally the same failure shape as every guard landed in this cluster
since s190: an unvalidated pointer-plus-offset walk over heap/list structures with no bounds check before
dereference.

**Source-read** (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c:4360-4701`, the full
`coalesceFreeHeapBlocks` function): found the s354 guard's own design was flawed. The guard's comment
claimed forcing `ctx->r3 = 0` on an out-of-range `v0` "sends control to L_80002358 exactly as if the
coalesce loop had genuinely stopped here" — this is false. `ctx->r3 = 0` makes the immediately-following
`andi $v1,$v1,0x8` / `beq $v1,$zero,L_80002358` pair take the branch TO `L_80002358`, which is the loop's
**entry** label, not an exit. Taking that branch re-enters the loop body carrying `ctx->r8 = v0 + 0x10`
(computed unconditionally in the branch's delay slot, `0x80002440`, regardless of which way the branch
goes — MIPS delay-slot semantics) straight into `L_80002358: lhu $v0, 0x0($t0)` (guest `0x80002358`), an
unconditional dereference of that same wild pointer. This exactly explains `verify5`: the guard fired
(bail path engaged, `v0` correctly detected as out-of-range) but the very next loop iteration crashed one
instruction into re-entering the loop, at a host offset (`+1052`) upstream of the original guarded site
(`+3452`) because it's now the loop's TOP rather than its tail-check.

The real "loop genuinely stopped" exit is `L_80002444` — reached when the branch is NOT taken, i.e. when
`ctx->r3 != 0` (flag bit `0x8` set: the game's own "next block in use, stop coalescing here" signal).
Confirmed by reading the rest of the function (`funcs_0.c` ~4702-4865, through to the function's next
loop and `ctx->r8` reassignment): `ctx->r8` is never read again anywhere between `L_80002444` and the
point where it's freshly reassigned (`ctx->r8 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x10)`, an unrelated second loop over a
different base register) — so forcing the "in use" branch on an invalid `v0` is safe: it drops the wild
pointer without ever dereferencing it again, matching the "treat unreachable state as a safe stop" idiom
every other guard in this project already uses, just applied to the correct branch this time.

**Fix** (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, same guard site as s354, not a new guard):
changed the bail assignment from `ctx->r3 = 0;` to `ctx->r3 = 0x8;` (any nonzero value survives the
`andi ...,0x8` mask the same way the real "in use" flag bit would). Rewrote the patch's header comment to
document the bug and the fix. Same env-gated diagnostic tag `[coalesce-heap-guard]`, same var
`ROGUESQ_LOG_COALESCE_HEAP_GUARD` (already armed by default in `run_s327waitpump.sh`) — no new tag/env
var needed since this corrects the existing guard's behavior rather than adding a new site.

pattern repeats twice" discipline s361 itself used) and found the identical unguarded priming read

|------|-----------------|-----------------|
| 1 | 0x8000819C | 0x800081D4 |
| 2 | 0x800081F0 | 0x80008228 |
| 3 | 0x80008238 | 0x80008270 |
| 4 | 0x80008298 | 0x800082D0 |
| 5 | 0x800082E8 | 0x80008320 |

10012-byte gap, so `+1696` is genuinely inside `heapWalker`'s own compiled

Also notable on its own: `heapWalker` compiles to ~10 KB / ~2500 ARM64
instructions from ~800 bytes / ~175 MIPS instructions of guest code (a ~14x
expansion) — explains why naive percentage-position interpolation between
ARM64 offset and guest address would have been unreliable.

**Decoded the crash instruction**: `0xb82a6928` at `heapWalker+1696` is
`STR W8,[X9,X10]` (32-bit register-offset store), immediately preceded by
`LDR X8,[X8,#24]` (-28) and `LDR X10,[X10,#16]` (-16). The exact instruction
bytes repeat 3x within a 96-byte disassembly window — matching heapWalker's
known 5x-loop-unrolling signature from the guard1/3/4 work (s157-s218).

`gpr r0, r1, r2, r3, ...` with `gpr` = `uint64_t`, so field offsets are
r0=0, r1=8, r2=16, r3=24): offset #16 = `ctx->r2`, offset #24 = `ctx->r3`.
This means the two preceding loads are NOT a raw-pointer chase (the first
hypothesis from s368's writeup) but plain `ctx->r2`/`ctx->r3` struct reads —
X8/X10 transiently held the `ctx` pointer, clobbered by the load result.

store in `heapWalker`'s 671-line body, `funcs_3.c:99-770`) found exactly one
match for "store the ctx->r3 value through ctx->r2 as the address, offset
+4": `MEM_W(0X4, ctx->r2) = ctx->r3;`, occurring once per unrolled loop at
guest `0x80007A3C/0x80007A98/0x80007AF4/0x80007B50/0x80007BAC`. `ctx->r2`
here is freshly loaded from a fixed global table slot two lines earlier
(`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r2, 0X63B0)`) and checked only for `!= 0` (the
surrounding `if (ctx->r2 == 0) {...; goto skip;}` gate that decides whether
the SECOND write executes at all) — never range-validated before being
dereferenced as a write address. Exactly the same checked-non-NULL-but-
unvalidated-pointer idiom as guards 1/3/4, on a new register (ctx->r2, not
the ctx->r3 list-walk cursor guards 3/4 already cover). The sibling write on
the same two lines, `MEM_W(0X0, ctx->r3) = ctx->r2;`, does NOT need a new
guard — ctx->r3 there is the value guard4 just validated two statements
earlier and unmodified since.

## Session 371 (2026-08-05) — M5 Step 6: found and fixed a real host-bridge byte-count bug; PCM confirmed 100% silent (hypothesis 2 CONFIRMED) even under genuine RSP-dispatched real ucode

Before writing the planned `ROGUESQ_LOG_PCM_SANITY` counter, NEXT.md's own prerequisite ("confirm
the sample-vs-byte-count question before writing the iteration bound") required reading
`src/main/main.cpp:677-681` and `lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/audio.cpp:25-36` together.
That read found a real, previously-undetected bug, independent of any runtime measurement:
`ultramodern::queue_audio_buffer` computes `sample_count = byte_count / sizeof(int16_t)` and
passes that **sample count** into the `queue_samples` callback — but the callback's parameter was
named (and treated as) `num_bytes`, and the old code passed it straight through as
`SDL_QueueAudio`'s byte-length argument with no conversion. `SDL_QueueAudio`'s `len` parameter is
a byte count, not a sample count, so every single call queued only **half** the correct number of
bytes to SDL — the back half of every PCM buffer's bytes was silently dropped, unconditionally,
since the day this bridge was written, independent of whether the ucode upstream produces correct
content. `M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md` §4 Step 6 explicitly described this host bridge as "already fully
implemented and functional... confirmed by the runtime survey, not assumed" — **that claim is
overturned** (see `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` superseded section). Fixed in the same edit: renamed the
parameter to `num_samples` and multiply by `sizeof(int16_t)` before calling `SDL_QueueAudio`.
Added `ROGUESQ_LOG_PCM_SANITY` (`[pcm-sanity]`) alongside it in the same function/build (batch
instrumentation rule — one build, one run for everything this step needs). `src/main/main.cpp`
only, no `lib/` touch, no regen pipeline needed (host-side C++, not recompiled guest code).

Ran two soaks with the new build (`ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE=1` + `ROGUESQ_LOG_PCM_SANITY=1`, HOLD_S=120,
`run_s327waitpump.sh` baseline, all standing guards armed):

- **verify1**: crashed pre-title (`title_reached` blank), `[pcm-sanity]` fired 7 times via the
  s327 emergency direct-`musyxSynthFrame`-pump path (`audtask_n=0` — real RSP `M_AUDTASK` dispatch
  never happened before the crash), all 7 calls `all_zero=1`. Crash signature
  `pc-symbol=musyxSynthFrame+4652`, `last-guest-pc=0x8000834c` — checked against the ledger before
  treating this as new: this is **byte-for-byte the same** pre-title crash already documented at
  CURRENT-TRUTH item -222 (s367 `verify2`), already explained there as a coincidental "last
  breadcrumb hit" global overwritten by an unrelated early crash, and already excluded from
  counting under the standing "crash under ~5s that never reaches title_reached is not a
  meaningful test" rule. Confirms this session's fix did **not** introduce a new pre-title crash —
  it's the same pre-existing background noise.
- **verify2**: `title_reached` at 45.6s (normal), ran ~84s into the 120s hold before an unrelated
  crash (`pc-symbol=trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1228`, `last-guest-pc=0x80065e94`) —
  `[pcm-sanity]` fired **13,825 times** over the run via genuine RSP-dispatched real ucode
  (`[audtask-dispatch]` confirms `real_ucode=1` firing 147 times sampled, i.e. real M_AUDTASK
  submission actively occurring, not just the emergency pump). Every single sampled call (n=0..19,
  then every 256th through n=13824 per the standing resample convention) was `all_zero=1` — **zero
  non-zero calls observed anywhere** in either run. `trackResourceListWithMappingTables+1228` is
  very likely the same "Apple system-framework `dladdr` fallback" background-noise family already
  cataloged at CURRENT-TRUTH (`+1192`, n=2 before this run, alongside `unregisterServiceWorker
  +536`) — the few-byte offset shift is consistent with this session's binary changing layout, not
  a different code location. That family's own escalation rule ("a 3rd independent hit is the
  trigger") is arguably now met (n=3), but per the standing "no reactive single-crash chases"
  directive this is being cataloged as a data point for the next M3 idiom-class audit, not chased
  this iteration.

**Step 6 verdict: Hypothesis 2 (silent-but-not-crashing) CONFIRMED, not merely plausible.** Across
both the emergency-pump path (7 calls) and the genuine RSP-task-dispatched real-ucode path (13,825
calls, `real_ucode=1` independently confirmed active in the same run), 100% of sampled PCM buffers
handed to `queue_samples` were exactly all-zero. This is a positive-controlled result (the
instrument fired thousands of times, and `audtask-dispatch` independently confirms real ucode
dispatch was genuinely occurring, not just completing a no-op) — not a null result lacking a
control. The "exactly zero, not merely near-zero" pattern across 13,825+ samples favors hypothesis
2 (silent) over hypothesis 3 (garbage/incoherent-but-nonzero) specifically, though sampling every
256th call rather than every call means a rare non-zero call between samples can't be fully ruled
out — noted as a limitation, not overclaimed. Net: the real MusyX ucode, even when genuinely
