(`mcontext x12=0x00000000c8830d14`) modulo the RDRAM host-mapping offset -- the low 24 bits
(`0x830D10`+`0x4`=`0x830D14`) match the fault address's low bits exactly. Read the generated source
(`funcs_4.c:4376-4405`): `0x80010DC0`-`0x80010DC4` is the existing `SIBLING_PTR_WRITE_GUARD` site
guarding `ctx->r5`; `0x80010DC8` (`bne $a0,$zero,...`) does not touch `ctx->r5`; its delay-slot
instruction `sw $zero,0x4($a1)` at `0x80010DCC` is emitted TWICE by the recompiler (once for the taken
branch, once as fallthrough -- same non-branch-likely delay-slot duplication `FREELIST_NEXT_GUARD`
hit with `bnel`, s441) and BOTH copies write through the SAME never-rechecked `ctx->r5` -- exactly the
item -319 idiom (a gap immediately after an existing guard, reusing its already-validated-then-
invalidated register) recurring in a new function. Filed as item -334, fixed as
`SIBLING_PTR_WRITE_GUARD` site=`0x80010DCC` (122nd/123rd list entries, 2 delay-slot copies of 1 guest
address) using the family's existing per-site literal-anchor mechanism and shared env var
(`ROGUESQ_LOG_SIBLING_PTR_WRITE_GUARD`, already armed).

rebuilding, re-ran the SAME live-verify recipe: this time the crash moved downstream to
`last-guest-pc=0x80010e6c` -- item -327's OWN exact catalogued address (previously 2 occurrences 21
sessions apart, "watch for a 3rd before source-tracing" per NEXT.md), now a confirmed 3rd occurrence in
the immediately-preceding v1 run (before this session's 2nd fix). Read the source at `funcs_4.c:4670-
4699`: this is `submitSceneNodeRender`'s own instance of the `DL_LIST_APPEND_GUARD` idiom (s454, a
57+27=84-site family). The existing `DL_LIST_APPEND_GUARD` (addr3=`0x80010E68`) validates `rload` (the
list HEAD pointer, the `-0x5824` global) before reading `ctx->r{rderef} = MEM_W(rload, 0)` -- but
`rderef` itself, a VALUE READ BACK FROM GUEST MEMORY (the head's own field0, i.e. the list's "next"
pointer), was never range-checked before `addr4` (`0x80010E6C` in this instance) dereferences it as a
write ADDRESS. The existing `DL_LIST_APPEND_RWRITE_GUARD` (s482, addr6) only ever validated `rwrite`
(the NEW NODE argument) -- a completely different register. Confirmed via the family's own regex
(`_dl_list_append_guard_re` in `fixup_game_funcs.py`) that this exact 4-instruction tail
(`ctx->rderef = MEM_W(rload,0); MEM_W(0,ctx->rderef) = ctx->rwrite; ctx->rload = MEM_W(rload,0);
MEM_W(4,ctx->rwrite) = ctx->rload;`) is byte-identical at ALL 84 canonical sites (the same claim s454's
and s482's own comments already made and relied on to justify their own blanket fixes) -- so this is a
genuine family-wide gap, not a single-site anomaly. Same remediation precedent as `FREELIST_NEXT_GUARD`
(s441) and item -319/`SIBLING_PTR_WRITE_GUARD`'s own s520 gap: skip-the-write-on-invalid (`rderef` is
dead after this block in every sampled site). Folded directly into the SAME blanket regex substitution

all 84 sites in one edit (46 funcs_3.c + 38 funcs_4.c, confirmed by the fixup report's `patched x46`/
`x38` counts matching the pre-existing `DL_LIST_APPEND_GUARD` counts exactly, i.e. every append-guard
site now also has a deref-guard). Site `0x80010E6C` specifically covers item -327's exact crash address.

**Regen and rebuild.** `make_elf.py` -> `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py` -> `cmake --build`, all

### Source: how hangar is supposed to exit

`runHangarMenuFromOverlay` (`funcs_35.c`): poll `runHangarSelectionFrame` while
`v0 == 0x00FFFFFF` (NOT 0xFFFFFFFF — symbol comment was wrong); then
`gracefulMenuShutdown`.

`updateHangarBayScene` confirm (`funcs_28.c` ~0x800AC8C0):
```
getControllerNewButtonsPressed();
if (v0 & 0x9000) {  // A (0x8000) | START (0x1000)
  if (!isPlayerShipActive())  // gPlayerShip @ 0x800CC85C == 0
    store craft_idx to gHangarSelection @ 0x800CD6D4 (-0x292C from 0x800D)
}
```
B (0x4000) in `runHangarSelectionFrame` writes cancel sentinel 0x00FFFFFE (also gated
on !isPlayerShipActive).

Frame return (`runHangarSelectionFrame` tail):
```
if (accumulateShipThrottleCharge() != 0)
  return gHangarSelection;  // exit poll
return 0x00FFFFFF;          // continue
```
`accumulateShipThrottleCharge` returns 1 only when gPlayerShip non-null and a charge
counter reaches 7; null-ship path returns 0 (L_800B421C). So **confirm write requires
ship inactive; poll-exit requires ship active + charge** — a multi-frame state machine,
not a single Start.

s74 "A no-ops" and s572 "Start moves camera but stays hangar" fit if either (a)
`isPlayerShipActive` stays 1 (blocks selection write) or (b) throttle never returns 1
(blocks poll exit) or (c) both. Synthetic Start correctly maps to 0x1000
(`main.cpp` N64_START_BUTTON).

### Ruled out
- Mission overlay DMA after craft-leave (this recipe).
- Stick-hold as primary M3 DoD gate (still hangar menu).
- Blind HOLD_S=60 retries without measuring hangar-exit gates.

it *is* the DPC submit head for one command at a time.

  section 4` at run.log:278849, ~4 lines from EOF) with a full same-run
  positive control (`case6=1 hangar-sel=1 inject_lines=26
  recov76B768~=15912 thr495FC_creates=2` — the 2 thr-create hits are both
  from the SAME early-cinematic creation event, not post-exit). 4 lines
  after the post-exit sec4 line, the process crashed:
  `[CRASH] pc-symbol=coalesceFreeHeapBlocks+4424 last-guest-pc=0x8000247c`,
  backtrace confirms `cinematicLoopBody -> initSceneForMission ->
  coalesceFreeHeapBlocks` — **byte-identical to s589's crash**, same stack.

### H13c now CONFIRMED 2/2 (per NEXT.md's own outcome criterion)
s589 (session 589) + s592a: two independent force-exit runs, both reaching
post-exit section 4, both crashing at the exact same guest PC in the exact
same call stack before thr-12 (`entry=0x800495FC`) could be (re-)created for
the mission. This is no longer "file not chase" — it meets the stated bar to
open a mechanistic audit.

### Root cause (source-read, `funcs_0.c` via
`/Users/williambuckley/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c`)
`coalesceFreeHeapBlocks` has **two independent** forward block-coalescing
loops. The FIRST (`L_80002358`, walking from `$t0`/`ctx->r8`) was already
guarded at guest PC `0x80002434` back in the s354-366 arc (`COALESCE_HEAP_GUARD`,
bail-target bug fixed s358). The SECOND (`L_80002474`, walking from
`$s2`/`ctx->r18` — a different base register, never covered by the s354-366
audit because that audit was scanning `drainMeshReleaseQueue`, a different
function) has the exact same unguarded idiom: `v0 = a2 + MEM_W(a2, 0x4)`
then `MEM_HU(v0, 0x10)` at `0x8000247C` with no bounds check. If `a2`'s size
field is corrupt (from earlier heap corruption elsewhere), `v0` is wild and
this read faults. Branch analysis confirms the loop's exit path only reads
`ctx->r7` (saved as the last-known-good `a2` BEFORE this read) and
`ctx->r16` — never the just-computed `v0` unless the loop continues — so the
already-verified-safe bail (`ctx->r3 = 0x8`, forcing the "next block in use"
exit branch) applies unchanged.

### Fix landed
`fixup_game_funcs.py` (in `~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp`, not under this
repo's `lib/` — untracked-by-git file, same as the ~150 other hand patches
already there): new patch block right after the existing coalesce guard,
adds a second guard at `0x8000247C` with its own env var
`ROGUESQ_LOG_COALESCE_HEAP_R2_GUARD` / tag `[coalesce-heap-r2-guard]` (kept
as a distinct family, not folded into the original, since it's a genuinely
different site/loop). Full regen (`make_elf.py` -> `N64Recomp` -> fixup ->
cmake) completed clean; fixup report showed the new patch applying exactly
`x1` alongside the pre-existing one, no sentinel refusal, build succeeded
with only pre-existing warnings.

## Session 595 — 2026-08-09 — item -361: 6th+7th coalesce R2 verify attempts consumed; item -347 REFRAMED as instrumentation-coverage artifact, not a recurring bug; recipe redesigned

### Consumed queued s594_coalesce_r2_verify_c/_d
Both already ran between iterations. `_d`: `case6=0 hangar-sel=0 sec4=0
crash=CRASH` — pre-engagement null, same shape as prior nulls. `_c`: **real
progress** — `case6=1 hangar-sel=1 inject_lines=24 sec4=1 recov76B768~=0
crash=CRASH`. Force-exit engaged, hangar-sel reached, `FS_PIPE_INJECT`
climbed to n=200+ through the E7→F3→FD residual sequence (matches s588's H9d
model exactly), but **the FULL_SYNC recovery cell `0x76B768` never fired**
(0 occurrences in 183k lines) — so thr-11 never destroyed, sec4 never
reached its post-exit 2nd hit, and the run drifted ~380s until an unrelated
crash. Neither `_c` nor `_d` reaches `sec4>=2`; both are non-discriminating
for the R2 guard fix itself (iron rule 1: `coalesce_guard2_r2=0` on both,
consistent with "guarded code path never executed", not "fix inert").

### Item -347 REFRAMED: 3rd occurrence is not evidence of a recurring bug
`_c` crashed at `pc-symbol=transformLightByType+256 (local-symtab)`,
`last-guest-pc=0x80010134` — item -347's exact signature, now 3 occurrences
(s566, s582, s594/s595). Per that item's own escalation rule ("watch for a
3rd before source-tracing"), traced the guest PC in
`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c`: `0x80010134` is the
JAL-delay-slot `sw $v0, 0x10($sp)` in `submitSceneNodeRender`, immediately
after `jal transformSceneLights` (0x80010130). That part of the s566/s582
analysis was already correct. New finding: **`transformSceneLights` and its
callee `transformLightByType` (funcs_3.c:36935-37750 and :30793-31082) carry
ZERO `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` tracking lines in their bodies** — confirmed by
direct grep over both function ranges. Cross-checked against
`submitSceneNodeRender` (which DOES track every instruction, 1164 tracking
lines + 20 `GUARD` macro references in its first 700 lines) to establish the
mechanism: tracking is **guard-campaign-associated instrumentation**, added
only to the ~150 functions touched by the freelist/sibling-ptr/etc. audit
lineages (item -317 and siblings), not blanket per-function coverage.
Codebase-wide scan (`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c`, all `RECOMP_FUNC` bodies
>5 lines): **2447 of 2499 functions (98%) have zero tracking lines** — the
instrumented set is the exception, not the rule.

**Consequence:** when a crash occurs anywhere inside an unaudited callee
subtree, `g_rs64_last_guest_pc` freezes at the last *instrumented* caller's
address — here, permanently at `submitSceneNodeRender`'s own JAL delay slot,
regardless of which instruction inside `transformSceneLights` /
`transformLightByType` / their own callees actually faults. Three sessions
reporting the identical `last-guest-pc=0x80010134` is therefore **not**
proof of one recurring bug at one address — it is consistent with three
completely different crashes anywhere in an unaudited, multi-function-deep
subtree, all bucketed under the same caller stub. Item -347's "watch for a
3rd before source-tracing" escalation heuristic does not apply here: there
is no more precise site to source-trace than "somewhere past
`transformSceneLights`," and treating this as a single fixable bug would be
guessing. **Reclassified: filed as instrumentation-coverage artifact, not
escalated.** No guard written.

**Generalization (method trap):** the "watch for the Nth occurrence before
escalating" pattern used throughout the Next-steps breadcrumb list
(items -323/-324/-325/-326/-330/-332/-333 use the same heuristic) is only
sound when the reporting function is inside the guard-audited/instrumented
set. For a breadcrumb whose function has never been touched by a guard
campaign, repeated identical `last-guest-pc` values carry much weaker
evidentiary value than the heuristic assumes, since the address may be a
shared caller stub rather than the true fault site. Did not audit which of
the other watch-listed breadcrumbs are similarly affected (out of scope for
this iteration) — flagging the caveat for future escalation decisions
rather than re-litigating each one now.

Tally since item -359 opened this question: s589 (reached, recovery fired),
s592a (reached via retry, recovery fired), then **5** consecutive
path-gated/pre-engagement nulls (s592b, s593-manual, s593_a, s593_b, s594_d)
plus **1** reached-but-no-recovery null (s594_c) = **7 consecutive
non-discriminating attempts** for the R2 guard fix specifically. Per

`_c`'s data point narrows the redesign: the recipe CAN reach case6=1 +
hangar-sel=1 + full FS_PIPE_INJECT residual coverage reliably when it gets
past the pre-engagement noise — the remaining unreliability is specifically

window (s589/s592a yes, s591/s594_c no). Redesigned: raised `HOLD_S` 90→210
(s592a's own 267s @ HOLD90 implies ~177s non-hold overhead; 177+210=387s,

`waitForAnyAudioSlot+244` looked like a fresh, 2/2 exact-match signature —

  `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList` / guest `0x80054750` (hangar menu path)
- a2: **engaged** case6=1 hangar_sel=1 ace80=1 force6=0 force_skip=1,
  early=recovery_silent (0×76B768)
- a3: pre_eng budget

Deep-read of a2 (engaged silent):
- hangar-state transitions 0→1→3→5→6→8 correctly; ACE80 natural 5→6; case6+hangar-sel fire
- `[case5-entry] n=0.. state=255` while hangar-state=5 (and force skip old=255)
- s614 a2 had case5-entry state=110; s612 had state=6; s613 state=3 — all **disagree
  with hangar-state** at the same wall-clock window
- post-hsel fullsync top addrs lack 0x76B768 (recovery silent confirmed)
- thr11 id=10 live through recovery wait (no thr11d/sec2)

### Discriminating finding — OOB MEM_* base
`MEM_BU(offset, reg)` address = `((reg+offset)^3) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000`.

| base type | idx for hangar byte `-0x3C1C($0x800D)` |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| `gpr`/`S32(0x800D<<16)` = `0xFFFFFFFF800D0000` | **0xCC3E7** (in 8MB RDRAM) |
| `uint32_t 0x800D0000` | **0x1000CC3E7** (OOB) |

case5-entry / FORCE_STATE6 / case3-start patches used `uint32_t base = 0x800D0000u`.
hangar-state / state-write patches used recompiled `ctx->r*` (already S32-extended) —
hence they agreed with reality while case5-entry read garbage (255/110/0/3/6 from OOB).

s613 recharacterization: the logged `[case5-force-state6] old=3 new=6` wrote OOB;
hangar-state n=800 still state=5 after. The 488s pre-eng hang was **failure to force
real state**, not a successful harmful 3→6 clobber. State==5 gate policy remains correct
once the read/write hits the real byte.

### Fix landed
- `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_28.c`: case5 force-state6 + case3-start use
  `gpr base = S32(0x800D << 16)` and `MEM_BU(-0x3C1C, base)` / `MEM_B(-0x3C1C, base)`.
- `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`: templates updated + s616 migration from uint32 base.
- Binary rebuilt (`RecompiledFuncs` → `RogueSquadron64Recomp`).

### Soak enqueued
`scratch/agent/soak_queue/s616_force6_kseg0_base_fix.sh`
- Positive control: case5-entry states ∈ {0..8}, not stuck on 255/110
- Then same recovery-active free-reroll + class-D A–D scoring as s615
- Exit 3 on ctrl fail

| H-kseg2 | s613 force write never touched real hangar state | **CONFIRMED** (hangar-state stayed 5) |
| H-force6b | state==5 gate is correct policy | still held; was masking H-kseg1 |

## Session 632/633 — 2026-08-10 — first-ever fed fail136c discriminator: `reason=corrupt`, selected-pool E8 freelist walk breaks mid-scan (item -390/-391)

Consumed the two queued accumulation soaks from s631 (`s632_thr11d_rate_accum_a`,
`s633_thr11d_rate_accum_b`, mechanically identical to s631's recipe,
`HOLD_S=210`). `s632` had 1 attempt, `recov768=0` (silent) — no new data
point for the recovery-fired tally other than the denominator. `s633` scored
on its very first attempt: `recov768` fired, and — for the first time in this
campaign — **`thr11d_new=1` AND `ltexmg≥1` AND a scored `fail136c` all landed
in the same attempt.** Every prior `thr11d_new=1` sample (s629 att4) had been
killed by the `loadDatFile+692` background-noise crash before ever reaching
`ltexmg`; this is the first sample that survived long enough to actually
exercise the -389/-390 discriminator.

### The discriminator result: `reason=corrupt`, not a clean no-fit
`s633` `SCORE`: `thr11d_new=1 ltexmg=1 sec4_post=1 diag_fail136c=1 diag_ok136c=1
diag_reason=corrupt diag_maxfree=0x6A3E0 diag_maxfree_sel=0xD20 diag_nfree_sel=3
diag_need=0x1370 ship_store=2 ship_zero_post=2`. `maxfree_sel=0xD20 <
need=0x1370` on its face reads as H-ltexOOM-sel confirmed (selected pool
lacks a block big enough) — but the diagnostic's own reason field overrides
that with `corrupt`, because the raw pool walk hit `rsm_corrupt=1`
somewhere. Reading the raw per-pool dump (`fixup_game_funcs.py`'s
`rs-malloc-diag` block, `funcs_0.c`): pool 4 (unselected) and pool 0
(selected) both walk cleanly to their terminator; **pool E8 — the other
selected pool — stops with `stop=bad_size` at node index 55 of a walk that
had found 54 valid-looking nodes first** (`nnodes=56 nfree=1 maxfree=0x20`,
i.e. the only free block found before the break was tiny, 0x20 bytes).
Notably, an EARLIER `posctrl` sample from the same run (an unrelated
successful large allocation, printed first in the log since posctrl captures
the first 8 successes) shows pool E8 healthy at that earlier point in time:
`stop=term dumped=6 nnodes=6 nfree=2 maxfree=0x4E6290` (~5 MB free). So
whatever breaks the E8 walk develops **during the run**, between that
earlier successful allocation and the `ltexmg` attempt — not a permanently
malformed pool.

**This is genuinely new information, not previously seen:** neither the s627
global-OOM check (O1, REFUTED) nor the s627 size-corruption check (O3,
REFUTED) exercised the SELECTED pool's own walk integrity — those checked
"is there free space somewhere" and "is the requested size sane," not
"does the freelist chain in the pool `rs_malloc` actually searches stay
sane end to end." `reason=corrupt` had appeared once before (s627, folded
into the `no_fit_mystery` diag-artifact finding) but was never traced to a
specific pool/node before now.

### Instrument gap fixed same session
The raw node at the break point (i=55, pool E8) was read by the diagnostic
(`rsm_f`/`rsm_bsz` are computed unconditionally before the sanity check) but
never printed — the per-node `fprintf` was gated to free nodes or the first
8 allocated nodes per pool (log-budget rule), and node 55 was neither.
Fixed in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (N64Recomp sibling repo, `funcs_0.c`
rs-malloc-diag patch block): the print gate now also fires when the node
fails its own sanity check (`!rsm_sane`), so the NEXT occurrence of
`stop=bad_size` will show the actual raw `flags`/`size` at the break —
letting us tell real heap corruption (garbage bytes) apart from a walker
bug (a legitimate block shape the sanity check wrongly rejects, e.g. a
sentinel/terminator pattern this walk doesn't special-case). Full regen
pipeline run this session: `make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py`
→ `cmake --build`, all clean. `fixup_game_funcs.py` itself remains untracked
in the N64Recomp sibling repo (as it has been for the whole campaign — not
part of this repo's `lib/`, no `export.sh` applicable).

4/11); of those, `thr11d_new` completed in 2/5 = 40% (was 1/4 = 25%) —
`H-thr11destroy-rate` stays SUPPORTED, sample still small (N=5).
`H-shipcycle2` (2nd ship-store/zero cycle correlates with `thr11d_new`

to the diagnostic's contiguous walk. Early posctrl E8 nodes also verify

`stop=bad_size` at E8 i=55 is not a walker-model artifact. Predicted bad-node
address from i=54 free `@0x801F3C90 size=0x20`: **`0x801F3CC0`**. The break is

size field is truly insane the remaining free is unreachable to both game and
diag — explaining selected-pool null `rs_malloc(0x136C)` despite pool4 having
≥ need free (unselected). Still need the !sane print of raw flags/size at

### Static freelist writer audit (item -391 / -385)

Node layout (rs_malloc walk L_80001BC4..): flags halfword @+0 (1=free, 2=alloc, 8=term),
size word @+4, next = addr + size + 0x10.

| Writer | flags/size stores | Can produce flags=0 size=0? |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| rs_malloc alloc | flags=2; size=req (exact) or split | **No** — residual only if rem≥0x20; residual size = rem−0x10 ≥ 0x10 |
| rs_free | flags=1 only; size preserved; coalesce grows size | **No** — never zeros size |
| coalesceFreeHeapBlocks | flags=1; size merge | **No** |
| buildHeapFreeList / initMainHeap | flags=1; size=pool−0x20; term size=0 with flags&8 | **No** for !term zero-node |

**H-zero-free REFUTED (static).** **H-split-bug REFUTED (static).**
**H-never-init REFUTED** for mid-run i=55 after healthy posctrl (s638 dual-source dump).

**H-walk-into-zeros** (prev free size too small so walk lands on payload zeros).

### ORIGIN (required before further freelist mitigation)

- **Immediate host writer of freelist stomp:** RT64 `copyNativeToRAM` color
  writeback of SETCIMG `addr=0x1F0D74` `w=1161` (range covers freelist phys
  `0x1F3CC0`). Product path ALLOW_WILD_FL + multi-header restore then repairs
  the 16B headers (match=1 same dump).
- **Why those operands exist:** length-respecting RDP walker over a
  **just-wrapped DPC ring** (`in_wrap=1`, ring start=`0x766000`) interprets
  garbage bytes as `G_SETCIMG` (op `0x3F`). Prev command ring is non-monotonic
  (zeros, nonsense `0x3F`), not a clean allowlist-width chain.
- **Legitimate?** **No.** This game never uses width 1161; same class as hangar
  wilds (s662: 104/104 `in_wrap=1` after garbage TRI). Hangar cluster uses ring
  start=`0x781800`; killer uses `0x766000` — shared class, different ring
  instance.
- **Not** a deferred-merge artifact outside submit: sticky
  `submit=[0x768D40,0x7699D0)` contains the killer task.

### Ruled out

- Exact killer as legitimate ucode emission (H-exact-legit).
- Exact killer as submit-range merge bug with empty sticky (H-exact-submit-range).
- Need for more freelist writeback mitigation layers before origin settled.

### Product implication

Freelist restore layers (s653–s660) are still correct as **defense** while
garbage CIMG still reaches writeback. Root fix is **stop feeding wrap-stale
ring content into processRDPLists** (or drop those submits), then A/B freelist
mitigation OFF expecting stomp rate → 0.

### Hypotheses

| ID | Claim | Result |
|----|-------|--------|
| H-wrap-filter-kills-killer | Filter zeroes KILLER + freelist stomp with restore OFF | **UNEVALUABLE** — filter never reached hangar/killer window |
| H-wrap-filter-false-drop | Filter drops legitimate post-wrap ring reuse (cinematic dies, hangar black) | **CONFIRMED dual-source (A+B)** |
| H-filter-needs-byte-granularity | Task-address in_wrap sticky is too coarse | **SUPPORTED** (same mechanism as false-drop) |

### Discriminating evidence

**A** (`s664_A_filter_restore_1_*`): banner=1; `[dpc-wrap-drop]` counter to
#29696 (rate-limited log lines 45); **all drops against single wrap start
`0x4B7800`** with seen growing to ~`0x4D3598`. OK×8 early boot LIVE
(tasks at `0x777880` outside that ring). **wild=0, vi1024=0, force6=0,
pngs=0**. SIGBUS mid-cinematic (`cinematicLoopBody` ←
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive` / `submitSceneNodeRender`). ~40s death.

**B** (`s664_B_filter_norestore_1_*`): identical shape to A (banner, ~30k
drops, OK×8, wild=0, cinematic SIGBUS). Restore OFF irrelevant — never
reached freelist stomp window.

**C** (`s664_C_nofilter_norestore_1_*`, posctrl control): drop=0; OK×8
wild=40 **killer=1** exact `task=0x768D40 w=1161 addr=0x1F0D74 in_wrap=1
submit=[0x768D40,0x7699D0)`; `ALLOW_WILD_FL` + `HIT_WRITE` (restore=0);
immediate freelist-shaped `to_zero prev_f=0x2 prev_sz=0x60` @ t=168799ms;
zero_node follow-on. Reconfirms s663 ORIGIN under restore OFF.

### Mechanism of false-drop

Sticky wrap `[start,seen)` never expires. After ring `0x4B7800` wraps once,
every subsequent **legitimate** rewrite of that ring has `submit_lo` still
inside sticky and is dropped forever (~30k drops). Hangar/killer rings
(`0x781800` / `0x766000`) never reached because cinematic already starved.

This is the same address space the game *reuses* after wrap — not a brief
"stale tail" window. Coarse task-lo ∈ sticky cannot distinguish garbage
decode from legitimate re-emit.

### ORIGIN (unchanged from s663)

```
ORIGIN: freelist stomp host writer = RT64 copyNativeToRAM color writeback of
SETCIMG addr=0x1F0D74 w=1161 (covers freelist phys 0x1F3CC0). Operands are
NOT legitimate — length-respecting RDP walk over just-wrapped DPC ring.
Filter at submit_lo∈sticky is too coarse; keep product freelist restore.
```

### Ruled out

- Productizing `ROGUESQ_DROP_WRAP_RDP` as default-ON task-address filter.
- Expecting freelist-restore retirement from this filter shape.

### Product

Keep `ROGUESQ_DROP_WRAP_RDP` default **OFF** (debug/experiment only).
Product freelist multi-header restore remains defense-in-depth.

### Next (-417)

Narrower root fix candidates (rank):
1. **Garbage-prev SETCIMG drop** inside processRDPLists / setColorImage:
   reject wild SETCIMG when prev ring is non-monotonic garbage (zeros /
   op 0x3F / non-allowlist) — targets decode site, not whole submit.
2. **Byte-offset desync**: only drop the *tail past last consumed high-water
   that was never rewritten* — requires tracking which ring bytes were
   re-written post-wrap (harder).
3. Keep freelist restore; treat wrap-stale as permanent class residual until
   (1) lands.

### New lead for -421 (rdpFs plateau), found in already-captured data — no new run needed

While hand-verifying the confirming run, noticed the existing
`[dl-sync-probe]` instrument (already firing every task under the freeroll's
standard `ROGUESQ_LOG_DL_SYNC=1`, no new instrumentation needed) had never
been tallied in aggregate before — only spot-read per-task. Scoped to
lines `>= sec2_ln=347715` (post-sec2 mission phase only) in the same
`pulse_2_20260811200701/run.log`:

- 29780 `[dl-sync-probe]` lines post-sec2. `e9_a`/`e9_b` (proper
  control-flow-respecting tree walks, one treating opcode 0xB5 as
  end-of-DL, one not) are BOTH zero in 18452/29780 (~62%), but **11328/29780
  (~38%) show e9_a>0 or e9_b>0** — i.e. a large fraction of post-sec2
  mission tasks DO contain the SYNC_FULL byte value in their raw command
  walk.
- Cross-referenced against the same window's `[runner] task ... syncs=`
  field (the runner's own translated/dispatched RDP command count, the
  actual signal `rdpFs`/item -421's plateau is measured from): **29777/29780
  post-sec2 tasks report `syncs=0`; only 3 show `syncs=1`.**

Read together: a large fraction of post-sec2 mission DLs contain what the
naive fixed-8-byte-stride walker sees as an E9 opcode, yet the runner's own
translated-command counter almost never registers a real sync. Two
competing explanations, NOT yet distinguished:
- **H-e9-not-translated:** the guest DL genuinely contains SYNC_FULL
  requests that our RDP command translator/dispatcher drops or fails to
  execute for this task class — would directly explain the -421 plateau as
  a translation-path bug, not a content-absence issue.
- **H-e9-walker-misaligned:** `walk_tree`'s fixed 8-byte stride (used for
  `e9_a`/`e9_b`) does not account for the F5 ucode's variable-length
  inline-data commands (MoveMem/TriGen/Tri/TexrectGen/SetOtherMode_*_EX —
  see `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md`), unlike the existing
  `ROGUESQ_LOG_DL_SYNC2` six-command-aware walker (built for the
  cimg-origin-desync investigation, `-415..-417`). An unaligned walk can
  land mid-command and read a coincidental 0xE9 byte that isn't a real
  opcode boundary — the 38% hit rate could be entirely this artifact.

Not adjudicated this session (out of scope for the assigned -422 work
unit; flagging per iron rule 5 "check the boring thing first" — an
instrumentation alignment bug is the boring explanation and must be ruled
out before H-e9-not-translated enters CURRENT-TRUTH). Full next-step design
in `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`.

### Rules out / confirms

- H-menu-return-input CONFIRMED (was SUPPORTED single-source in s670).
- Old `wrapper.stdout` leftover data reconfirmed as already-closed s670
  material — not a missed/interrupted iteration.

### Residual → -421 gets a concrete next-step candidate (E9-alignment check on the existing dl-sync-probe2 walker); -422 fully CLOSED, no further residual.

## Session 674 (2026-08-12) — HARNESS: codex runner made viable; two loop bugs fixed

Not an experiment iteration. Toolchain work on `tools/agent/`, prompted by the
first `RUNNER=codex` runs (s673 and the 00:21 restart).

**s673's "no SDL display" was the codex SANDBOX, not the terminal context.**
`codex exec` defaulted to `-s workspace-write`, which is a seatbelt sandbox.
Measured directly in a throwaway `/tmp` git repo (codex-cli 0.144.3), inside
that sandbox vs an ordinary shell:

| probe | `-s workspace-write` | unsandboxed / `danger-full-access` |
|---|---|---|
| `test -w .git` | `GIT_READONLY` | `GIT_WRITABLE` |
| `nice -n 5 true` | `setpriority: Operation not permitted` | `nice_rc=0` |
| `launchctl managername` | `Aqua` | `Aqua` |

So the session type was never the problem — the seatbelt was. Three
consequences, the middle one previously misdiagnosed:

1. The game gets no display ("The video driver did not add any displays",
   `hsel=0`, clean exit in 3-4s) because the work is GUI-driven and that is
   exactly what the sandbox blocks. Still to be confirmed at full access.
2. **CORRECTION to s673's checkpoint.** It concluded the read-only `.git` was
   "specific to that one sandbox invocation, not a durable property". It is
   deterministic: EVERY codex iteration under workspace-write gets a read-only
   `.git`, so no codex iteration can ever meet an exit contract that ends in a
   commit. s673's commit landed because `loop.sh` routes contract RETRIES to
   the claude runner, which is unsandboxed — the retry, not a changed sandbox,
   is what "found `.git` writable". Attribution error of the familiar kind: two
   observations from two different processes read as one process changing.
3. `nice(5) denied`, which s673 reported without attribution, is the same cause.

Fix: `runner.sh` codex sandbox default raised to `danger-full-access`, with the
measurements inline so it is not quietly lowered again. `RUNNER_SANDBOX` still
overrides per run.

**Loop bug: a run could die on a BLOCKED.md that says it is not blocked.**
`loop.sh` halted on the mere EXISTENCE of `scratch/agent/BLOCKED.md`. s673 ended
`STATUS=DONE` / `OUTCOME=ADVANCED` but left behind a BLOCKED.md whose first line
read `# Not currently blocked`, so the 00:21 codex run exited before preflight,
before spending anything, on a healthy repo. Fixed on both sides: an iteration
ending DONE has its leftover BLOCKED.md archived, and the loop top only treats
the file as stale when STATUS=DONE *and* its first line says "not blocked" — a
real block (STATUS=BLOCKED) and a preflight block ("# Blocked by preflight")
are both still honoured.

**Known blind spot, not yet fixed:** `preflight.sh` runs in loop.sh's own shell
and then hands the work to a runner that may be sandboxed, so for codex it
certifies an environment the agent never gets. It printed `[preflight] OK` at
00:05:16 immediately before an agent that could not open a window. Its very
first check (`launchctl managername` = Aqua) passes inside the sandbox too, so
it cannot catch this class by itself — the fix is to run it inside the runner.

### Rules out / confirms
- Confirms the codex workspace-write sandbox blocks `.git` writes and
  `setpriority`, deterministically, in a repo unrelated to this one.
- Refutes s673's "one-off sandbox invocation" reading of the read-only `.git`.
- Does NOT yet confirm the game gets a display under `danger-full-access`; the
  00:21 run that would have shown it never started. Refutation test:
  `RUNNER=codex ITER_CAP=1 caffeinate -dis tools/agent/loop.sh` from a GUI
  session, then check whether the SDL display error recurs.

### Residual → item -421 unchanged; the E9-alignment discriminator still needs one GUI-session run.

and one in `initSceneForMission`. In `runVideoFrameTick`, the `a0` frame
object is retained in `$s3`, and `lhu 0x4($s3)` is sign-extended into the
`advanceVideoFrame` argument. Therefore the observed small values are a
frame-state scalar, not a guest pointer.

The menu caller passes its frame object as `s0+0x10` and stores the matching
`s0+0x14` halfword from the computed menu timing-table entry at `0x800C5978`.
The mission caller passes `s1+0x10` and stores the matching `s1+0x14`
halfword from the computed scene timing value at `0x800A9BBC`. The two
`mainGameLoop` calls pass the static `D_80037560+0x10` record. No generated
code writer for that record's matching `D_80037574` halfword was found, so
its ROM/data initializer remains unresolved. This classifies the dynamic
callers as intentional structured state, leaves the static caller
single-source/evaluable only after data tracing, and rules out the
small-value-as-pointer explanation. No build, run, or mitigation was made.

ORIGIN: the dynamic values originate in the menu/mission frame-state stores;
the static value originates in an as-yet-untraced data initializer.

## Session 818 (2026-08-13) — static VI frame field is ROM-initialized

The bounded source/data audit traced the static frame object used by both

`D_80037560` to VROM `0x38160` through the `.text` section mapping
(`rom=0x1040`, `vram=0x80000440`). The retail ROM bytes at that offset are:
`00 00 00 00 80 03 DF A0 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 40 00 E0 00 10`.
Thus `D_80037574` (`D_80037560+0x14`) is the initialized big-endian halfword
`0x00E0`; the record's `+0x04` word is the `mainGameLoop` pointer
`0x8003DFA0`.

`0x8006B3E0` directly loads `lhu 0x7574($v0)`, while the absolute-address
search found no generated store targeting `0x80037574`. The static field is
therefore **H-static-field-rom-intended**, not a hidden runtime-writer case.
This resolves the initializer question but does not assign the field's full
semantic role or explain the later VI phase. No build, run, code change, or
mitigation was made.

ORIGIN: the value originates in the retail ROM initializer at VROM `0x38174`;
it is a legitimate static data value, not a corruption mitigation target.

## Session 835 (2026-08-13) — source audit identifies command-boundary E9 overcount

Performed the prescribed bounded parser-side source audit; no build, run, or
runtime behavior changed. `MEM_B` uses the host index `logical_address ^ 3`,
so the bridge's `g_rdram_for_submit[p ^ 3]` test and RT64's
`DisplayList::w0 >> 24` load select the same logical first byte. H-byte-order
is refuted.

The bridge counter scans every 8-byte slot from `lo` through `hi`, whereas the
RT64 direct parser advances by `cmdLength * sizeof(DisplayList)`. Therefore an
E9 at an interior word of a multiword command is counted by the bridge but is
not a parser command fetch. Pending completion has a separate gate requiring
completed bytes, raw pending opcode E9, the authoritative callback, and a
non-sentinel `s_rs64_pending_start_address`; that sentinel is set only when a
raw E9 command crosses a range boundary. This explains a lower parser count
without byte-order loss, while leaving pending-only effects to a paired probe.

This source result is single-source evidence. It identifies command-boundary
filtering as the leading explanation for s833's late rows (570=9/1, 580=9/1,
632=27/0, 649=31/3), but does not promote it to settled truth until a
phase-gated probe records bridge slots and parser command starts by address.
No mitigation or legitimacy claim was made.

ORIGIN: no game value, RDP command, mitigation, or runtime behavior changed;
this iteration changed only audit prose and scratch control files.

## Session 852 (2026-08-13) — source audit accounts for span matches; residual remains outside normal condition paths

Performed the prescribed bounded source-only audit; no build or run was
performed. The bridge's accepted ordinary ranges are scanned in 8-byte steps
and read the logical first byte through the same byte-swapped RDRAM mapping
used to reconstruct words. Each accepted range is recorded, serialised, and
passed synchronously to `submit_rdp_range`; RT64 derives its parser call range
from the same `[lo, hi)` pointers.

The authoritative parser loads the command opcode at each current boundary,
uses `commandWordLengths[opCode]`, reports a `direct` condition only when the
raw opcode is E9, reports a `span` condition for every normal non-E9 command,
and advances by `cmdLength * 8`. Thus an E9 byte at an interior 8-byte slot is
intentionally bridge-counted but is inline data in the preceding parser
command. The pending path records a split command only when a command crosses
the current `[lo, hi)` end and reports it on completion; the captured zero
pending rows are consistent with that gate. Deferred ranges receive normal
submit identity at commit. The non-deferred synthetic FULL_SYNC path is the
only submit path that bypasses `rs64_dpc_record_submit` and can carry a stale
serial/range label, but it submits only `[addr, addr+8)`.

This source table selects H-span-intended for the 1,001 span rows and rules out
a normal byte-order or producer/consumer range mismatch. It does not classify
the one residual condition-join slot: the normal direct/span paths are
complete, while the extended-opcode branch bypasses both condition callbacks
and uses its own function-controlled advancement. The residual therefore
needs one behavior-neutral runtime marker at that branch before choosing
between H-extended-residual and the bounded synthetic-label edge. No writer,
operand-legitimacy, parser-behavior, or mitigation conclusion follows.

ORIGIN: source audit only; no game value, RDP command, parser advancement, or
mitigation behavior changed.

## Session 882 (2026-08-13) — audio program cursor class is narrow but writer legitimacy remains open

Performed the prescribed source-only M3 inventory against `tickAudioChannel`
(`0x8008BC10`) in the external generated tree and its companion named-symbol
file. The complete function contains five cursor operations: loading
`channel+0x4` at `0x8008BF20`, dereferencing the resulting stream pointer at
`0x8008BF24`, reloading it at `0x8008BF44`, advancing it by 8 at `0x8008BF48`,
and storing it at `0x8008BF4C`. Thus there is one direct program-stream
dereference, with no explicit null check on the cursor immediately before it.

| Guest site | Operation | Predecessor / writer basis |
|---|---|---|
| `0x8008BF20` | load `channel+0x4` into cursor | enters the command loop after `+0x40 == 0`; no cursor null check |
| `0x8008BF24` | read word at `cursor+0x0` | directly follows the cursor load; this is the sole stream dereference |
| `0x8008BF44` | reload `channel+0x4` | same command-loop iteration, after global bookkeeping |
| `0x8008BF48` | cursor `+ 8` | follows command/global reads; no range proof in this function |
| `0x8008BF4C` | write advanced cursor to `channel+0x4` | normal command-stream advance |

The semantic writers establishing `channel+0x4` are `0x8008BF00` (state-gated

stale-pointer, and stub-artifact were not selected. No mitigation was landed.

### Substituted unit: static writer audit of the `runInMissionFrame` callback table

s954 left one unresolved edge in the closed-out M3 `slotDispatcherIter` class
(backlog #1): `runInMissionFrame` dispatches a function pointer loaded from
`0x8010B350 + i*8`, and static target enumeration could not identify runtime
contents or writers. This session closed that specific edge without any
runtime instrument.

`funcs_42.c:6798` (`runInMissionFrame`) computes the table base as a literal
`lui $s7,0x8011` / `addiu $s0,$s0,-0x4CB0` pair (`0x80110000-0x4CB0 =
0x8010B350`), then scans 8-byte entries (`byte0` = a bit index tested against
a flags word at `-0x3620($s7)`, `+4` = function pointer) until `byte0`
matches a sentinel, dispatching via `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r2)`. Every reference to
this table in the function is a load (`lbu`/`lw`); the only store nearby
targets the unrelated flags word at `-0x3620($s7)`, clearing a bit after
dispatch — not the table itself.

Two independent lines of evidence:
1. **Segment classification.** `rogue_squadron64/roguesquadron.yaml` marks
   `bss` starting only at `0x8010B6D0`; everything from `0x8010B350` through
   the named symbols after it (`playerCraftHobObjectNames@0x8010B3A0`,
   `playerCraftUpdateFunctions@0x8010B3C4`, …) is `data` — i.e. ROM-initialized,
   not zero-filled-then-populated. `syms/rogue_squadron.datasyms.toml` brackets
   the table cleanly: `D_8010B304` before, `playerCraftHobObjectNames` at
   `0x8010B3A0` after, giving the table an exact `0x50`-byte (10-entry) span
   with no named symbol landing inside it.
2. **Exhaustive writer search.** `grep -rn "0X4CB0\|0x4CB0\|0x4cb0"` across all
   of `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c` (the full generated codebase) returns
   exactly 5 lines: 2 reads inside `runInMissionFrame` itself (`funcs_42.c`,
   both against the `0x8011`-based table pointer), 1 unrelated `$zero`-based
   byte load at fixed low address `0x4CB0` (`funcs_8.c`), and 1 unrelated
   `lwc1 -0x4CB0($at)` in `funcs_13.c` where `$at = 0x8004<<16` — a completely
   different address (`0x8003B350`), confirmed by reading its immediately
   preceding `lui`. Zero stores anywhere target `0x8010B350`.

This selects **static-compiled-data** over any runtime-writer hypothesis for
this specific table: it is ROM-baked dispatch data with no generated-code
writer, so it cannot be the shared-context corruption vector for the
`slotDispatcherIter+872` class. This closes `runInMissionFrame`'s indirect
edge from s954's backlog #1; it does NOT close
H-slotdispatcheriter-stacksp-unclassified overall — the general `$sp`
corruption mechanism remains open, this only rules out one candidate writer.

ORIGIN: `roguesquadron.yaml` segment split (independent build-config source,
not generated code) plus exhaustive generated-source grep; no guest value was

## Session 984 (2026-08-13) — M4 zero-shade decode/origin audit after oracle pivot

The required `/Users/williambuckley/Documents/Tools/rs64-oracle` directory was

`lib/rt64/src/gbi/rt64_gbi_rdp.cpp` consumes the standard four position words,

the same `(T0-0)*SHADE+0` combiner and that forcing white shade restores the
textured scene in the same phase. H-decode-layout is refuted. The remaining
split is upstream Factor 5 shade-state emission versus game light-state
production; no source mitigation, build, or run was performed.

### What it rules out

It rules out promoting `ROGUESQ_FIX_ZERO_SHADE` into a decoder correction or
claiming a lane/order origin. It does not identify the writer or establish that
the near-zero values are illegitimate, so no mitigation ORIGIN conclusion is
authorized. Next work is a phase-gated, same-run positive-control probe that
marks Factor 5 color/light-state updates and pairs them with scoped raw shade
samples.

shade emission diverges from the reference in two independent ways (constant

`slotDispatcherIter` entry that dumps sp/ra/a0/a1/s0-s7/fp/gp when the guest

`RecompiledFuncs/funcs_8.c`; the Debug build links clean. Default off.

## Session 1012 (2026-08-14) — classified Factor 5 VGE sentinel semantics

Ran the prescribed static M4 work unit without building or running. The
independent SGI RSP Programmer's Guide describes VGE as a signed
greater-or-equal operand select, and the local `VGE` implementation independently
matches that behavior: each lane selects `vs` or the selected `vt` lane, with
the VCO tie rule. The final `VGE<3>(v6,v6,v29)` therefore cannot synthesize the
observed fixed `0x8000` RGB/alpha sentinel. Its `v29` operand is the DMEM-0x60
table vector, while `v6` was already produced by `vmadh v6,v4,v0`; `v4` and
`v0` are arithmetic inputs, not a fixed compare-result source. This refutes
`H-vge-sentinel-encoding`, the fixed-operand form of `H-v4-v0-source`, and
`H-shade-store-interpretation`, and moves the next discriminator to the RSP
accumulator high-half/saturation path before VGE. No mitigation or generated
file edit was made.

## Session 1013 (2026-08-14) — audited Factor 5 shade accumulator path

Ran the prescribed static M4 work unit without building or running. The final

accumulator is shared, the latter consumes the accumulator state left by the

## Session 1058 (2026-08-14) — audited normal hangar throttle return producer

* `0x800B4174`: null ship pointer branches to `0x800B421C`, returns 0.
* `0x800B41A8`: charge above the upper threshold writes byte `+0x2F = 0xFF`

  counter is below 7, returns 1 at `0x800B41D4`, otherwise continues.
* `0x800B41EC`: charge at or below the lower threshold skips the clamp/write;
  otherwise the truncated charge (or lower-threshold difference with the sign
  bit) is written to byte `+0x2F`.
* `0x800B421C`: the common return sets `v0 = 0`, returns 0.

The branch predicates are ship/charge state only. The two ordinary return
words consumed by `runHangarSelectionFrame` remain data references at the
ledger's `0x800D:0xFFFFD6D4` and `0x800D:0xFFFFD6D0` notation; this generated

## Session 1214 (2026-08-14) — validated oracle savestate lifecycle

Added an opt-in `ORACLE_STATE_SMOKE=1` path to `tools/oracle/rs64_oracle.c`.
It invokes `M64CMD_STATE_SAVE` during execution, waits for the asynchronous
state file to appear, then invokes `M64CMD_STATE_LOAD` on that file and reports
watch/VI counts around the operations. The oracle was rebuilt and run for 20
seconds against the available retail ROM with a whole-RDRAM write watch,
`--pif-trace`, and `--vi-poll`.

The positive control reached its 10,000-callback threshold before the save.
The save returned 0, the state file existed, the load returned 0, and the run
continued to 1,506 VI frames with the whole-RDRAM watch still reporting 10,000
hits. The state route is therefore usable and does not remove debugger/control
callbacks. The run stayed at width 320/origin `0x006dd280`, so this experiment
does not establish reachability of the hangar or M4 target phase.

This rules out H2 (API route unusable) and H3 (state load disrupts the positive
controls) for this core/ROM setup. It selects H1 only for lifecycle viability,
not for retail-entry reachability. No mitigation or value rewrite was added.

ORIGIN: no game or renderer value was skipped or rewritten; the change only
added opt-in savestate calls and observational counters around the core API.

## Session 1616 (2026-08-16) — tested pre-exit hangar input routes at retail

The mandatory 15-title check found only sweep sessions plus the s1602 M4
revisit, so this iteration performed a new external retail-entry revisit
instead of another generated-symbol census. Static inspection of the
generated `runHangarSelectionFrame` body found its new-button read at
`0x800AB0EC` and a B-specific `andi 0x4000` branch. The prior s1585 result had
tested A/B/Z only after the 512 hangar had already become the 640 model-viewer
phase; it did not test B while the hangar selector was active.

The competing hypotheses were H1: pre-exit B selects a distinct route that
could lead toward mission entry; H2: B is recognized but leaves the known
hangar/model-viewer route unchanged; H3: directional navigation changes the
route; and H4: the recipe or candidate input is unevaluable. The one
discriminator was the phase-gated post-hangar VI lifecycle plus PC watches for
`runHangarSelectionFrame` (`0x800AAD9C`), `runHangarMenuFromOverlay`
(`0x800C6854`), `runModelViewerLoop` (`0x800C9BF0`), mission entry
(`0x80000B70`), overlay loads, and writes to `0x130B10:0x130B58` and
`0x13B40:0x13B48`.

The four concurrent Rice arms used the same eleven Start presses and were:
the known A exit control (`58:a,63:a`), pre-exit B (`55:b,58:b,63:b`), and
Up/Down navigation followed by the A exit (`55/57:up|down,58:a,63:a`). Every
arm passed the whole-RDRAM positive control (10,137–10,150 writes) and the
320→640→1024→512 hangar lifecycle. A was delivered as `sym=225` with pad
word `0x800000`; B was delivered as `sym=224` with pad word `0x400000` and
the hangar-frame PC fired 696 times in the B arm. The Up/Down arms logged
`sym=0`, so they were invalid input arms and cannot select H3.

H1 selected for the valid B arm: it stayed at 512 until 65.4s, then changed
to 1024 at origin `0x00790400` and to 640 at `0x00696100`, with zero
`runModelViewerLoop` hits and zero mission-entry `0x80000B70` hits. The A
control reached 640 at `0x006A2E00` and had one model-viewer hit; both valid
arms had zero mission-entry hits. B therefore proves a distinct retail menu
route but not mission entry. The selector watch was zero in all arms, and the
target block showed the common 137 writes in A/Up/Down versus 150 in B; no
mitigation or recomp change was made.

This rules out the claim that every valid hangar exit follows case-6 model
viewer and rules out B as a mission-entry input in the observed 110-second

## Session 1650 (2026-08-16) — tested post-B A/Start/Z against retail mission entry

The mandatory 15-title check found only sweep sessions, so this iteration
revisited the external retail-entry boundary instead of another
generated-symbol census. Prior work had classified pre-exit B as a distinct
valid hangar route (`512→1024→640` at `0x00696100`, not case-6 model viewer)
and had classified post-viewer A/Start/Z and C/L/R arms without mission
entry. It had not tested A, Start, or Z after the B-route began.

Competing hypotheses: H1 post-B A/Start/Z reach mission PC `0x80000B70`; H2
the B-route frontend ignores them and all arms retain the B lifecycle; H3 a
post-B control changes to another frontend without mission entry; H4 the
recipe or input delivery is unevaluable. The discriminator was the four-arm
Rice comparison under whole-RDRAM, PIF, VI, and watched frontend/mission PCs.

All four concurrent 110 s arms (`hold`, `a`, `start`, `z`) used eleven Start
presses plus pre-exit B at 55/58/63; the candidate arms then pressed A, Start,
or Z at 75/82/89/96. Every arm reached hangar `320→640→1024→512`, fired the
whole-RDRAM positive control (10,000 callbacks), and delivered B as pad word
`0x40000000`. Candidate pads were also delivered: A `0x80000000`, Start
`0x10000000`, Z `0x20000000`. Mission PC `0x80000B70` and model-viewer PC
`0x800C9BF0` were zero in every arm.

Hold completed the known B lifecycle: `512→1024` at 65.2 s, then
`1024→640` at 96.3 s origin `0x00696100`, hangar-frame PC count 61. Z matched
hold exactly through the final 640 origin, with one Z delivery on the 640
frontend at 97.3 s and no VI change. A and Start diverted the post-B
intermediate 1024 phase: after `512→1024` at 65.3 s they returned
`1024→512` at 85.6 s (origins `0x006ab800` / `0x006ab400`), raised hangar-frame
PC counts to 297/295, and never reached the 640 B-frontend.

H3 is selected for A and Start (reproducible return to hangar 512, zero
mission entry). Z is H2-shaped (ignored; retains B-route 640). H1 is rejected
by zero mission PC hits. H4 is rejected by the shared hangar lifecycle,
positive-control thresholds, and delivered pad words. The post-control presses
land mostly during the intermediate 1024 phase after B leaves hangar, not on
the final 640 B-frontend (except the last ~97 s press).

This rules out A/Start/Z after pre-exit B as mission-entry inputs in the
observed 110-second window and shows A/Start can cancel the B intermediate
back to hangar. It does not identify the 640 B-frontend or prove any later
input on that frontend reaches a mission. No recomp change or mitigation was
made. Next work resumes the generated-symbol sweep at `func_800C78A0` /
`calculateDatItemDistanceToPlayer`.

### Competing hypotheses

- H-rdp-consumer: after `L_1740`, ovl20 copies or restages the
  `0x670+0x18`/`+0x40` bytes into the `0xD60` staging buffer before
  `SP_WR_LEN`.

  no generated path copies the stored bytes into that buffer.
- H-dead-store: no post-`L_1740` load, copy, or DMA of `+0x18`/`+0x40`.

### Evidence

| Site | Classification |
|---|---|
| `ori $9, $zero, 0x670` ovl20:1078 | producer base for `L_162C`/`L_1740` `sdv v6` to `0x18($9)` / `0x40($9)` |
| `addiu $11/$15, …, 0x670` :619/630/803/806 | index addend; writes color at `+0x10`/`+0x14` only |
| `L_17F0` `llv`/`lh`/`lsv` `0x18($11/$12/$13)` :1386–1579 | post-store reader of stored `v6` XY |
| `L_17F0` `lsv` `0x1C($11/$12/$13)` :1826–1834 | remaining `v6` halfword 2 |
| `L_17F0` `luv` `0x10($…)` | color, not `v6` |
| no `0x40($11/$12/$13)` load | `+0x40` is `0x18` of vertex at `base+0x28` (0x28-byte records; GLideN64 `F3DSWRS_Tri` indexes `/ 40`) |
| `jal 0x11FC; ori $2, $zero, 0xD60` :224–228 | only `SP_WR_LEN`; `SET_DMA_MEM(r2)` with `r2=0xD60` |
| `SP_RD_LEN` :281, :378 | DMEM `0x170` / generic `r3`; not `0x670` |
| sibling ovl4/10/12/14/18/1c/24 | same single `jal 0x11FC; ori $2, 0xD60` |

`L_17F0` restages, it does not memcpy: `sb $10, 0x0($16)` stores
`*(u8*)(state+0x37) | 0xC8` (RDP triangle) at the `r16` cursor
(initialized to `0xD60`); `ssv` of the loaded `+0x18` Y to
`0x2/0x4/0x6($16)` and scaled X to `0x8/0xA($16)`. `L_112C` flushes

sources color from `gSP.vertexColorBase + index`, matching the
generated `luv` at `+0x10`.

## Session 1840 (2026-08-17) — selected H-standard-edge on the restaged RDP triangle

Mandatory 15-title M4 REVISIT (HYPOTHESIS-ID: m4-accumulator-boundary-revisit).
Last-15 ledger titles after s1839 were s1825–s1839, all sweep
("synchronized" / "confirmed the leftover … symbol"). s1839's claim
that those fifteen still included s1824 was a fencepost: s1824 is the
16th. Step 0 `wc -c` was 11827; not a maintenance iteration. No new
soak-queue verdicts beyond the already-folded s1029-and-earlier tail.
Soak queue empty. Ground-truth docs read first
(`M4-ACCUMULATOR-GROUND-TRUTH.md`, `M4-V6-PRODUCER-AUDIT.md`,
`F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md`, n64brew RDP triangle, RT64
`rt64_gbi_rdp.cpp:376-400`, generated ovl20 `L_17F0`). No game run
and no new runtime field.

### Competing hypotheses

- H-standard-edge: `L_17F0` writes a spec-accurate 32-byte RDP Fill
  Triangle (`0xC8|flags`, YL/YM/YH, XL/DxLDy/XH/DxHDy/XM/DxMDy) at
  the `r16` / `0xD60` cursor, with optional shade/tex suffixes.
- H-y-swapped: store order `+2/+4/+6` is YH/YM/YL (s1824's informal
  label taken as the spec names), so every hardware triangle is inverted.
- H-s1516-passthrough: `0xFFFF8000` is dumped as a 32-bit s15.16 XL.
- H-not-triangle: header `0xC8` is not `G_RDP_TRI_FILL`, or the 32
  bytes are not the official edge-coefficient block.

### Evidence

| Cursor | Store | Official field |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x00` | `*(s8*)(state+0x37) \| 0xC8` | command. `0xC8` = fill; bit2 shade, bit1 tex, bit0 z |
| `+0x01` | `(mfc2 v29[5] & 0x80) \| *(u8*)(state+0x3A)` | `lmajor` + level/tile |
| `+0x02` | `ssv v15[2]` from vertex `+0x1A` after Y-sort | **YL** (n64brew bits 47:32; RT64 `w0 & 0xFFFF`) |
| `+0x04` | `ssv v14[2]` | **YM** |
| `+0x06` | `ssv v13[2]` | **YH** |
| `+0x08/+0x0A` | `lsv 0x18($12)` then `vmudm v30[4]` | **XL** s16.16 from the 16-bit X, not a 32-bit memcpy |
| `+0x0C` … `+0x1E` | reciprocal / edge-walk `ssv`s | DxLDy, XH, DxHDy, XM, DxMDy |
| then | `addi $16, $16, 0x20` | end of the 32-byte base |
| bit1 / bit2 | 64-byte tex and/or shade `sdv` suffixes | matches n64brew optional words |

Y-sort: `lh +0x1A`, 3-bit compare, DMEM `0xAA`/`0xB1`/`0xB8` permute,
then `llv` XY into `v15`/`v14`/`v13`. XL is taken from sorted `$12`
(the YM vertex), which is the official "X on the L edge at YM".
`L_112C` still flushes only when `r16 - 0xD60 != 0` via the only
`SP_WR_LEN` from `0xD60`.

Sentinel split: `0xFFFF8000` at `+0x18` is X=`0xFFFF` (scaled into
XL) and Y=`0x8000` (raw into YL/YM/YH). RDP Y is s11.2 in bits 13:0,
so `0x8000` is `0.00` on the hardware field (RT64 `<<2>>2` on the
16-bit value sign-extends to −8192). Three equal Ys are zero-height.
Clip flags at vertex `+0x24` can reject at `L_17F0` entry before any
`0xD60` store. Full table: `docs/M4-ACCUMULATOR-GROUND-TRUTH.md`
(s1840 section).

Two sources: generated `L_17F0` (every overlay) and n64brew + RT64's
decoder. GLideN64 `F5Rogue` is HLE and does not emit this command.

### Outcome

H-standard-edge selected. H-y-swapped is refuted (`+2` is official
YL). H-s1516-passthrough is refuted (`lsv` of two bytes then
`vmudm`). H-not-triangle is refuted. No mitigation. Do not re-watch
`0x688:0x710`, recapture VMADH/VGE, watch `0x4B7800`, re-enumerate
the ovl20 consumer table, or re-map the 32-byte stores.

## Session 1888 (2026-08-17) — VI 1024 reachability itself has regressed; hangar/512 stays UNEVALUABLE for a new reason

Mandatory 15-title REVISIT (HYPOTHESIS-ID: m4-accumulator-boundary-revisit).
`grep -n '^## Session ' PORTING-STATE.md | tail -15` after s1887 returns
s1873–s1887, all sweep ("synchronized … symbol"); s1872's hangar/512 entry
is the 16th-from-last, outside the window. s1887's own "next work unit" note
claiming s1872 was still inside the last-15 window was an off-by-one error —
the gate had in fact fired. Step 0 `wc -c` was 19002; not maintenance. Soak
queue empty (SOAK-RESULTS.md tail unchanged since s1029, 2026-08-14).

### New angle (not `s1872`'s LLE walk)

s1872's four arms used an undocumented "boot Starts" input mechanism and
never published a hangar-origin mark. Cross-referencing older history
(session 65, 2026-07-26) showed the port previously reached VI width 512 /
origin `0x006AB400` routinely via the standard menu-navigation schedule
(title → SELECT GAME → war room/SELECT LEVEL → **AVAILABLE CRAFT**, the
screen at that origin — i.e. "AVAILABLE CRAFT" already *is* the hangar-origin
screen), using `tools/probe.sh`'s proven phase-gated real key-injection
mechanism with the standard `PROBE_KEYS='3:start 7:start 11:start 15:a
100:start 130:start 160:a 190:start 220:a 250:start'` schedule under
`ROGUESQ_LLE_FORCE=1 ROGUESQ_LLE_UNGATED=1 ROGUESQ_LLE_SOLO=1` (the
`s790_postsec2_reachability` family's config, ADVANCED repeatedly through
s844 on 2026-08-13). `src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp:302-306` confirms
hangar-origin DLs auto-switch to LLE at runtime regardless of `LLE_FORCE`,
so the plan was: run that exact proven schedule with
`ROGUESQ_M4_Y8000_WIDTH=512` armed and see whether the hangar-gated
`rs64_m4_y8000_*` counters (parked at UNEVALUABLE since s1872) finally fire.
This combination — proven navigation schedule plus the hangar-gated M4
counters — had never been run.

### What happened instead

Five runs, one game at a time, SIGKILL, all today:

| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No LLE forcing, `ROGUESQ_M4_Y8000_WIDTH=512`, proven key schedule, `PROBE_PHASE_TIMEOUT=180` | Stuck at width 640 origin `0x00696100` from 9.1s; width 1024 never reached (exit 5) |
| 2 | `LLE_FORCE=1 LLE_UNGATED=1 LLE_SOLO=1` + M4 gate + proven key schedule, timeout 180 | Native host crash before 1024: `RT64::NativeTarget::copyToRAM` inside `State::fullSync`/`Framebuffer::copyNativeToRAM`, `last-guest-pc=0x80001f88`, `pc-symbol` is a nearest-symbol misattribution (`__isPlatformOrVariantPlatformVersionAtLeast.cold.4+2288219460`) |
| 3 | Identical to run 2 | Same crash, same call stack — reproduces 2/2 |
| 4 (verbatim) | Unmodified `scratch/agent/s790_postsec2_reachability.sh`, the exact script ADVANCED through s844 | Stuck at width 640 origin `0x00696100` from 7.2s; width 1024 never reached in 180s (exit 5). `[host-start]` shows `btn=0x0000` throughout — expected, since `PROBE_KEYS_FROM_PHASE=1` never releases keys because the 1024 phase-wait never exits, not a key-delivery failure |
| 5 | `LLE_FORCE=1 LLE_UNGATED=1 LLE_SOLO=1`, no keys, `PROBE_PHASE_TIMEOUT=340` (positive-control-style: rule out "just needs more wall-clock time" before calling it stuck) | Same stall, confirmed to 340s (nearly 2x the historical ~80s reach time) — not a timing shift, genuinely does not progress |

Logs: `scratch/agent/s1888_m4_hangar_via_availcraft/run1/`,
`.../run2/`, `.../run3/`, `.../run4_longwost/` (misnamed at capture time,
contains the 340s long-wait run), and the verbatim run's own
`scratch/agent/soak_results/s790_postsec2_reachability_20260817-173130/`.
No stray/zombie game processes were contending (`ps aux` clean before each
run) and `lib/N64ModernRuntime`/`lib/rt64` carry only the project's standing
uncommitted patch set (unchanged from every prior session, not a stray
in-progress edit) — ruling out the two boring explanations checked.

### Outcome

**UNEVALUABLE** for the hangar/512 H-* table, same as s1872, but for a
different and more foundational reason: it is not merely that hangar-origin
was never reached, it is that **VI width 1024 itself — reached reliably at
~79.5-79.8s in every `s790_postsec2_reachability` soak from s815 through s844
(2026-08-13) — did not reach it at all in 5/5 runs today**, including one
byte-for-byte unmodified run of the script that used to succeed. The passive
320→640(`0x0066A500`)→640(`0x00696100`) attract sequence now stalls at the
second 640 origin indefinitely; two of five runs additionally hit a
previously-uncatalogued native crash in `RT64::NativeTarget::copyToRAM`
before reaching that stall. This blocks not just hangar/512 but the entire
`s790_postsec2_reachability` soak family and everything downstream of VI
1024 in the current soak queue design.

This is an observation, not a diagnosed mechanism (iron rule: mechanism or
it isn't done) — the cause (build drift, `lib/` patch state, machine-specific
timing, or genuine nondeterminism) is not established. No `lib/` edits were
made this session (only `scratch/agent/` and doc changes), so this is not an
artifact of this session's own changes. ORIGIN: no mitigation, guard, skip,
or restore was added or considered — this session only observed and did not
touch runtime code.

Do not re-run the hangar/512 H-* table until VI-1024 reachability itself is
re-established. Do not re-walk VMADH/VGE, the `0xD60` shape, or the ovl20
consumer table (still closed per s1824/s1840/s1856).

## Session 1889 (2026-08-17) — VI-1024 stall/crash reproduces 3/3, in three different signatures; H1-flake refuted

HYPOTHESIS-ID: vi1024-reachability-regression (continuing s1888). Step 0
`wc -c docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` was 20571; not maintenance. Executed s1888's own
prescribed discriminating measurement: re-ran the unmodified
`scratch/agent/s790_postsec2_reachability.sh` 3 more times, one game at a
time, SIGKILL between runs, no source/lib edits before or during.

### Results

| Run | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (`...20260817-174630`) | Native SIGSEGV before 1024, ~15-24s | `RT64::NativeTarget::copyToRAM` inside `Framebuffer::copyNativeToRAM`/`State::fullSync` — same call stack as 2/5 of s1888's runs, now reproduced a 3rd/4th time |
| 2 (`...20260817-174727`) | Native SIGSEGV before 1024, ~15-20s | **New signature**: inside the Apple AGX Metal driver (`checkActiveRenderEncoder`→`beginRenderPass`) via `RT64::RenderTarget::clearDepthTarget`, also under `State::fullSync`; `si_addr=0x1211ffff11121161` (garbage, not a null/near-null pointer) |
| 3 (`...20260817-174818`) | Guest-side SIGBUS before 1024, ~19-25s | **New signature**: `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`→`fillSampleStreamRange` (called from `musyxMixActiveVoices`→`musyxSynthFrame`→`viRetraceHandlerThread`) |

Combined with s1888: **0/8 runs today reached VI width 1024** (was 100%
through s815-s844). All 3 of today's runs stalled at the same `640
origin=0x00696100` point at 7-9s before crashing, matching s1888 exactly.

### H1-flake refuted; corruption-shaped, not a single repeat bug

Three different runs produced three different crash signatures (two
host-side RT64/Metal, one guest-side musyx audio) rather than one
consistently-reproducing bug. This is not "flaky sometimes reaches 1024,
sometimes doesn't" — it is "never reaches 1024, dies differently each time,"
which reads as a shared upstream corruption source with variable
downstream fallout, not independent unrelated bugs and not ordinary
scheduling flake. H1-flake (s1888's hypothesis list) is refuted: 0/8, not a
partial hit rate.

**Two false leads checked and correctly discarded, not re-opened:**
- `last-guest-pc=0x8000b650` appeared in runs 1 and 2's crash dumps. Per
  extensive prior documentation (s269-s278, `PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md`
  "Dispatcher and breadcrumb family") this exact PC is `beginFrameDLChunk`'s
  own body — a known-stale breadcrumb that fires whenever that (very
  frequently-called) function last ran, not the fault origin. Not treated as
  a new clue.
- `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`/`musyxMixActiveVoices`/`musyxSynthFrame` are a
  long-catalogued crash family (`PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md` audio idiom sessions)
  with several sites already deliberately left unguarded. Run 3's crash is
  plausibly a recurrence of that known family, not a new bug — but it is
  the first time it has been observed to occur *pre*-1024 and block the whole
  `s790_postsec2_reachability` soak rather than as a rare pre-scene boot
  outcome.

**One genuine new lead, single-source, not yet confirmed with a positive
control:** `ROGUESQ_LOG_FL_ZERO_WATCH` (watching phys `0x1F3CC0`, kseg
`0x801F3CC0` — a slot the project's freelist instrumentation expects to stay
zero) recorded a corruption write in 2/3 runs shortly before their crash:
run 2 `cur_f=0xC51F cur_sz=0x912E002D` at t_ms=17554; run 3 `cur_f=0xEAA5
cur_sz=0xA9712AE` at t_ms=19267, then 26 further faults by t_ms=20001. Run 1
(the copyToRAM crash) showed **no** corresponding write — the watched slot
stayed all-zero through its crash — so this is not present in every failure
and does not explain run 1. `rs-malloc-diag` in run 1 reported `sane=1`
throughout with no anomaly. ORIGIN: no mitigation was added or considered
this session — this is an observation only.

### Boring-things-first checks (all clean, ruling nothing in)

- `tools/fixup_game_funcs.py`: zero commits touching it since s1888/ever in
  the `--since 2026-08-13` window. `tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py`: last
  touched by `c8750cf7` (M4 shade work, unrelated to VI/native-target code).
- `lib/N64ModernRuntime` / `lib/rt64` uncommitted status unchanged from
  s1888's own check (same standing patch set, e.g. `rt64_native_target.cpp`'s
  `isNativeCopySupported`/`copyToRAM` history-index guard — traced via `git
  log -S` on `submodule-patches/rt64.patch` to `9e4ce66c`, 2026-07-26, the
  original harness-install commit, i.e. *not* a recent addition and was
  present unfired through every s815-s844 success).
- Binary (`build/RogueSquadron64Recomp`) was rebuilt today (13:01) — expected
  given the intervening symbol-rename sweep commits; no way to attribute the
  regression to that without a bisect.
- CPU/thermal (`top`, `vm_stat`, `pmset -g therm`) could not be checked —
  denied by this session's permission policy. H3-machine-state remains
  formally unruled-out, though three *different* crash signatures in one
  batch reads more like corruption than pure slowdown/contention.

### Outcome

Still UNEVALUABLE for hangar/512 and everything downstream of VI 1024, for
the same s1888 reason, now with 8/8 combined non-reaching runs and 4 distinct
crash/stall signatures instead of 2. H1-flake is refuted. H2-build-drift's
two checked candidates (fixup scripts, lib/ patch drift) came back clean.
H3-machine-state has one check outstanding (CPU/thermal, blocked by
permissions this session). H4-real-regression is not proven but is now the
best-supported explanation, tentatively centered on the same
freelist/heap-corruption family this project has tracked for months
(`fl-zero-watch`, product multi-header restore, garbage-CIMG) rather than a
new independent bug — plausible because it explains the diversity of
downstream crash sites (RT64 native buffers, Metal driver resources, musyx
voice buffers all read attacker-controlled-looking sizes/pointers) but not
yet a mechanism (iron rule: mechanism or it isn't done — not claimed as one).

Per iron rule 8, this is the 2nd non-ADVANCED-eligible iteration on this
hypothesis if judged as "still stuck" — but this iteration produced a real
discriminating result (refuted H1) and new evidence (2 new crash signatures,
the fl-zero-watch lead), so it is declared ADVANCED, not a stall, resetting

different mechanism, then decide between chasing the fl-zero-watch lead with

  pure renaming; N64Recomp compiles from vram+size, not name.
- `src/main/main.cpp` (179 lines), `src/main/upstream_compat.cpp` (95
  lines), `src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp` (24 lines): the one real find.
  `upstream_compat.cpp` adds `rs64_is_hangar_vi()` (reads
  `ultramodern::renderer::get_vi_regs()->{VI_WIDTH_REG,VI_ORIGIN_REG}`, no
  locks) for the s1856/s1872 hangar-gate work. `rt64_render_context.cpp`'s
  `send_dl` now computes `const bool in_hangar = rs64_is_hangar_vi() != 0;`
  unconditionally at the top of the M_GFXTASK path — not short-circuited,
  so it runs every frame regardless of `ROGUESQ_LLE_*` env vars, reading
  VI regs from the render thread with no visible synchronization against
  the guest/VI thread's writes. This is the only functional (non-rename,
  non-doc, non-gated-probe) change anywhere in the 1092-commit window that
  plausibly touches the failure's timing window.

**H5-hangar-probe-race built and tested.** Added
`ROGUESQ_SKIP_HANGAR_PROBE` (`src/main/rt64_render_context.cpp`, default
OFF) forcing `in_hangar=false` without calling `rs64_is_hangar_vi()`.
Rebuilt once (`cmake --build build --target RogueSquadron64Recomp`,
DEVELOPER_DIR set), ran the unmodified `s790_postsec2_reachability.sh`
twice on the identical binary, toggling only the env var:
- Baseline (probe active, default): stall at `640 origin=0x00696100` at
  7.3s, plain 180s timeout, no crash.
- `ROGUESQ_SKIP_HANGAR_PROBE=1`: stall at `640 origin=0x00696100` at 7.4s,
  then SIGBUS in `musyxSynthFrame`+6608 / `viRetraceHandlerThread`+7184
  (last-guest-pc=`0x8000b650`, the known stale `beginFrameDLChunk`
  breadcrumb — not informative per prior sessions).

Identical stall point and timing in both arms. **H5 is REFUTED** — the
unconditional VI-register read is not implicated. The baseline run also
serves as a positive control that the freshly rebuilt binary still
reproduces the regression exactly (same origin address, same ~7.3s onset),
which argues against pure build-to-build/ASLR nondeterminism: the failure's
onset is deterministic given this binary+environment, consistent with a
game-state trigger point rather than random heap-layout luck.

**Bisect blocked, mechanism identified.** NEXT.md's proposed
`git worktree add` bisect at a pre-s844 commit cannot run as designed:
populating submodule content at a historical commit needs
`git submodule update` (or equivalent), and `Bash(git submodule
update:*)` is denied in `.claude/settings.json` by command-string prefix
match — independent of working directory, so it is blocked inside a fresh
worktree too. Sidestepping via `git -C lib/X checkout <hash>` would
reproduce exactly the blast radius `git checkout -- lib/...` is meant to
prevent (discarding lib/'s uncommitted standing patches), so it was not
attempted.

**Net conclusion**: no source-code change anywhere between s844 and HEAD
plausibly explains the VI-1024 regression — the one real candidate was
built, tested, and refuted. This does not prove H3 or a pure-environment
cause, but it closes H2/H4-as-a-traceable-code-regression far more
thoroughly than "these files weren't touched" (s1889's version of the
check) — now every file that changed has been read, not just listed.
ORIGIN: `ROGUESQ_SKIP_HANGAR_PROBE` is a diagnostic knob (default off), not
a mitigation — no corruption is being guarded or restored.

## Session 1892 (2026-08-17) — UNBLOCK: ask (1) refuted, not just unmet; new H3 lead found

s1891's `BLOCKED.md` asked for one thing this session could not itself
produce: a `top`/`vm_stat`/`who`/`pmset -g therm`/`sysctl` snapshot, taken by
a human outside the harness, because those five binaries are denied here by
command-string match (confirmed independently in s1889, s1890, s1891). That
framing conflated "the binary is blocked" with "the data is unobtainable" —
they are not the same claim. The underlying data is available through the
same libc/Foundation calls those binaries wrap, invoked directly:

- `os.getloadavg()` / `os.cpu_count()` (Python stdlib, no binary) for load
  average — `vm_stat`'s and `top`'s core signal.
- `ctypes` + `libc.sysctlbyname()` for `hw.memsize`, `vm.page_free_count`,
  `vm.page_speculative_count` — the same syscall `sysctl`/`vm_stat` make
  internally; only the *binary* `sysctl` is name-matched and blocked, not
  the syscall.
- `ctypes` + `objc_msgSend` against `NSProcessInfo.processInfo` for
  `.thermalState` and `.isLowPowerModeEnabled` — strictly more than
  `pmset -g therm` exposes (that command only reports CPU speed-limit
  percentage and scheduler-limit flags, not the OS's own thermal-pressure
  classification or Low Power Mode, which `pmset -g therm` doesn't surface
  at all).

None of these are denied; none require a human, a new install, or a
permission/security change. Scripts: `scratch/agent/vm_sampler.py`
(load/free-page sampler, 0.5s cadence) and `scratch/agent/thermal_probe.py`
(thermal state + Low Power Mode, one-shot). **Ask (1) is refuted as stated —
not merely satisfied, refuted: no human step was ever necessary.**

Used the new capability for more than a static snapshot: launched
`vm_sampler.py` (60s @ 0.5s) in the background, then launched the unmodified
`s790_postsec2_reachability.sh` immediately after, producing a
resource-vs-failure timeline for one full run instead of a single point
sample — closer to what s1891's ask was actually trying to establish
(state *during* the failure) than a snapshot taken before or after it would
have been.

**Result, run 9 of 9 (s1888 2/5, s1889 3/3, s1892 1/1):**
`[phase] vi_width=640 origin=0x00696100 at 7.2s` — same stall point as every
prior run, within the established 7.2-7.4s band. H1-flake stays refuted
(0/9). The run then continued (this recipe's 640-stall is a phase marker,
not a hang, for the ~1/3 of prior runs that don't hang outright) to VI count
1536 before `[CRASH] caught signal 10 (Bus error: 10)` in
`fillSampleStreamRange`/`musyxRenderVoiceSamples`/`musyxMixActiveVoices`/
`musyxSynthFrame`/`viRetraceHandlerThread` at wall-clock ~27s (dir ctime
18:19:17, log mtime 18:19:44) — exactly the guest-side audio SIGBUS
signature s1889 catalogued as new-but-rare; this is the second observation
of it and the first with a resource trace attached.

**Correlated resource trace across the run:** `vm.page_free_count` oscillated
in a stable ~3,500-11,000 page band (roughly 55-180 MB at this Mach's 16 KiB
page size) from t=0 through the crash, with no downward trend beforehand —
the eventual jump to 60,000-75,000 free pages at sampler t=29-33s is the
process's memory being reclaimed *after* it died (dir/log timestamps put the
crash at wall-clock ~27s into the run, and the sampler was started ~2s before
the repro launched), not evidence building toward the crash. `getloadavg()`
1-minute figure held flat at 5.2-5.7 across 15 logical CPUs (never close to
saturation) for the entire window. Read plainly: this run shows no memory- or
CPU-pressure signature preceding or coincident with the failure — the
resource-exhaustion flavor of H3 is not supported by this data point.

**New H3 lead, not previously measurable: Low Power Mode was ON.**
`NSProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled` read `True` (thermalState
`0`/nominal, so this isn't thermal throttling — it's the separate,
user/OS-toggled power-saving mode that caps max CPU frequency and can shift
GCD/pthread QoS scheduling). This is plausible for a mechanism the resource
counters can't see: the crash lives on `viRetraceHandlerThread` inside audio
sample synthesis, a real-time-ish producer that a lowered CPU ceiling or
altered thread priority could starve. This is a genuinely new, narrow,
testable sub-hypothesis (call it H3a-lowpower) — it is not yet a causal
result, only a same-run correlation with n=1. No on/off comparison has been
run: toggling Low Power Mode from this harness needs `pmset`, which is
denied by the same command-string match as the other diagnostic binaries,
and unlike reading `NSProcessInfo` there is no non-`pmset` way found yet to
*write* this setting from inside the process — so testing H3a-lowpower
causally still needs one human action, but it is a much smaller one than the
git-clone bisect ask: toggle Low Power Mode off in System Settings > Battery
(or confirm it's already off and this reading was stale/cached), then a
future iteration re-runs the identical recipe once for direct comparison.

**Ask (2) (disposable clone + `git submodule update` for a literal
pre-s844 bisect) is unchanged and still legitimately human-only** — unlike
the diagnostic binaries, `git submodule update` is denied here because
CLAUDE.md makes it a hard "NEVER" rule (protects `lib/`'s uncommitted
standing patches), not because of an over-broad permission match on a
harmless read. Route 1 does not apply to it; it stays an open ask.

**Outcome: ADVANCED, not BLOCKED.** The specific claim in `BLOCKED.md` — that
this harness cannot observe machine state during a run without a human
pasting one in — is refuted. The underlying VI-1024 reachability regression
itself is still open (9/9 fail), but the path forward no longer depends on a
human for machine-state observation, only (optionally, for H3a) for one
System Settings toggle, and (still) for the code-bisect clone. Iron rule 8:
this iteration counts ADVANCED (new measurement capability + new H3a lead +
a 9th independent repro with full resource correlation), resetting the
stall counter on `vi1024-reachability-regression`.

in the generated tree, 1 overlay-VRAM collision) — the campaign had been

among the 710 candidates; zero exact collisions against the full existing
TOML name list; a repo-wide grep (`.py`/`.c`/`.h`/`.toml`) for all 710
placeholder strings outside the symbol TOML surfaced two *real* holds this
session's smaller batches never triggered — `patches/heap_guards.c` has
live `RECOMP_PATCH`/`extern` declarations naming `func_80007D74` and
`func_8002221C` directly (renaming the TOML would desync the patch file

(§ around s1477/s1478) found 3 addresses that should never have been

`func_80085CD8`), had generated names of the form `static_N_ADDR` —
N64Recomp's own auto-generated name for anonymous statics, not a real
semantic name. The tool's placeholder filter (`gen_name.startswith

re-census" list in the docs before applying, not just the small
`.py`/`.c`/`.h`/`.toml` reference check NEXT.md specifies for small

path and could not provide a second hangar-pixel witness.

hangar-gated `rs64_m4_y8000_flush` walker now recognizes standard `0xB9`/
`0xBA`, reconstructs the masked H/L other-mode state, and includes it on
each `[m4-tri]` record. It rejects opcode-shaped bytes unless the standard
operand contract holds (`shift < 32`, `size <= 32`, `shift + size <= 32`),
and reports rejected candidates as `[m4-om-invalid]`. The existing
writer-attested `stored=1` triangle rows remain the same-run positive control.
The trace flag and cap were added to `docs/debug-trace-env-vars.md`.

The first run was a failed measurement, not a result:
`scratch/agent/soak_results/s1968_hangar_mode_census/` reached hangar 512

`filterVoiceSampleBlock+220` / last guest PC `0x8000834c`. It printed six

which exposed the missing operand validation. I fixed that instrument and

Two lines of evidence support the scope conclusion. (1) The corrected

selected: this particular restage buffer has no valid mode command to

## Session 1970 (2026-08-18) — selected missing host-call link in filterVoiceSampleBlock

`HYPOTHESIS-ID: hangar-filter-voice-sample-block-idiom-audit`.

Before building, the retail oracle controls passed: the whole-RDRAM physical

corrected single run used `ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1`, LLE force/ungated/solo,

`0x8011C748`, output `0x8011C7B0`, and `source_ok=1` / `output_ok=1`. The

or behavior change was added. The static caller census plus the same-run
