## Session 1971 (2026-08-18) — bltzal $zero link-register class fix: hangar extended from 4s to 60s+

**Hypothesis:** N64Recomp's direct-call lowering for `bgezal`/`bltzal` instructions
never writes the link register (`ctx->r31 = PC+8`), causing all Factor5/MusyX PIC
idiom sites to compute data pointers from stale/zero `ctx->r31`.

**Class census (static):**
- `rg` across all 54 `funcs_*.c` files found `bgezal`/`bltzal` only in `funcs_27.c`
  and `funcs_49.c`.
- `funcs_49.c:1726`: `bltzal $fp, L_801096D8` — real conditional (non-$zero),
  post-branch code uses no `$ra` consumer. Safe.
- `funcs_27.c:13413–13671,98399,106602`: `bgezal/bltzal` in code surrounded by
  `do_break()` / INVALID-instruction traps — dead-code zone. Safe.
- Six `bltzal $zero` sites with immediate `addiu $rN, $ra, offset` consumers
  (the Factor5 PIC "get-PC" idiom: $zero is always 0, so 0 < 0 is always false,
  branch never taken, but link $ra = PC+8 is written unconditionally on hardware):

| # | PC | Link (PC+8) | Consumer | Function |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0x8009D7E0 | 0x8009D7E8 | `addiu $t7, $ra, 0xD4` | filterVoiceSampleBlock |
| 2 | 0x8009D8EC | 0x8009D8F4 | `addiu $t0, $ra, 0x84` | applyVoiceDelayFilter |
| 3 | 0x8009DBA4 | 0x8009DBAC | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x190` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |
| 4 | 0x8009DBC8 | 0x8009DBD0 | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x184` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |
| 5 | 0x8009DBEC | 0x8009DBF4 | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x170` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |
| 6 | 0x8009DC10 | 0x8009DC18 | `addiu $t3, $ra, 0x164` | renderVoiceAudioBlock |

- `bgezal $zero` sites in `renderVoiceAudioBlock` call `audioMixStereoBlock8` and
  `runVoiceLatticeFilter` — both callees confirmed to use ctx->r31 zero times
  (grep verified). Safe.

**Discriminating evidence:**
- Static: N64Recomp generates `if (SIGNED(0) < 0) { call; goto after_N; }` — the
  body is dead code and ctx->r31 is never written.
- Runtime (s1970): ctx->r31=0 at filterVoiceSampleBlock site; static intended link
  was 0x8009D748. Two independent sources confirm H-link-lost.

**Fix:** `fixup_game_funcs.py` s1971 patch: for each of the 6 sites, insert
`ctx->r31 = 0x[link]u;` immediately before the post-bltzal PC-consumer comment.
Anchor is the unique PC-address comment for each instruction. Each anchor verified
to appear exactly once in funcs_27.c. The game code saves/restores the caller's
$ra around the PIC idiom so overwriting ctx->r31 is safe.

**Build and run results:**
- Regen order: `make_elf.py` → N64Recomp → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → cmake. All
  succeeded; all 6 patches confirmed present in funcs_27.c.
- Hangar probe (ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1, eleven-Start, PROBE_PHASE_WIDTH=512,
  PROBE_PHASE_TIMEOUT=60): phase 512 at 26.5s, 17 frames captured in 60s, NO SIGBUS.
  `drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` site spinning at n=218M+ by end.
  `[vi] update_screen #5312` — VI advancing continuously.
- **Before fix: 1 frame / ~4s then SIGBUS. After fix: 17 frames / 60s, no crash.**

**Outcomes:**
- H-link-lost SELECTED class-wide. H-link-preserved, H-legitimate-data,
  H-other-corruption all refuted statically.
- filterVoiceSampleBlock SIGBUS family is CLOSED.
- New observation: `drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` spinning at 218M+
  iterations in 60s. Similar to the `menuControllerInput` spin that was fixed
  with ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD. Audio path may be stuck in same class of host-yield
  starvation. Needs investigation.
- Soak enqueued: `soak_queue/s1971_hangar_180s.sh` — 180s hangar stability check.
- Next work unit: investigate drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer spin (determine if
  it's a new spin-yield site or a different bottleneck) with a new idle-yield
  probe. HYPOTHESIS-ID: audio-drain-spin-class.

## Session 1972 (2026-08-18) — audioDrain spin-yield gate closes the third host-starvation site; hangar stable 180s / 48 frames

**Context:** s1971 observed `drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` spinning at 218M+
iterations across the 60s window (same class as the two fixed menuInit/menuInput
spins). A 180s stability soak (`soak_queue/s1971_hangar_180s.sh`) failed at rc=127
because the script used `dirname "$0"/../../../../` — one level above the repo root —
and `zsh tools/probe.sh` wasn't found. Soak discarded; probe run inline this session.

**Competing hypotheses:**
- H-spin-benign: spin resolves once audio data arrives; VI continues because the spin
  and VI run in independent threads.
- H-spin-starves-audio: spin starves the audio-mix thread, causing silence or
  eventual crash.
- H-new-yield-needed: same as menuControllerInput — yield lets the idle/audio thread
  run, keys on a voice, anyAudioSlotActive returns nonzero, drain completes.

**Discriminating measurement:** Add ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD gate at `L_800B24D4`
(funcs_30.c, the `anyAudioSlotActive` back-branch in `drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer`);
run yield=1 for 180s; check whether audioDrain spin-yield fires (positive control)
and whether spin count is materially lower than s1971's 218M+.

**Static analysis:** `funcs_30.c:11114` — `L_800B24D4` is the loop label for a
`beq $v0==0` spin on `anyAudioSlotActive` (`0x8008E57C`). Identical in structure
to `L_800B8050` (menuControllerInput) and `L_800C5930` (menuOverlayInit). The
`tickMusyXIfActive` call before the loop gives the audio engine one tick; then the
loop waits for a slot to activate. With the audio-activation thread starved by the
spin, no slot activates and the loop runs forever.

**Fix:** Added s1972 fixup block to `fixup_game_funcs.py` (N64Recomp repo) inserting
a yield-self-1ms gate at `L_800B24D4` in funcs_30.c, mirroring the s1949 menuInput
pattern. Applied directly to funcs_30.c (RecompiledFuncs already patched from prior
runs; full regen not performed). Rebuilt with cmake (funcs_30.c.o recompiled, binary
relinked, zero new warnings).

**Build:** touch funcs_30.c → cmake rebuild → funcs_30.c compiled; linked as
RogueSquadron64Recomp. Pre-existing format warning at funcs_30.c:3688, not new.

**Run results (yield=1 arm, 180s, ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1):**
- Phase 512 (hangar origin `0x006AB400`) reached at 25.1s.
- 48 frames captured; 206 `update_screen` calls; **zero crashes** (no SIGBUS,
  no SIGSEGV, no slotDispatcherIter+872).
- `[spin-yield] site=audioDrain n=1 spin=100000` → n=2 spin=200000 → n=3 spin=300000
  (positive control confirmed live; spin resolved after ~300k iters, function returned).
- menuInit n=1,2 and menuInput n=1..4 also confirmed (existing gates still live).

**Comparison vs s1971 (single-source cross-session):** s1971 with no audioDrain
yield gate saw 218M+ iterations in 60s with no resolution. s1972 with yield gate
saw ~300k iters and resolution. Ratio ≈ 726× fewer iterations; function returned
and the 180s window extended cleanly (vs s1971's 60s probe window, no crash in
either — but s1971's function never completed).

**Outcomes:**
- H-new-yield-needed SELECTED for audioDrain site. H-spin-benign is inconsistent
  with the s1971 218M+ observation (benign would imply eventual resolution without
  yield, but 218M in 60s with no sign of stopping is inconsistent).
- H-spin-starves-audio: the spin did not cause visible crashes in s1971 (VI was
  advancing) so starvation was not causing immediate crashes — but the function
  never completing IS an unresolved drain. With yield, drain completes cleanly.

## Session 1975 (2026-08-18) — drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer #17 spin root cause: tickMusyXIfActive submits no RSP task at craft-select exit

**Hypothesis context.** Three competing hypotheses from s1974/NEXT.md:
- H-vi-queue-full: host VI message queue fills; retrace messages dropped; audio tick
  starves.
- H-game-recv-blocks: hangar state machine calls osRecvMesg on a non-VI queue that
  never receives.
- H-yield-missing: an unidentified CPU spin in the hangar state machine holds the
  thread and prevents VI drain.

**Probe.** `scratch/agent/s1975_freeze_probe/` (120s, `ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1 ROGUESQ_LOG_AUDIOTICK_TRACE=1`); phase-gated to VI width 512 hangar entry. 77169 log lines.

**Key trace (lines 69759–69903).**

| Line | Event | Meaning |
|------|-------|---------|
| 69759 | slot-ret-caller site=drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer n=16 | drain #16 returned |
| 69762 | spin-yield site=audioDrain n=1 spin=100000 | drain #17 started; 100k iters, no slot |
| 69784 | [lle task] ... | audio tick (recv2 n=1965) submits RSP audio task |
| 69802 | spin-yield n=2 spin=200000 | drain #17 still spinning; no slot at 200k iters |
| 69822 | spin-yield n=3 spin=300000 | drain #17 still spinning; no slot at 300k iters |
| 69873 | vi-recv-path n=1970 pre_vc=0 deq_any=0 post_vc=0 blocked=1 | audio tick stuck in do_recv(0x80114388) |
| 69874–69902 | vi-enq n=2016..2044 | 29 VI retraces pile in external_messages; nobody drains |
| 69903 | [vi] update_screen #2176 fs=1256 stalled=1 | game frame counter frozen |
| — | rest of 120s probe | only vi-enq events; no game-thread events ever again |

**Critical observation: NO `[lle task]` from the main game thread between lines 69759 and 69903.** The only [lle task] in that window is from the audio tick thread's recv2 (n=1965), submitted long before drain #17. This means `tickMusyXIfActive` (called once at the start of drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer, before the spin) did not submit an RSP audio task on drain #17. With no RSP task running, no audio voice key-on occurs, and `anyAudioSlotActive` returns 0 on every spin iteration.

**Slot-ret-caller semantics (clarified).** The slot-ret-caller PATCH fires on every call to `anyAudioSlotActive` inside the spin, not just at function exit. It is rate-limited to the first 16 total calls (then every 1e6). Drains #1-16 each activated a slot in 1–2 spin iterations (total ≤ 16 anyAudioSlotActive calls = n=1..16 all logged, all returning non-zero quickly). Drain #17 started at n=17 (not logged due to rate limit); the spin ran 300k+ iters with `anyAudioSlotActive` always returning 0. `after1024=0` just means vi_width=512 (hangar, not 1024); it says nothing about slot state.

**Root cause — confirmed mechanism.**
`drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer` calls `tickMusyXIfActive` once before the spin label `L_800B24D4`, then loops: `anyAudioSlotActive(); if (r2==0) goto L_800B24D4`. On drain #17 (the final drain after `tickCraftSelectScreen` returned the "screen complete" sentinel 0xFFFFFFFE), `tickMusyXIfActive` found MusyX in a shutdown/idle state and submitted no RSP audio task. Every subsequent anyAudioSlotActive call returns 0. The spin is infinite.

**Audio tick deadlock.** Once the drain spin exceeds 300k iters, three yield gates (n=1,2,3) fired via ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD. Each delivered a VI retrace to 0x80114388 and ran audio tick synths n=2199–2204. None activated a slot (MusyX has nothing to play). After synth n=2204 (n=1969's processing), audio tick entered vi-cb-recv1 n=1970 with no message in 0x80114388 (deq_any=0, pre_vc=0) → blocked in do_recv → run_next_thread_and_wait. After that point, vi-wait stops at n=8113 permanently. The scheduling analysis suggests a cooperative-scheduler breakdown (likely idle thread stuck in wait_for_resumed after audio tick n=1970's run_next_thread_and_wait found its expected partner thread unexpectedly absent from running_queue), but this specific breakdown mechanism is not fully traced in this session.

**Hypothesis verdicts.**
- H-vi-queue-full: **REFUTED.** vi-enq continued to n=8825 (VI ISR healthy). The freeze is not producer-side.
- H-game-recv-blocks: **CONFIRMED (audio tick variant).** Audio tick is stuck in do_recv(0x80114388) — VI retrace messages accumulate in external_messages but nobody drains them.
- H-yield-missing: **REFUTED as stated.** No new unidentified spin. The freeze is in the KNOWN audioDrain spin. The root cause is `tickMusyXIfActive` not submitting an RSP task, not a missing yield.

**Caller structure (confirmed from code).** `funcs_34.c:8430–8510` at `0x800C5E88`:
```
initCraftSelectScreen();
r17 = 0xFFFFFFFF;
do { r16 = tickCraftSelectScreen(); } while (r16 == r17);
drainAudioAndFinalizeSpeechBuffer();   // drain #17 is the LAST drain (r16 == 0xFFFFFFFE)
return (r16 != 0xFFFFFFFE) ? 1 : 0;
```
Each outer-caller loop iteration: one tickCraftSelectScreen loop (cooperative, waits for
waitForPrevFrameDone → waitForPostSwapAck → osRecvMesg(0x80128CF0)) + one drain. Drains
#1-16 each completed because MusyX was active and a slot activated quickly. Drain #17
is the "screen done" drain; by then MusyX is in shutdown/idle → no RSP submission → infinite.

**Fix for s1976.** Add `tickMusyXIfActive` call **inside** the spin loop at `L_800B24D4`
in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (after the yield gate, before `anyAudioSlotActive`). This matches
the `menuControllerInput` spin pattern which already calls both in each iteration. Also add a
safety timeout: if `anyAudioSlotActive` has not returned true after 10M iters, break
(log warning). Rebuild + run 120s probe: verify `[slot-ret-caller] site=drain n=17` appears,
verify `fs` advances past #2176.

**OUTCOME: ADVANCED** — root cause of the #2176 freeze identified with mechanistic evidence.

**Ground truth first.** Ran the retail ROM through

control and a physical watch on `0x154620:0x154621`. The positive control
reached 10,015 callbacks; the watched byte had 15 writes. Retail attributed
the relevant writes to `0x8009B7EC` (three writes at 49.0–49.1s, with the
other hits from initialization and stop paths). This independently confirms
that the worker-side zero store is real and game-owned; it is not a port-only
address or an assumed writer.

**Instrument.** Added incremental `apply_s1997_svc_pool` to
`/Users/williambuckley/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` and the
generated `funcs_26.c`. It shares an arm flag set at shutdown call 3, logs
`serviceVoicePoolFrame` entry/gate state, and logs all three status-store
sites (`0x8009B7A8`, `0x8009B7CC`, `0x8009B7EC`). The first run's global
first-8/every-1000 budget left a sub-1000 post-arm ambiguity and produced no
store-site positive hit, so it was not used for a strong null conclusion.
The fixed version widened only the same census to log every armed worker
entry/store; no game store or control flow was changed.

**Probe.** `scratch/agent/s1997_svc_pool_fixed/run.log` — the exact
eleven-Start LLE-solo hangar recipe with
`ROGUESQ_DRAIN_INLOOP_TICK=0`, `ROGUESQ_SPIN_YIELD=1`, and a 60-second
phase-gated run. Build passed. Hangar `[phase] 512 origin=0x006AB400`
arrived at 24.6s and the run captured 17 frames with no crash marker.

Positive controls (same run): `[svc-pool]` entries 1–8 and `n=1000` all
fired before arming with `gate=1`; `[shut-enter]` calls 1 and 2 had
`b0=0x00 gate=1` and their `shut-spin` wrappers exited; call 3 had

**Census.** After `[shut-enter] n=3`, there were zero
`[svc-pool] ... armed=1` entries and zero `[svc-store]` rows. The
`[shut-spin]` then held `v0=0x03`, `a0=0`, `a1=1`, and `b0=0x03` through

worker's pre-arm entries and the retail oracle.

## Session 1999 (2026-08-20) — reconciled retail audio gates with generated output

The M5 ground-truth and generated-gate reconciliation work unit ran exactly one
retail-oracle capture before any build or runtime change. The oracle command
watched whole RDRAM plus physical `0xA0F50`, `0x14998A`, and `0x14974C` ranges
for 30 seconds. It completed normally at 1,799 VI with 17,184 whole-RDRAM
write hits, so the positive control passed.

The `0xA0F50` watch had two exact hits: retail PC `0x8008EA34` wrote zero and
`0x8008EB40` wrote one, both in `setDisplayMode`. The generated `funcs_23.c`
has the same stores and values. This independently confirms that the retail
0-to-1 transition is legitimate guest gate state, not a port-only shortcut.
The retail trace had no `0x8008EC88` hit in the reached attract phase, so it
does not validate that later `reapplyDisplayMode` tail.

The narrow `0x14998A:0x14998C` watch reported zero, but that null is not
usable: the oracle's debugger callback reports aligned addresses. The positive
whole-RDRAM trace nevertheless attributed 1,795 writes to retail PC
`0x800916A4`, which the generated source identifies as the halfword write to
the `0x8014998A` countdown. The current source also contains the seed at
`0x80091ECC`; no conclusion was drawn about its absence in this phase.

The narrow `0x14974C:0x149750` watch reported 3,590 aligned-word hits, not an
exact byte-owner count. Their retail PCs were `0x8008F20C` (1), `0x8008F490`
(1), `0x800916DC` (1,793), `0x800917A8` (1,794), and `0x80091928` (1).
Generated-source mapping shows `0x8008F490` is the observed exact target
(`0x8014974C`) init clear; `0x800916DC`, `0x800917A8`, and `0x80091928` write
the neighboring `+1` byte, while `0x8008F20C` writes the `+2/+3` halfword.
The other generated exact target writers (`0x80091680`, `0x800912F8`) did not
appear in this reached phase. The flag-owner question therefore remains open,
but the composite watch is not evidence of a new port writer.

Static reconciliation confirmed the existing `fixup_game_funcs.py` regex for
`0x8008EC88` requires the instruction comment to be immediately followed by
`MEM_B`; current generated output inserts `rs64_probe_submit_gate_store` between
those lines, so the force-zero rule does not match and the generated tail writes
one. This selects H-generated-mismatch for the next regeneration repair. It is
not a runtime gate conclusion and no mitigation or de-stubbing change landed.

`src/main/main.cpp:get_rsp_microcode` remains statically env-gated: every
`M_AUDTASK` increments `[audtask-dispatch]`, returns `musyx_stub` by default,
and returns `factor5_ucode_b` only when `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE` is set. Gate
activity therefore does not prove host audio-task dispatch; that arm remains a
separate work unit. The worker/status-3 and MORT questions were not tested.

This run selects legitimate retail gate semantics for the reached
`setDisplayMode` transition, the fixup/generated mismatch for `0x8008EC88`,
and leaves the `0x8014974C` wait-owner question unevaluable beyond its observed

## Session 2064 (2026-08-20) — attributed image canary and Broke to generated guest flow

This was the queued M5 static origin audit from `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`; it
used the existing generated image source and did not build, regenerate, run the
game, or enqueue a soak. I checked the generated scalar/vector store sites,
the `SQV`/`SSV`/`SDV` address implementations, the image DMA helpers, the
`factor5_ucode_b` registration, and the fixup self-gating.

The exhaustive candidate table for stores that can overlap the host canary
`DMEM 0xF80..0xF8F` is:

| Generated site | Effective destination | Why it reaches the canary |
|---|---|---|
| `L_146C`, `SQV` through `r28` | `0xE50..0xFCF` in 24 16-byte steps | `L_169C` seeds `r28=0xE50`; the loop advances it by `0x10` and runs from `r26=0x3F0` to `r29=0x570`; the `r28=0xF80` iteration writes `0xF80..0xF8F`. |
| `L_1D24`, two `SQV` stores through `r9` | `0xE50..0xFCF` in twelve 32-byte rows | `r9` starts at `0xE50`, the two stores cover each row, and the row beginning at `0xF70` covers the canary. |
| `L_1F40`, `SQV` through `r6` | `0xE50..0xFCF` in 24 16-byte steps | `L_1EF0` receives `r6=0xE50`; the loop advances by `0x10` for `0x18` iterations; the `r6=0xF80` iteration writes the canary. |

The other generated stores do not overlap the interval: scalar stores are
`0xE48..0xE4F`; the fixed vector ranges include `0x320..0x33F`,
`0x3F0..0x6EF`, `0x6F0..0x8DF`, `0xCC0..0xE3F`, and `0x740..0x8BF`;
`L_1A40`'s data-dependent base is `0xAF0 - (field << 6)` (congruent to
`0x30 mod 0x40`) and therefore cannot start at the `0xF80` aligned block.
The `L_1938`/`L_1EF0` short stores are `0xCB0..0xCBF` and `0x738..0x73F`.
The image's `DO_DMA_READ` destinations are the lower fixed/data ranges
`0x220`, `0x340`, `0x350`/`0x3A0`, `0x6F0`, `0x8C0`, and `0xCB0`; none reaches
the canary. Its `DO_DMA_WRITE` path reads from DMEM `0xCB0`, so it is not a
DMEM canary writer.

The only `return RspExitReason::Broke` in `factor5_ucode_b_recompiled.c` is
the generated `break 0` at `L_1328`, reached after `L_1314`'s final DMA-write
return edge. The other image returns are the unreachable fallthrough
`ImemOverrun` and the indirect-dispatch `UnhandledJumpTarget`. The synthetic
`L_1090` iteration cap and `L_10E8` source-end anchor in
`tools/fixup_factor5_ucode.py` are gated by the exact `factor5_ucode(`
function-name test; they do not apply to `factor5_ucode_b(`. `run_task` only
seeds the canary before the selected ucode and reads it afterward.

This selects the generated-writer portion of **H-CanaryLegitimateTaskOutput**
at source scope and refutes a synthetic-cap or image-DMA-staging origin. It does not yet establish, from an
independent retail witness, whether the host's description of `0xF80..0xF8F`
as reserved is compatible with this image's task ABI; that is the next M5
boundary. No mitigation or behavior change was made.

ORIGIN: the named writers are the generated `factor5_ucode_b` loops at
`L_146C`, `L_1D24`, and `L_1F40`; their values are legitimate generated guest
DMEM stores at source scope, while host/retail ABI legitimacy remains open.

## Session 2065 (2026-08-20) — audited image DMA/task ABI crosswalk

This was the prescribed bounded M5 static ABI audit. I did not regenerate,
build, run the game, or enqueue a soak. I read every generated
`DO_DMA_READ`/`DO_DMA_WRITE` path in `build/factor5_ucode/factor5_ucode_b_recompiled.c`,
the inclusive-length and 8-byte RDRAM-alignment helpers, and the staged OSTask
field layout. `git diff --check` passed.

The helper macros add one to the encoded length, mask the RDRAM address with
`0xFFFFF8`, mask the DMEM address with `0xFFF`, and clamp at the memory ends.
The table uses `A8(x)=x&0xFFFFF8` and half-open byte spans `[start,end)`.
`B=DMEM[0x348]`, `P=DMEM[0xE4C]`, `Q=DMEM[0x34C]`, `S=DMEM[0x6F0]`,
`T=DMEM[0x6F4]`, and `N=HU(DMEM[0x342])` unless a row defines another
register-derived value. The two generated `DO_DMA_READ` lines in `L_1418`
are one reachable DMA: the second is after `goto do_indirect_jump` and is
unreachable duplicate output.

| Site / caller | Direction | Effective DMEM span | Effective RDRAM span | Controlling formula | OSTask field match |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `L_10A8 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x340,0x350)` | `[A8(data_ptr),A8(data_ptr)+0x10)` | `r5=data_ptr`, `r6=0x340`, `r7=0xF` | `data_ptr` source |
| `L_10C4 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0xCB0,0xE48)` | `[A8(B+0x100),A8(B+0x100)+0x198)` | `B=word(data_ptr+8)`; `r5=B+0x100`, `r6=0xCB0`, `r7=0x197` | indirect data payload; no direct field |
| `L_10E8 -> L_1418` | read | `[0x350,0x3A0)` | `[A8(data_ptr+0x10),A8(data_ptr+0x10)+0x50)` | `r4=data_ptr+0x10`, `r5=r4`, `r6=0x350`, `r7=0x4F` | derived from `data_ptr`; no direct field |
| `L_12F0 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x340,0x350)` | `[A8(P+0xA10),A8(P+0xA10)+0x10)` | `r5=P+0xA10`, `r6=0x340`, `r7=0xF` | indirect data state; no direct field |
| `L_1340` first -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0xAF0,0xAF0+h0)` | `[A8(w0),A8(w0)+h0)` | `w0=word(r2+0x30)`, `h0=HU(r2+0x38)` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1360` second -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0xAF0+h0,0xAF0+h0+h1)` | `[A8(w1),A8(w1)+h1)` | `w1=word(r2+0x34)`, `h1=HU(r2+0x3A)`, conditional `h1!=0` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1384 -> L_1418` | read | `[0x220,0x320)` | `[A8(word(base+0x40)),A8(word(base+0x40))+0x100)` | `base=r5`, `r6=0x220`, `r7=0xFF` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1394/L_13A8 -> L_1418` | read | `[base_dmem,base_dmem+0x50)` | `[A8(r4),A8(r4)+0x50)` | `base_dmem=0x350` or `0x3A0`; `r5=r4`, `r7=0x4F` | register-derived; no direct field |
| `L_1924 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x6F0,0x700)` | `[A8(B),A8(B)+0x100)` | `r5=B`, `r6=0x6F0`, `r7=0xFF` | indirect data payload; no direct field |
| `L_1D68 -> L_13E8` | read | `[0x6F0,0x738)` | `[A8(Q),A8(Q)+0x48)` | `Q=DMEM[0x34C]`, `r6=0x6F0`, `r7=0x47` | indirect task data; no direct field |
| `L_1E00` positive -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0x8C0+2e,0x8C0+2e+2d)` | `[A8(S),A8(S)+2d)` | `d=r15+0xC0-T>0`, `e=T-r15` | DMEM audio state; no direct field |
| `L_1E04` nonpositive -> `L_13E8` | read | `[0x8C0,0xA40)` | `[A8(S+2r15),A8(S+2r15)+0x180)` | branch condition `r15+0xC0-T<=0` | DMEM audio state; no direct field |
| `L_1200 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xC30,0xCB0)` | `[A8(B+8k),A8(B+8k)+0x80)` | `k=(old DMEM[0xE48]&0xF0)-0x10`, low nibble zero path | indirect data/ring state; no direct field |
| `L_1294/L_12AC -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xC30,0xC30+8n)` | `[A8(B+8m),A8(B+8m)+8n)` | `m/n` are the high/low nibble-derived ring index/length | indirect data/ring state; no direct field |
| `L_12E0 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0x6F0,0x9F0)` | `[A8(word(r2+0x44)),A8(word(r2+0x44)+0x300)` | `r5=0x6F0`, `r6=word(r2+0x44)`, `r7=0x2FF` | indirect table; no direct field |
| `L_1314 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xCB0,0xE48)` | `[A8(B+0x100),A8(B+0x100)+0x198)` | `B=word(data_ptr+8)`, `r5=0xCB0`, `r6=B+0x100`, `r7=0x197` | indirect data payload; no direct field |
| `L_1E48 -> L_13B0` | write | `[0xE50,0xFD0)` | `[A8(S+0x180N),A8(S+0x180N)+0x180)` | `r13=0xC0*N`, `r14=S`, so `r6=S+2r13` and `r7=0x17F` | indirect DMEM audio state; no direct field |

The OSTask is staged at DMEM `0xFC0..0xFFF`: `output_buff` is at `0xFE8`,
`data_ptr` at `0xFF0`, and `yield_data_ptr` at `0xFF8`. The image has only the
two direct task-field loads at `0x30($r1)` and `0x34($r1)`, i.e. `data_ptr` and
`data_size`. No generated instruction reads `0x28($r1)` or `0x38($r1)`.

The canary-covering stream is therefore not a partial write: `L_1E48` writes
the complete `[0xE50,0xFD0)` source span, including `0xF80..0xF8F`, to an
indirect destination. The separate `L_1314` write is `[0xCB0,0xE48)` and is
the write immediately before the natural `L_1328` `Broke` edge. Neither path
is statically matched to `output_buff` or `yield_data_ptr`; the s2063 zero
payload result cannot identify the intended task field from payload alone.

This selects **H-OutputRouteUnevaluable** under the declared discriminator.
H-ImageWorkScratch, H-ImageOutputStaging, and H-ImageTaskAbiMismatch remain
unselected because the source proves the generated writer and its spans but
not the live relationship between the DMEM-derived destinations and the
OSTask/task-data values. No mitigation or behavior change is authorized.

ORIGIN: the canary writer is the generated guest `L_1E48` DMA source fed by
`L_146C`/`L_1D24`/`L_1F40`; it is legitimate generated guest work at source
scope. Whether that work is scratch, output staging, or an ABI mismatch is
not established without an independent live task/value crosswalk.

`0x800902CC` = 68,443, `0x8009024C` = 162, and `0x8002BEEC` = 19. The exact
`0x800903F0` caller watch recorded zero hits despite the valid controls.

### Static crosswalk and result

The generated definition and companion symbols place
`fillSampleStreamRange` at `0x8008FAAC` with size `0x500`, and
`musyxRenderVoiceSamples` at `0x8008FFAC`. At the active `0x800903F0` edge,
the caller sets `a0 = s0 + 0x28`, loads the sample-position value from its
stack frame into `a1`, aligns and doubles it, then adds `MEM_W(s1, 0x34)` in
the delay slot. It forms `a2` from the frame/output structure's `+0x48` value
plus the stack-frame extent, aligns and doubles that value, and loads `a3 =
MEM_W(s1, 0x34)`. The companion mapping describes this function as the
per-voice resample/mix kernel feeding an output buffer.

The callee copies `a1` to `t4` and `a2` to `t2`. It uses `t4` and `t4+t2` in
allocator-block boundary comparisons and writes the resulting ranges into
stream-block nodes; it uses `a3` as the block discriminator. There is no
direct load through `a1` in the function body, and the copied `a0` is not used
by the visible range logic. This is an address/range-endpoint contract, not a
scalar/tag or alternate-register contract.

The discriminator selects **H-CalleePointerContract** at ABI scope. It rules
out H-LegitimateNonDramArgs and H-AlternateRegisterContract, while the retail
null at `0x800903F0` rules out treating that exact port-active edge as a
retail callsite. Retail callee activity through the other callsites leaves
the voice-slot `+0x34` writer/copy as the next open boundary. The prior port
values outside RDRAM remain unexplained; no mitigation was added.

Ran the M5 source-semantics work unit from `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` without a
build or runtime change. The generated definition at `0x80090C80` is inside

loads at `0x80090A4C` and `0x80090A54` resolve to `0x80149760` (halfword count)

store is `head + count*0xA10 + inner*0x50 + 0x44`.

The companion symbol mapping independently identifies `0x80149750`/`0x80149760`
as the MusyX RSP command-list head/count and `0x801496F8` as the separate
voice-slot-array pointer with stride `0x88`. The generated `0x800921E8` audit

`base + (voiceIdx & 0xFFFF)*0x88`, and stores `sampleDesc+0x4` at `+0x34`.

pointer to `musyxKeyOnVoice`, while `startStreamedSampleVoice` and
`soundMacroOpPlaySampleKeymap` pass `(voiceIdx, sampleDesc, adsrFlag)` to
`musyxInitVoiceFromSample`.

rejects `H-VoiceBaseMismatch` and `H-ReallocatedVoiceBase` as explanations of
the source arithmetic. It supersedes s2089's `H-WrongField` interpretation,
which was believable only because the two exact retail writers had been
compared against the same assumed voice lattice. The retail command-list root
and formula remain to be qualified independently; no port-facing conclusion,

samples, 13210 nonzero, FNV `0xA28B37D0`; index 419 had word count 249,
6080 samples, 4783 nonzero, FNV `0xF166120B`; and index 545 had word count
843, 18880 samples, 16344 nonzero, FNV `0xFB04E2D2`. Every row also had
decoded first/last sample 0 and min/max values within the signed 16-bit
range; the complete byte-count and waveform table is in

the four decoded 8000-Hz/type-0 rows. It does not cover the 16000-Hz or
nonzero descriptor-type classes, so it does not select the extended codec
contract. The reference compiler initially rejected the Windows-only
`StdAfx.h` include and `unsigned __int64`; the harness's temporary adapter

fixed command completed. No audio arm, task ABI, output route, host shortcut,

caller/framebuffer rows used `0x62B800`, plus `0x695C00` for one caller; the
retail control rows showed `0x805D4000` and `0x8066A000`. This is a
caller-contract/argument mismatch observation, not proof of the missing
second-origin cause because the first oracle run printed only its bounded
execution samples at target-phase time. It rules out oracle coverage failure,

  `recomp_context ctx{}` and sets only `r29` (sp), `r4` (arg), `mips3_float_mode`,

  identified: the generator convention omits `ctx->r31` for direct JAL-to-named-
  function calls, but `convertMat3x4ToN64Mtx` depends on the guest `$ra` value.

Legitimate value = `0x800155EC` (standard MIPS PC+8 link register value for
that JAL). This is not a mitigation; it is the correct return address the recomp
generator convention omits.

override `$ra`, then add `ctx->r31 = 0x800155EC;` before the converter call in

phase. The `m5-scheduler-id-control` fired at both title (1024) and hangar (512)
phases, confirming the route gate was live.

The sixteen words at gspTask (0x800377C8) are STABLE and non-zero across all
observations in both title and hangar phases:
`0A8C2907,88C3045E,20848201,2907F858,17F04A94,911C317E,1FE145F4,12060623,
1FE16082,C12A50A7,84820188,07F85820,5F8A9C29,4470CB04,7F8317E0,4818188C`.
These values carry the known struct-cast endian defect (s2484) and cannot be
directly mapped to OSTask fields without a MEM_W-based per-field decoder.

0x800377C8` with `yield_match=1, payload_match=1`, confirming gspTask is both the
event payload and the task being restarted via osSpTaskLoad/osSpTaskStartGo in a
yield-and-restart cycle. In the title (1024) phase the event payload is also
0x800377C8 but the started task is 0x80149470 (distinct, consistent with s2484).

**H-DescriptorPopulated selected** (74 hangar-phase yield rows, non-zero stable
fingerprint). **H-DescriptorStaleOrEmpty refuted** (non-zero, consistent).
**H-DescriptorWriterUnjoined refuted** at dispatcher boundary (event_payload ==
gspTask == started task in the hangar). Open: endian-correct per-field decode to
verify type, data_ptr, yield_data_ptr values against retail ground truth. Artifact:
`scratch/agent/s2487_m5_descriptor_capture/audit.md`.

## Session 2490 (2026-08-26) — explained descriptor macro discrepancy

The oracle whole-RDRAM positive control ran before the port capture and
reached its 10,000-callback threshold in 8 emulated seconds. The Debug build
succeeded. Two short port captures were non-results because their input
recipes did not reach the target phase; the fixed run used the established
eleven-Start boot-relative schedule and reached 512 / `0x6AB400` at 26.1
seconds.

The fixed run recorded 36 phase-10 and 28 phase-12 comparison rows. Every
selected field had `MEM_W == TO_PTR != explicit memcpy` at the same host
offset; e.g. field 0 was `0x60A77444` versus explicit `0x00000001`, and field
2 was `0x0CB0001D` versus explicit `0x800825D0`. The existing raw-byte rows
retain the coherent OSTask shape, and descriptor/scheduler controls fired.

This selects the pointer-ABI explanation: the callback takes `task_ptr` as
`uint32_t`, while `MEM_W` and `TO_PTR` require the sign-extended guest
representation when subtracting `0xFFFFFFFF80000000`. The callback therefore
zero-extends the pointer before both reads, making them agree on invalid host
memory. This rules out a TO_PTR-only struct-layout difference at this
boundary. No task dispatch, audio behavior, descriptor remap, or guard was
changed. Artifact:
`scratch/agent/s2490_m5_descriptor_compare_hangar/audit.md`.

## Session 2559 (2026-08-26) — ran M5 stub-image contract checkpoint

HYPOTHESIS-ID: m5-audio-destubbing-contract

Before the build, I defined four competing outcomes: audio degeneracy would
produce a new downstream edge in the image arm; an image contract gap would
show image execution without that edge; route-only variation would show
matched phases without an audio delta; and image instability would prevent a
valid target window. The Debug target built successfully. The staged recipe
ran the retail oracle first, then the silent arm before the image arm, with
phase-gated title and hangar controls.

The independent retail whole-RDRAM control reached 10,000 callbacks and
recorded both title (`1024 @ 0x00790400`) and hangar (`512 @ 0x006AB400`). Both
port arms reached title and hangar and ended by SIGKILL with zero `[CRASH]` and
`[ABORT]` markers. The silent arm recorded 1,472 ABI/DMA rows, zero generated
DMA ranges, and unchanged DMEM. The image arm recorded 1,136 ABI/DMA rows,
2,328 generated DMA ranges, and repeated positive ABI rows with `changed=1597`,
`break_pc=0x1328`, `exit=1`, and `dma_count=3`. Both arms reported PCM source
and consumer boundary rows (94/94 silent; 88/88 image), so the image arm did
not produce a distinct downstream PCM edge in this capture.

This selects `H-contract-gap` at the current observable boundary: image
execution and generated DMA are proven, but the checkpoint does not close a
new task/output/service/slot/voice/PCM edge. `H-image-instability` is ruled out
for this target window; `H-audio-degeneracy` is not selected because the
downstream discriminator was not image-specific. `H-route-only` remains a
possible confound for shared PCM controls, so this is not evidence for
promotion. No task field, output pointer, gate, guard, or mitigation changed.
Artifact: `scratch/agent/s2559_m5_step1_contract_pair/driver.log`.

join would select `H-index-alias`; live unjoined endpoints would select

corresponding dead endpoint. The first build used a broad consumer anchor at

anchor after the actual `0x13D8` B00/B02/B04 loads, rebuilt, and reran the same

control fired 514 times, but producer rows and consumer rows were both zero.

iteration; it reached the 10,000-hit cap and recorded title and hangar VI
phases. Thus the target route and control machinery were live, but both M4
endpoints were absent. This result does not distinguish producer-dead from
consumer-dead and does not select either index hypothesis. It rules out only
the claim that a qualified target-phase join was observed. The regeneration-

`512 @ 0x006AB400`. The silent and image port arms both reached those phases,
so the route controls were valid.

The silent arm selected `musyx_stub` and produced 1,297 ABI/task rows but no
image-stage or DMA-range rows. The image arm produced 1,014 ABI/DMA rows,
2,189 DMA-range rows, and 4,496 image-stage rows; representative rows reached
`break_pc=0x1328`, `exit=1` (`Broke`), and wrote the expected spans
`0x166450`/`0x1798B0`. Those image DMA payloads and both PCM endpoints were
zero-valued. The image arm had no crash, abort, or missing-function marker;
the silent arm ended `rc=139` in hangar.

This selects `H-ContractGap` over `H-AudioDegeneracy` using two independent
lines: the retail oracle established the phase/task ground truth, while the
same-build arm separation showed image-only task work without output joins.
The silent crash is a recorded failure signal and does not identify its cause.
It rules out route absence and a silent/image dispatch-equivalence explanation,
but does not authorize writeback, remapping, or gate changes. Artifact:
`scratch/agent/s2616_m5_step1_contract_pair/`. Next is a bounded census of
port-side PCM writer/copy edges.

silent M_AUDTASK baseline with the independent retail oracle. The oracle
passed the whole-RDRAM positive control at 10,000 callbacks and reached title
1024 at origin 0x00790400 plus hangar 512 at origin 0x006AB400. The first

## Session 3054 (2026-08-28) — checkpoint: identified VI-mode stall as route root cause

Stop-gate retry. No new experiment was run. Analyzed the s3053 run.log data
that the original session entry omitted.

`osViSetMode_recomp` logs unconditionally. The s3053 run.log contains exactly
4 `osViSetMode` calls: #1 width=320 (initVideoSubsystem, line 42), #2 width=2
(swapBufferWithViMode, line 1242 — suspicious/corrupt data), #3 width=640
(initVideoSubsystem, line 1249), #4 width=640 (applyPendingViChanges,
line 1342). The game never calls osViSetMode with width=1024.

The route predicate at `src/main/main.cpp:1376–1380` reads VI_WIDTH_REG via
`rs64_vi_committed_width()` and fires only when width==1024 (title) or
width==512 (hangar). PORTING-STATE history confirms this is correct: older
runs show "vi_width=1024 (was 640) origin=0x00790400 at 45.3s" and
"vi_width=512 (was 1024) origin=0x006AB400 at 74.4s" as the expected
transition signature. The route predicate is not wrong — it was calibrated
against actual retail behavior.

The M4 summary at the end of the s3053 run shows `viw=640 origin=0x005D4500`
as the steady-state VI, confirming the game renders ~10 seconds of content at
width=640 without ever issuing a width=1024 mode change. This selects
`H-TitleOsViNotCalled` as the most specific hypothesis: the game code path
that calls osViSetMode(width=1024) is never reached in current AUTOPILOT runs.

This is a pre-title state-machine stall, not a DP-event ordering or
ProducerMark issue. It explains why all target-phase measurements in sessions
3040–3053 returned `H-MeasurementInsufficient`: the route predicate is
structurally unreachable if the VI mode never transitions to 1024.

Next discriminating probe: use the retail oracle to capture the PC that calls
osViSetMode(1024) in retail, then check via port osViSetMode logs whether that
call site executes in port AUTOPILOT runs. If the retail caller PC maps to a
named recompiled function, check whether that function is called at all in
port. No behavior changed. New evidence: osViSetMode call-count data in
`scratch/agent/s3053_m5_gfx_action_order/run.log` (lines 42, 1242, 1249, 1342).

## Session 3402 (2026-08-31) — M5 retail slot 0x149764 pre-phase initialization

Work unit: retail-oracle-only capture watching physical slot `0x149764:0x149768`,
with whole-RDRAM positive control, title/hangar phase gates (`--pc-hist-phase`),
and `0x1935E0` post-value control. Oracle ran 120 seconds.

Controls all passed: whole-RDRAM positive-control threshold (10,046 callbacks),
title-1024 (633 VI frames), hangar-512 (1,316 VI frames), `0x1935E0` (40 hits).

Slot `0x149764` results:
- Total: 6 writes from `pc=0x8008F2C8`, all storing value `0x801797B0`
  (nonzero, fnv=0x380f190b). Zero writes during title-1024 phase. Zero writes
  during hangar-512 phase. All 6 writes occurred before the first phase gate.
- `0x800078EC` had 0 writes to the slot range, as expected (it writes to the
  buffer the slot points to, not the slot pointer itself).

Combined with s3401's port witness (slot stored `0x80178C80` at title-1024,
`0x801797B0` at hangar-512 from the same PC `0x8008F2C8`), two independent
lines of evidence discriminate among the three hypotheses:

- `H-PortStage3OwnerAbsent` (retail does not write to the slot in target
  phases): refutes this — retail writes to `0x149764` 6 times, all pre-phase.
- `H-PortStage3Field348ProducerGap` (retail writes a different value):
  selects this for title-1024 (port stores `0x80178C80`; retail stored
  `0x801797B0` pre-phase — a different buffer address). refutes it for
  hangar-512 (both store `0x801797B0`).
- `H-PortStage3DownstreamGap` (same value, downstream gap): selects this for
  hangar-512. Both retail and port have `field348=0x801797B0` at hangar, but
  port PCM remains zero. The gap is in the dispatch/trigger for `0x8002BEEC`
  (the JAL that calls `0x800078EC`), not in the `field348` pointer value.
  Next discriminator: oracle `--watch-pc 0x8002BEEC` to capture the exec-prev
  histogram naming the JAL site that dispatches `0x8002BEEC` in retail.

The slot-level investigation is closed for the hangar-512 scope. The `field348`
pointer is correct in the port; the open gap is why `0x8002BEEC` never executes
in the port while firing 37,635 times in retail. Next probe: use the oracle's
`--watch-pc` option to capture the `exec-prev` histogram for `0x8002BEEC`,
revealing what PC (JAL site) dispatches it in retail. The port contrast then
shows whether the caller exists in the port or is silenced.

No audio behavior changed. Evidence: `docs/M5-S3402-SLOT-PREPHASE.md` and
`scratch/agent/s3402_retail_field348_owner/oracle.log`.

## Session 3534 (2026-08-31) — resolved AI-frequency return contract

The bounded unit was a static contract audit, so no build or runtime
instrument was added. The complete retail ELF body of `osAiSetFrequency` at
`0x80029D20` computes `dacRate = round(osViClock / frequency)`, rejects a
too-small rate, clamps/programs the AI registers, and returns
`osViClock / dacRate`. The retail `osViClock` is the NTSC clock
48,681,812. For the qualified input `0x5622` (22,050 Hz), `dacRate=2208` and
the returned actual frequency is 22,047 (`0x561F`).

This exactly explains Session 3533's independent retail observation of
`0x561F` after the shared `0x5622` input. The current host implementation in
`librecomp/src/ai.cpp` returns the input because its equivalent calculation is
commented out. This selects `H-InternalReturnSemantics` and refutes
`H-LaterStoreABI` at the qualified boundary. No behavior change was applied;
the next unit is the named host contract correction and route validation.

ORIGIN: retail ELF disassembly plus independent retail/port return evidence;
the legitimate writer is `osAiSetFrequency`, whose contract returns actual
programmed frequency, not requested frequency. See
`docs/M5-S3534-AI-FREQUENCY-CONTRACT.md`.
